title: Anchors away: White Oaks Mall's last anchor store announces it is closing later this year
author: Claire Grant
description: It's the end of an era for White Oaks Mall as its last anchor store is closing in early 2025. Here's what you need to know.
content:
It's the end of an era for White Oaks Mall as its last anchor store announced it was closing in early 2025.
Sixty-six of Macy's stores will shutter their doors by the first quarter of 2025. In December, Macy's announced a plan to cut 150 underperforming stores by the first quarter of 2026.
The list included just the one Illinois store.
Macy's first announced in February of 2024 plans to close one-third of all locations nationwide in a part of the company's "A Bold New Chapter" plan. Liquidation sales will come into play for two to three months at closing stores starting in January of this year, according to the Macy's Inc.
"Bold New Chapter" is a plan designed by Macy's Inc. to focus on the 350 remaining stores open once closures take place and investing in the remaining locations, to return the company to a profitable sales growth through the 2026 fiscal year.
The Macy's location at White Oaks is the eastern anchor store of the Mall, and is the last traditional anchor store inside the shopping center.
In 2018, other anchor stores Bergner's and Sears closed.
In a company statement on the closings, Macy's chairman and CEO Tony Spring said the underproductive stores closing will allow the company to 'focus our resources and prioritize investments in our go-forward stores."
Macy's joins a number of other big retail chains closing locations nationwide.
Bed Bath & Beyond has announced the closure of several of its locations in 2025 alongside Kohl's which will be closing 27 locations by the end of April, and Big Lots, which planned to close all its stores, including two in Springfield, three months after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

title: Illinois rejects more than 300 license plates in 2024
author: Tom Ackerman
description: "WEENIE" and "HOKTUAH" were just some of the license plates rejected by the state of Illinois last year.
content:
To understand the list recent list of rejected license plates in Illinois, you may need to consult the internet to understand the reasons why.
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias' office rejected more than 300 specialty license plates in 2024 for being offensive.
Here's what you need to know.
What are some of the plates that were rejected?
HOKTUAH, GYATT, MUNCH, BICHIN, JAGWEED, BADARSE, AXEHOLE, ILLCUTU, HOHOHOE, ABADMF, WEENIE, DUCKOFF, SHIDDED, UGEWANG, and THICCAF.
Why were the plates rejected?
The Secretary of State's Office can reject plates that create 'a connotation that is offensive to good taste and decency,' the office said, citing state law.
Some plates, like MWMWMWM or OOQQOO, were rejected this year because they are difficult to read, and they could pose problems for law enforcement.
How are the plates vetted?
'The office flags combinations of letters and numbers that can be construed as lewd or offensive, including expletives, racial epithets, sex and drug references and allusions to violence,' the SOS wrote in a news release.
Any rejected combinations are placed on a permanently prohibited list, which currently contains over 8,000 plate combinations.
How many plates were approved?
Residents submitted 60,537 requests for the vanity plates in 2024, including the 335 that were denied.
How many of the custom plates are on the road?
Over 530,000 personalized plates are attached to registered vehicles, in addition to over 294,000 vanity plates.
What's the difference between vanity and personalized plates?
Vanity plates contain up to three numbers only or one to seven letters only. Personalized plates contain both letters and numbers.
How to request a custom license plate?
One option is to go to the office's website at apps.ilsos.gov/pickaplate. There, applicants can see if a desired combination is available for purchase.

title: © 2025 www.sj-r.com
author: Natalie Morris
description: Huge Savings: Subscribe today to enjoy sports, entertainment, life, money, tech, and travel news along with videos, apps, and more.
content:
Why did California Kitchen cross the road?
Because the shuttered Kentucky Fried Chicken building was the fastest way to return to serving its customers after a Sept. 16 fire closed the popular late night haunt at 1132 N. Ninth St.
But owner Amer 'Adam' Snober is quick to call the move to 1111 N. Ninth St. – in the same block as its original home – an expansion, not a relocation.
More: Springfield restaurant displaced by fire appears to have found new home
'It's a second location. Same menu. Same name,' Snober said of the Dec. 26 opening in the former KFC spot. 'I still plan to repair the original (California Kitchen). Plan to reopen, probably in a couple months. But we'll stay here too."
California Kitchen's expansive menu – complete with fried fish and chicken, kebabs, gyros and Philly cheesesteak sandwiches – has grown at the new locale to include two new Middle Eastern dishes, shawarma and falafel.
Shawarma is seasoned meat roasted on a spit that is thinly sliced and served on a pita. Falafel is a deep-fried fritter.
The new spot offers both dine-in service and a drive-through window. Hours are 10 a.m. to 4 a.m. daily. Phone: 217-970-4131.
The McDonald's at 3035 Chatham Road will only have drive-through service throughout the month of January while the building's dining room is renovated.
Owner Kim Derringer said this is a standard lobby remodel required by the fast-food brand's Chicago-based corporate office every decade.
Work will include a refresh of the lobby with updated, chairs, seating and tables. The self-serve drink station will remain for now, despite a corporate push to retire this feature by 2032. The new indoor layout will include pick up areas for digital orders and third party delivery.
Within 24 hours of posting Broadguage's opening date for the fine dining restaurant on social media in 2021 the Petersburg establishment was booked for a week.
The same thing happened last weekend when a Jan. 4 Facebook post announced that both Broadgauge and its sister business, Talisman Coffee & Baked Goods, – both located in the historic Broadgauge building in downtown Petersburg – have closed permanently.
The business's tenure will wrap following two remaining public events that involved dinner service.
'We have loved being able to serve this community over the last three years and hope to find someone (who) wants to continue building Broadgauge's next chapter,' the post read, advising customers with gift certificates to reserve a seat for dinner service planned before shows Jan. 17 and Jan. 25.
A follow up note Jan. 5 said both days were booked and pointed interested parties to a waiting list.
'Broadgauge (restaurant) was very popular, drew crowds,' owner Douglas Pope said this week when asked about the decision to sell the building – complete with kitchen equipment and furnishings. 'We looked out into what we personally have planned for 2025 and made the decision it was time for us to move on.
'Broadgauge (the building) has been around 150 years. It's only been the last three years (it has operated) as a hospitality business. But the building has been a big part of the community for a much longer time. We're excited to see what's next for it.'
Pope said he plans to list the 14,000-square-foot building later this month with Realtor Dan Sperry for $2.9 million.
Pope spent 14 months breathing life back into the historic building – home to the Broadgauge store built in 1872 as central Illinois' original 'mega store' complete with hardware, grocery and dry goods all under one roof.
Pope used the renovated building as home to the fine dining restaurant, cafe and private event space.
He also managed to attract many top names from Springfield's culinary world to join in the endeavor, including Corey and Emily Faucon (who formerly owned the celebrated Long 9 Junction in downtown Springfield), David Radwine (general manager for the storied Sangamo Club from 1992-2015) and Sean Keeley (owner/chef of the former Ross Isaac Contemporary Cuisine and general manager for the former Sangamo Club from 2021-2022).
Renovation is completed at JT Costelloe's Pizza-Pub-Grill on a new designated carry-out section.
The roughly 8-foot addition to the establishment at 7024 Kingsmill Court has carved out space for to-go customers to pick up both fully baked and frozen pies, completely separate from the dining area.
The new carry-out section also is stocked with candy and snacks for sale, along with Costelloe's signature hot wing sauce and branded merchandise.
The expansion also freed up space for additional tables in the dining area.
Eddie's Rise n' Dine is set to fill the vacancy left by the Huddle House's Dec. 31 departure from Williamsville sometime in January.
Don Schomaker – the former Huddle House franchise operator for the business – is rebranding his holdings, naming the new family-owned establishment after his father, Eddie.
District manager Amber Randall said the menu will offer traditional American diner fare for breakfast, lunch and dinner, using fresh ingredients. Operating hours will be 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily.
An opening date for the Williamsville diner has yet to be set but is expected later this month, she said.
The Williamsville site near the Love's truck stop just off Interstate 55 is Schomaker's only holding north of Interstate 70. The other three businesses are in southern Illinois.
The first Eddie's Rise n' Dine opened in Breese in 2020. Schomaker rebranded his Huddle House in Highland in February 2024 and the former Huddle House in Mascoutah – which is being remodeled – is set to open as an Eddie's Rise n' Dine this February.
The Atlanta-based Huddle House brand opened in Williamsville in 2006. Schomaker purchased the business in 2020.

title: Lawmakers advance bill requiring removal guns from domestic violence situations
author: Andrew Adams
description: A bill that would require police officers temporarily removing guns from a person who has an order of protection has advanced in Illinois.
content:
It's been 18 months since Karina Gonzalez and her 15-year-old daughter Daniela were shot and killed on Fourth of July weekend at their Chicago home, allegedly by her husband.
Gonzalez had filed for an order of protection from her husband just two weeks before her death. That order caused his Firearm Owner's Identification card to be revoked, but law enforcement never removed the gun he owned from his possession.
After more than a year of negotiations, the Illinois General Assembly passed 'Karina's Bill' on Tuesday with bipartisan support. It clarifies that local law enforcement must temporarily remove guns from a person who has an order of protection against them when the alleged victim successfully seeks firearm removal as a remedy in court.
'We are talking about people who are abusing the people that they claim to love, that are threatening them with harm, that are shooting them and killing them,' bill sponsor Sen. Celina Villanueva, D-Chicago, told the Senate Monday night.
Gonzalez's son, Manny Alvarez, who survived the 2023 shooting, joined Rep. Edgar Gonzalez Jr., D-Chicago, on the House floor for the bill's final passage. It needs only a signature from Gov. JB Pritzker to become law.
Current law allows people asking a court for an order of protection to request a 'firearm remedy' that would lead to law enforcement removing guns from the alleged abuser's possession. Karina's bill seeks to close the loophole that made it unclear who was responsible for removing the gun from the situation.
Under the bill, the person who seeks an order of protection can also ask the court to issue a search warrant that will allow local law enforcement to seize firearms from the alleged abuser. The petitioner or state's attorney must demonstrate probable cause that the alleged abuser poses an immediate threat to the petitioner. Law enforcement would then be required to execute the warrant within 96 hours of it being issued.
Road blocks, delays
The bill ran into road blocks, including that lawmakers wanted to wait for the U.S. Supreme Court to weigh in on a similar federal case.
The nation's high court upheld a federal law last June that prohibits people with domestic violence-related restraining orders from having guns. Though Karina's bill had previously passed through the House, senators delayed action while waiting for the decision. The court's ruling 'gave us far more elbow room than I would have expected to tackle this issue,' Senate President Don Harmon, D-Oak Park, said in a Senate committee Monday.
Illinois law enforcement organizations also had concerns about their ability to carry out the law, including where police agencies would store the confiscated firearms and the logistics of carrying out search warrants against alleged abusers. Stakeholders came to agreement over those logistics, including giving police 48 hours to research the situation behind the order of protection so they can properly execute the search warrant.
However, some Republicans expressed concerns that small sheriff's departments in rural districts would continue to struggle to carry out the law with limited resources.
'We don't have the people to do these things,' Sen. Chapin Rose, R-Mahomet, said.
But supporters of the bill said the state needed to strengthen its laws to support victims of domestic violence and prevent deaths like Gonzalez's.
'Our current laws are confusing for victims and judges and the result is that victims aren't getting what they need: their abuser's guns taken away,' Villanueva said in committee Monday.
Domestic violence shooting deaths were up 63% from 2019 to 2023 and were responsible for three times as many gun deaths in 2023 as non-domestic violence incidents, Amanda Pyron from The Network, an anti-domestic violence organization, told the Senate committee.
'The emergency order of protection stage is the most dangerous moment and the time a survivor is most likely to be killed because it is when an abuser realizes they're losing power over a survivor,' Pyron said.
But gun rights lobbyists expressed concerns the bill undermines due process afforded to people accused of crimes. They argued taking guns away from a person with an order of protection against them assumes guilt on criminal charges and violates their constitutional rights. Orders of protection are filed in civil court.
The bill received bipartisan support in the legislature, but some Republicans echoed the concerns of the gun rights groups.
'There is not another amendment in our Bill of Rights that you have to petition a court to get your right back before you're convicted of something,' Sen. Neil Anderson, R-Andalusia, said in the Senate Monday.
Kane County State's Attorney Jamie Mosser told the Senate committee she believes the bill will withstand any court challenges. Mosser, who officially took a neutral position on the bill, said due process is honored because the guns are temporarily confiscated, and the person can file objections if the guns were taken away permanently.
The measure, House Bill 4144, passed 43-10 in the Senate and 80-33 in the House.

title: Inauguration Day and MLK Day fall on the same day. Here's what Illinoisans should know
author: Tom Ackerman
description: President-elect Donald Trump will return to the White House this coming Monday. That day also happens to be MLK Day. Here's what you need to know.
content:
President-elect Donald Trump will return to the White House this coming Monday. That day also happens to be MLK Day.
Here's what you need to know for the day in Illinois.
When is Inauguration Day?
The inauguration is scheduled for Monday, Jan. 20. It will take place at the Capitol Building in Washington, D.C.
What happens at the Inauguration?
The president-elect and the vice-president-elect are sworn in and take office. The day marks the swearing-in ceremony, the inaugural address, and the pass in review.
Is Inauguration Day a federal holiday?
Federal employees in the Washington D.C. area are entitled to a holiday on this day, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. The holiday is given to reduce traffic and facilitate local attendance at the ceremony.
What about MLK Day? Is it a federal holiday?
Yes, MLK Day is a holiday for federal employees. The holiday is observed on the third Monday of January annually.
What is MLK Jr. Day?
MLK Day celebrates the life and legacy of Martin Luther King Jr. who advocated for Civil Rights reforms in the 1960s in the U.S.
The day became federally recognized nearly 20 years after King's assassination in 1968. By the year 2000, all 50 states recognized the holiday, USA Today reported.
MLK Day is designated as a national day of service when Americans are encouraged to volunteer to improve their communities, according to the Smithsonian National Museum of African American History & Culture.
Schools
Most schools across the state will not hold class, but it is up to the school districts to determine if classes are held.
State and city offices
State of Illinois offices and courts will be closed. City offices will also be closed.
Federal facilities
U.S. federal offices and courts are closed Monday.
Lincoln Presidential Library
The Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum will host events on the holiday including a reading of King's 'I Have a Dream' Speech at 10:30 a.m. and 12:30 p.m. in the museum's main plaza. Actor Reggie Guyton will be performing the speech.
The museum will also host a blood drive outside of the museum. The ImpactLife Blood Mobile will be parked in front of the museum entrance from 10:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.
Lastly, a string quartet will play music specifically written for the special exhibit, 'Freedom in Form: Richard Hunt.' The quartet will perform at the exhibit from 1 to 3 p.m.
'Hunt's sculptures include a monument to King, and much of his work was inspired by the civil rights movement and the struggles of African Americans,' according to a press release.
The museum and library will additionally be open during their regular hours on the holiday.

title: Springfield restaurant racks up 30 health code violations in December
author: Claire Grant
description: Health inspectors found black mold, mouse droppings, expired food and much more in kitchens in the Springfield area in December.
content:
Show Caption
An east side food joint capped out 2024 with over two dozen health code violations from the Sangamon County Health Department.
Mr. Hibachi at 1066 E. Ash St. garnered 30 health code violations on a Dec. 3 routine inspection last year. During the visit, the Sangamon County health inspector noted multiple variations from protocol including spoiled eggs in the kitchen standing cooler, raw salmon stored above sauces in the cooler and bleach stored over plates.
In repeat violation, this is the second time food handler certificates were not available at the restaurant and a third repeat violation for allergen training certifications for employees not being available.
How violations work
Food establishments are inspected by the Sangamon County Department of Public Health on an annual schedule that is determined by assigned risk type. The risk types are high, medium, or low risk, as defined by the Illinois Food Service Sanitation Code. These are determined by the complexity of food preparation taking place at the facility. Routine inspections are conducted unannounced. Follow up and complaint inspections are conducted as needed.
Critical violations concern hygiene, food temperatures, sanitizing procedures, and cross contamination. Non-critical violations concern the maintenance and cleanliness of a facility.
Here are the Sangamon County restaurants that received more than 10 violations from the health department during the month of December.
In total, 175 inspections took place around the county, with eight businesses making the list.
China King
Location: 120 W. North Grand Ave., Springfield
Date/inspection type: Dec. 9, Routine inspection
What: Inspection found 23 violations, 10 risk factors.
Notes from inspection: According to a note left by the health inspector on duty, despite continued education efforts by the health department, the facility continues to improperly handle foods and ignore safe food handling education, and a doctor was brought in to help strengthen food safety behaviors.
The location is in need of a detailed cleaning as well as repairs, as there was a missing ceiling tile above the microwave in the kitchen. The restaurant had a number of mouse droppings in the dry storage area on the floor and along shelving. In a re-inspection 10 days later, the location had been cleaned and other violations improved, but mouse droppings were still observed in the dry storage.
Godfather's Pizza
Location: 1549 S. Dirksen Parkway, Springfield
Date/inspection type: Dec. 10, routine inspection
What: Inspection found 15 violations, four risk factor.
Notes from inspection: Mold was noted throughout the inspection on the soda machine nozzles, which was corrected during the inspection process. Multiple surfaces in the back of the kitchen were soiled with food substances including a pink substance built up on the ice machine, a wire cart covered in grease, the floor under the Broasters and under the three-part sink to be unclean and a sink unsealed from the wall near the chicken preparing area.
Jaalsa
Location: 3114 S. Sixth St., Springfield
Date/inspection type: Dec. 10, routine inspection
What: Inspection found 13 violations, with five risk factor.
Notes from inspection: Like Godfather's Pizza before it, Jaalsa also was found to have mold buildup on the nozzles of soda guns at the restaurant bar. According to notes left by the inspector, there were issues in the kitchen involving large containers of spices not properly covered to avoid food contamination, nor was there any sanitizer solution available for use during food prep.
Mas Sabores
Location: 321 N. Main St., Chatham
Date/inspection type: Dec. 12, routine inspection
What: Inspection found 12 violations, five risk factor.
Notes from inspection: According to the inspector's notes, multiple foods were marked out of date on the shelves, as well as other foods were missing date markings. During the inspection, the expired food was removed from the restaurant.
As far as cleanliness goes, single service utensils were stored face down against compliance with food handling law, while forks, spoons and knives were in contact with soiled shelving above the cake prep area. Black mold was observed coating the caulking near the dish machine, which has been ordered to be replaced to the business owner.
212 China 1
Location: 212 E. South Grand Ave., Springfield
Date/inspection type: Dec. 5, routine inspection
What: Inspection found 12 violation s, five risk factor.
Notes from inspection: According to the inspector, takeout menus were being used as liners on trays holding various foods like egg rolls. In a repeat violation, raw scallops were stored over bean sprouts and chicken was stored on the floor of the cooler, which violates food safety precautions and could cause cross contamination. Other repeat violations included the fan above the freezer soiled with dirt, the chest freezer lid held together with duct tape and the Certified Food Protection Manager on staff neglecting to have their allergen training complete and certificate posted on the wall.
Antonio's Pizza
Location: 1233 Toronto Road, Springfield
Date/inspection type: Dec. 16, routine inspection
What: Inspection found 11 violations, one risk factor.
Notes from inspection: Almost half of the list for December revolves around pizza kitchens, including Antonio's Pizza on Toronto Road, which was found to have leaking sinks and missing drains on the floor. According to the inspector, there were no active sanitizer buckets while food was being prepped.
Luca Pizza
Location: 2937 W. Iles Road, Springfield
Date/inspection type: Dec. 9, routine inspection
What: Inspection found 11 violations, two risk factor.
Notes from inspection: Raw shell eggs were observed stored on top of a pan of mushrooms in the walk-in cooler and was corrected during the inspection to stop the possibility of cross contamination. Two of the three chest freezers have lids that are damaged, with large cracks and exposed insulation. The lids are no longer smooth and would be difficult to clean, which could cause food buildup.

title: Popular Springfield restaurant expands its menu with a twist on a southern favorite
author: Natalie Morris
description: A Springfield restaurant continues to expand its offering of savory treats with an Asian take. Here's what you need to know.
content:
Almadina Halal Restaurant is serving up Middle Eastern and Indian cuisine in a fast-food format.
The latest tenant at 3109 Chatham Road has everything on the menu from shawarma to samosa, biryani to baba ganoush, mandi to hummus. Dessert options range from the Indian doughnuts gulab jamun to the Middle Eastern kunafa to the traditional Yemeni bint al-sahn.
And for the less adventurous, there are hamburgers, chicken strips, hot dogs and fries.
Operating hours are 10 a.m. to midnight Sunday through Thursday, 10 a.m. to 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday. Dine in and take out available. Phone: 217-679-1271.
The new dining establishment is a sister business of the Almadina International Foods grocery store in the Chateau Village strip mall at 2700 W. Lawrence Ave.
The restaurant's home on Chatham Road was previously occupied by Papa John's, but more recently has housed the well-received but short-lived, locally-owned operations Wuakamoles Mexican Grill and Fresh Hut.
New breakfast solutions
A Taste of Seoul has added breakfast selections to the downtown fusion restaurant's menu.
'When we found out (Cafe) Moxo wasn't coming back downtown I figured I'd bring breakfast back,' owner/operator Kimsimone Manning said of the decision to add weekday morning menu to the lineup at 406 E. Adams St.
Morning dishes range from Cajun biscuits and gravy to a Korean-Tex-Mex breakfast taco, bagels with a schmear of cream cheese to a breakfast bagel with a choice of kimchi wasabi or sriracha sauce giving your eggs a little extra kick.
Scrambles feature a choice of egg or tofu and served with oven-roasted potatoes, choice of toast or biscuit and scratch-made compote. The breakfast menu also includes muffins, as well as coffee, tea and orange juice.
Winter hours feature breakfast served from 6 to 11 a.m. and lunch served from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. Tuesday through Friday. Dinner service is 5 to 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday and brunch from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. Saturday and Sunday.
A Taste of Seoul also continues its culinary globe trotting dinner series with a stop in Brazil planned for Jan 26. The meal will be served from 6 to 9 p.m. The dinner starts with Brazilian limonade, followedby Pao de queijo cheese roll, black bean stew served over rice, grilled skirt steak with chimichurri and, for dessert, brigadeiro served with spiked coffee. Cost is $75 a person.
To reserve a seat, call or text 217-970-0810.
The operator of Cafe Moxo has announced plans to open in the former Three Twigs & Co. footprint in Montvale Junction after a June 19 fire forced the popular, downtown breakfast and lunch spot to cease operations at 411 E. Adams St.
Menu expanding
Taki Taco continues to expand its offering of savory treats with an Asian take on a Southern dish – fried chicken and waffles.
The Parkway Pointe eatery has created its version of this comfort food dish with both Korean and Vietnamese twists. This newcomer joins the lineup of taiyaki frozen treats, Korean corn dogs, mochi donuts and boba tea.
'We started with just sweet treats but people like our products, really liked the Korean corn dogs so we decided to try wings,' said Phuong 'Crystal' Hang, who co-owns the business with her husband Phong Thai.
The chicken and waffle entree comes with a choice of chicken wings or buttermilk-soaked chicken tenders fried with a light, seasoned coating and served with Vietnamese mayonnaise and seasoned scallion oil. A dozen additional sauces are available, ranging from a Korean Gochujang to Vietnamese tamarind to the house special Taki sauce.
Other combos featuring the chicken wings and tenders include combo meals replacing the waffles with choice of fries or rice.
Chicken wings also can be purchased a la carte, in party packs and all you can eat options.
Taki Taco at 2955 Lindbergh Blvd. is open from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily.
Lincoln Land's education offering
Lincoln Land Community College's spring lineup of community education offerings range from demos on advanced knife skills to tips on fermentation to hands-on cooking classes ranging from Super Bowl snacks to sausage making.
But anyone hoping to still snag a seat at the popular Bistro Verde dinners will have to get in line.
The line up of four dinners, prepared by local celebrity chefs already are booked. Those still interested are asked to add their names to a waiting list by emailing Jennifer.Lewis@llcc.edu.
Hands-on baking classes offered the spring semester range from cheesecakes to churros, macarons to puff pastry desserts. Cooking classes feature everything from farm fresh vegetarian dishes to freezer meals, soups to salmon. Youth classes, specifically geared to the 8 to 18 crowd, include sessions on yeast doughnuts, tacos and salsa and cupcakes. Classes cost $69.
Looking for a culinary adventure without all the work? Night out classes offer a chef demo with minimal food prep, accompanied with drinks. Events range from Mardi Gras to Medieval, tapas to tacos and tequila. Cost is $79.
A full list of continuing education culinary classes and events can be found online at llcc.edu/community-education/culinary-offerings. Registration is available online or by phone at 217/786-2292.

title: Supreme Court upholds law that could ban TikTok in the U.S., leaving the matter to Trump
author: Maureen Groppe
description: In an unsigned opinion, the Court sided with the national security concerns about TikTok rather than the First Amendment rights. There were no noted dissents.
content:
WASHINGTON − The Supreme Court on Friday unanimously upheld a law that would effectively ban TikTok in the United States on Sunday, siding with the government's national security concerns over the First Amendment rights of the company and its 170 million TikTok users.
That decision shifts the focus to whether President-elect Donald Trump can intervene after he takes office on Monday.
Trump, who tried to ban TikTok during his first administration, has since promised to 'save' the wildly popular platform, though it's unclear how he could do so.
Minutes before the court released its decision, Trump said on social media he'd just spoken with Chinese President Xi Jinping about TikTok and other issues.
'It is my expectation that we will solve many problems together, and starting immediately,' Trump posted.
After the court upheld the law, Trump said he will decide what to do "in the not too distant future."
"Stay tuned!" Trump posted.
Alan Rozenshtein, an expert on the law and technology policy at the University of Minnesota Law School, said none of Trump's options are 'particularly promising.'
'The bottom line?' Rozenshtein wrote in an analysis posted on Lawfare. 'There are a lot of moving pieces and it's foolish to make particularly confident predictions, but the most likely outcome is that TikTok goes dark on the 19th and stays that way for the immediate future.'
The company has said that even a temporary ban on the short-term video app would have 'devastating' effects on TikTok's ability to attract users and content creators. About 170 million Americans − and more than 1 billion people worldwide − use TikTok, according to the company.
The court's decision came a week after the justices heard more than two hours of heated debate on Jan. 10 on whether the government can require the short-form video app to divest from its parent company, China-based ByteDance.
TikTok called that a "massive, unprecedented restriction" of free speech.
"One of America's most popular speech platforms will shut down in nine days," Noel Francisco, an attorney for TikTok who served as solicitor general during Trump's first administration, told the justices on Jan. 10. "That shouldn't happen."
In an unsigned opinion, the court said that while TikTok offers a 'distinctive and expansive outlet for expression, means of engagement, and source of community,' Congress has determined that divestiture is needed because of 'well-supported national security concerns.'
There were no noted dissents, although Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Neil Gorsuch gave their own explanations for why the law should be upheld.
A majority of the court rejected TikTok's argument that the law must meet the toughest test for overcoming a 1st Amendment challenge.
The sell-or-be-banned provision addresses an important government interest unrelated to the suppression of free expression and doesn't go farther than it needs to address that goal, the court said.
The court also cautioned that its analysis is 'narrowly focused' on how the law applies to TikTok, given the abbreviated amount of time the justices had to evaluate it because of the impending deadline.
Still, free speech advocates said the court's decision paves the way for additional 'repressive policies."
Jameel Jaffer, executive director of the Knight First Amendment Institute, said the court has 'weakened the 1st Amendment and markedly expanded the government's power to restrict speech in the name of national security.'
The Department of Justice had argued the restriction is not on speech but on a foreign adversary's ability to control a widely used means of communication. Unless TikTok is sold, the government said, China can gather data on Americans or manipulate the content on TikTok to shape U.S. opinion.
"The Chinese government's control of TikTok poses a grave threat to national security," Solicitor General Elizabeth Prelogar told the court last week.
She said before Trump steps in, he should review all the updated national security information since he was last in office.
In Friday's opinion, the court described Trump's efforts during his first administration to separate TikTok from ByteDance.
Despite his past concerns, the "Art of the Deal" president-elect had urged the Supreme Court to pause the ban to give him time to "negotiate a resolution."
TikTok ban Trump talks to China's Xi Jinping hours before Supreme Court decision
Once in office, Trump could direct his attorney general not to enforce the law. But it's uncertain if Apple, Google and other conduits for the app will feel that's enough protection from the law's stiff penalties.
Pam Bondi, Trump's choice for attorney general, declined during her confirmation hearing Wednesday to commit to enforcing the law.
Bondi said she would "in general" defend U.S. laws against constitutional attacks, but said she couldn't make that specific pledge about the TikTok ban.
Trump could try to take advantage of ambiguity in the law as to whether the president can declare that TikTok is no longer controlled by a Chinese entity.
And there are questions about whether Trump can extend the deadline for TikTok to be divested from ByteDance.
Asked about that during the Supreme Court's debate, Prelogar called it a "statutory interpretation question."
She also said TikTok may have been playing a game of chicken with the U.S. and would find a way to divest once it was clear whether the deadline would hold.
Francisco, TikTok's attorney, told the court the platform would "go dark" on Sunday unless the law was blocked.
'Essentially, the platform shuts down," he said.
But the law doesn't require TikTok to act. The penalties fall on the app stores and companies such as Oracle that host TikTok's content in the U.S. Changes by those companies would make the platform harder to use over time but wouldn't necessarily stop its immediate use for people who already have the app.
On Friday, Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco said enforcing the law "will be a process that plays out over time."
Trump's change of heart on TikTok may, in part, be related to the app's use in connecting him to young voters. His account had 14.8 million followers as of last week.
'TikTok's a great platform that many Americans use and was great for his campaign and getting his message out,' Rep. Mike Waltz, Trump's incoming national security adviser told Fox News Thursday.
Trump also had good things to say about TikTok after he met last year with billionaire Jeff Yass, a major conservative donor with financial ties to ByteDance.

title: 'A low-wage state': How Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker responded to Indiana's secession bill
author: Brittany Carloni
description: Indiana House Republicans unveiled their priorities for 2025, which included a bill to explore adjusting the boundaries of Illinois and Indiana.
content:
Democratic Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker called a bill proposed in the Republican-led Indiana General Assembly that would explore how Illinois counties could secede and join Indiana "a stunt" that is "not going to happen."
The bill, which was unveiled Tuesday as one of the priorities of House Republicans, was filed by House Speaker Todd Huston, the most powerful lawmaker in the House. House Bill 1008 would create the Indiana-Illinois boundary adjustment commission to discuss whether boundaries of the two states can be adjusted to allow Illinois counties to join Indiana.
The debate follows November elections where many rural counties in southern and central parts of Illinois voted to explore seceding from the state. The Illinois attorney general has previously expressed skepticism about the ability for counties to do so, and Pritzker voiced the same in a video clip posted to X Wednesday where he slammed the bill and Indiana's quality of life.
"It's a stunt. It's not going to happen," Pritzker said in response to a question about the secession bill. "I'll just say Indiana is a low-wage state that doesn't protect workers, a state that does not provide health care for people when they're in need, and so I don't think it's attractive for anybody in Illinois where wages are higher where the standard of living is higher, and we do provide health care for people in need."
The debate over the bill shows a clash between states led by two different political parties. Illinois has a Democratic governor in Pritzker and a Democratic-controlled state legislature. Indiana has Republican supermajorities in both chambers of the Statehouse and it's newest Republican governor, Mike Braun, was sworn in Monday.
While Pritzker called the bill a "stunt," Huston on Tuesday called it a "serious proposal."
"To all of our neighbors in the West, we hear your frustrations and invite you to join us in low-cost, low-tax Indiana," Huston said.
IndyStar reporters Hayleigh Colombo and Kayla Dwyer contributed to this story.

title: Pleasant Plains' sisters act soars into Sangamon County tourney: What to know, schedule
author: Bill Welt
description: This season's Pleasant Plains girls basketball team is truly one big happy family, and that love is showing on the court to grab the top seed in this week's Sangamon County tournament, which starts Monday night.
content:
Having multiple sets of sisters is a boon for the Pleasant Plains girls basketball team.
Junior point guard Bailey Leach starts alongside her younger sister, sophomore Jada Leach. The Cardinals' top returning scorer and rebounder, junior forward Anna Weber, welcomed her freshman sibling, Emma, this season. Ditto junior guard Grace Sabatka and her younger sister, also named Emma.
Head coach TJ Fraase's youngest daughter, Ro, is another addition to the team. Ro's sister, Adi, graduated last season and is playing both soccer and basketball at Lincoln Land Community College.
They say it not only creates a fun dynamic but it also strengthens their camaraderie and competitive edge.
The Cardinals (15-5) showed that recently with a 63-34 win over previously-state ranked Pittsfield ahead of this week's Sangamon County girls basketball tournament. Plains, the top seed, opens against either No. 4 Pawnee or No. 5 Williamsville in Tuesday's semifinals at Williamsville.
Boys County preview: How this Auburn senior is adding to family's basketball legacy
'We'll get competitive with each other,' said Emma Sabatka, 'but it's in a fun way and we don't take anything personally.'
Friendly competitors
Each sibling benefits from the other.
The veterans get tested in practice, and they assume the role as on-court mentors.
'As the older sister, I definitely try to guide her in the right way and the best I can,' Grace said.
It encourages the older players to hone their communication and leadership skills, something that Anna appreciates.
'It's really fun because she brings a spark to all the practices and she gives us someone to look forward to,' Anna said. 'We've always made sure to include her in all the drills. It also helps us as teachers and upperclassmen because we can teach younger kids how to do drills and what they need to do, so I think this year has been really fun having her because it makes the practices a little more fun and something to look forward to.'
That sisterly bond raises the intensity level at practice.
'When Grace and Emma (Sabatka) are guarding each other or Jada or Bailey (Leach), it'll always be a race to see who can score first or who can get a stop,' Anna said. 'I think that just adds to the competitiveness to the practices for sure.'
Having a blast
It's a constant competition between Bailey and Jada — in a good way, of course.
Jada made an immediate impact last winter after teammate Madison Burke went down for the season with an injury and was nearly averaging double figures in scoring.
Bailey, who was The State Journal-Register's Small School Girls Soccer Player of the Year as a freshman, said Jada is always smiling and brings joy to the game.
'Running up and down the court,' Jada said, "I'm just smiling and just trying to bring some laughter to the team when we're all just locked in.
'It's kind of just who I am and I like seeing other people happy. So if I'm happy, it makes other people happy.'
The Sabatkas both made sure to credit their teammates for setting them up to score. That close connection reverberates throughout the team and extends beyond basketball.
They generally all play different sports together such as volleyball and soccer. They will also study tests or even go on vacations together — with countless inside jokes to boot.
'Even at practice, we're always having a laugh,' Bailey said.

title: Motion calls appointment of Springfield City Clerk as 'unlawful,' seeks relief from judge
author: Steven Spearie
description: A city man wants a judge to take "any necessary steps" to invalidate Chuck Redpath's appointment as city clerk.
content:
A well-known Springfield media figure has filed a motion seeking a court injunction against the "unlawful appointment" of Springfield Clerk Chuck Redpath Sr.
Calvin T. Christian III filed the motion in Sangamon County court citing a number of legal and ethical violations.
Christian asked the court to require the city to take "any necessary steps" to invalidate Redpath's Jan. 7 appointment and "initiate a lawful process for filling the position in accordance with state law."
Redpath, who had served on the city council for nearly 30 years and since 2015 as Ward 1 alderman, was appointed clerk succeeding Frank Lesko.
Lesko resigned from the position on Dec. 31. He was sworn in as Sangamon County Recorder on Dec. 2 but stayed on as clerk when Josh Langfelder filed for a discovery recount in the race decided by 31 votes.
Several alderpersons openly questioned the process of gathering clerk candidates' names while favoring a more robust vetting system. The city council appoints candidates to positions clerk.
Redpath won the vote 5-3, with two alderpersons voting "present." Redpath voted for himself.
Christian, in his motion, pointed out that violates parts of the Illinois Public Officer Prohibited Activities Act and the Illinois Municipal Code and that it creates "a direct financial conflict of interest.
"Public officials," the motion continued, "must act in the public's best interest, not their own, and such self-serving actions undermine public trust in local governance."
In response to The State Journal-Register on Jan. 8, city attorney Gregory Moredock said Redpath was allowed to vote for himself under the city's consent decree.
The city has been under a consent decree following a successful lawsuit in 1987 that changed how Springfield city government operates.
Christian is behind the website Springfield Leaks and serves on the Massey Commission, formed in the aftermath of the July 6 fatal shooting of Sonya Massey.
Mayor Misty Buscher and the city of Springfield also are named as defendants.
A hearing before Circuit Court Judge Adam Giganti is set for Feb. 14.

title: What is the cheapest ticket price for the NFC & AFC Championship Games this weekend?
author: Dylan Reffe
description: Want to know what the cheapest ticket price is for this weekend's Conference Championship round of the 2025 NFL playoffs? We've got you covered
content:
Football fans are one Sunday away from knowing which two teams will compete at Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans.
The NFC Championship Game features Offensive Player of the Year favorite Saquon Barkley the Philadelphia Eagles hosting rookie sensation Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders.
The AFC Championship Game will write yet another chapter in the growing rivalry between two of the league's best quarterbacks when Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs take the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills.
Players from all four teams will put everything on the line, fans of all four teams have everything to root for, but just how expensive would it be to attend either Conference Championship game in person?
NFC Championship Game tickets
Philadelphia Eagles vs. Washington Commanders
This will be the third time the Eagles and Commanders square off this season, and fittingly will be a rubber match as the two teams split their regular-season series. Eagles vs. Commanders tickets have been selling well all week, and are by far the more expensive ticket between the two games.
When: Sunday, Jan. 26 at 3 p.m. ET
Where: Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pa.
Cheapest ticket: $608
Cheapest lower level ticket: $729
Shop Eagles vs. Commanders NFL playoff tickets
AFC Championship Game tickets
Kansas City Chiefs vs. Buffalo Bills
Mahomes and Allen have played against each other eight teams during their careers, with each quarterback winning four times. That said, Mahomes and the Chiefs are 3-0 in the playoffs against Allen and the Bills.
This is the playoff game most football fans wanted in the AFC, and it's a bit surprising that the cheapest ticket price to the AFC Championship Game is less than half the price of the cheapest ticket to the NFC Championship Game.

title: One last stop: Williamsville holds on to beat Riverton in Sangamo boys basketball thriller
author: Adrian Dater
description: Blake Shoufler scored 25 points, but it was Williamsville's defense that preserved a 42-40 win over Riverton.
content:
WILLIAMSVILLE — The gym at Williamsville High School, along with the school itself, is shiny and modern inside and out, complete with a scoreboard that can show high-definition video. But Friday night's boys basketball game between the host Bullets and visiting Riverton had as great an old-school, Americana vibe as possible.
The smell of hot, buttered popcorn wafted through the gym from the concession stand, while full-throated cheerleading squads from both schools entertained a standing-room-only crowd. There were babies and toddlers throughout, mixed among some who might have been students here when Jack Kennedy was President.
Fans from both sides had plenty to shout about, but it was Williamsville that prevailed in the end, 42-40, over the Hawks in a Sangamo Conference showdown. The Bullets improved to 18-1 on the season and bounced back after suffering their first loss last week against Auburn in the Sangamon County Tournament championship.
Point guard Blake Shoufler, as he's been known to be, was the leading man for the Bullets. He scored 25 of Williamsville's 42 points, while the Bullets held on at the final buzzer, intercepting an inbounds pass under their own basket with 2.2 seconds left to end it.
Williamsville had leads of 18-8 and 20-10 in the first half, but the Hawks stubbornly persisted and nearly pulled out a win.
'Teams like that, you've just got to put them away early, because they're just going to keep bringing it. They play super hard,' Shoufler said. 'Luckily, we got some free throws at the end and got some stops, so it worked out.'
Bullets coach Nick Beard wasn't at all thrilled at how his team played in the second half. But he was happy at beating a team that came in with a 16-2 record and getting its second straight win after suffering that first loss last week.
'It's a great rivalry. They're a really good team, well-coached. They're really physical defensively and took us out of a lot of what we wanted to do. We had a chance to kind of put the hammer on them, but we let them back in, turned the ball over too much. But we played well enough to win,' Beard said.
Beard made a very smart decision by not calling a timeout with the 2.2 seconds left, right after the Bullets threw away an inbounds pass. Riverton (16-3) was out of timeouts, while Williamsville had one. If Beard had called a timeout to devise a defensive play, that would have given Riverton time to draw up a play of their own.
Williamsville put heavy pressure on the inbounds pass and intercepted it around the top of the key.
'It was a scramble, for sure,' Shoufler said. 'We tried to throw a read on the ball real fast, and I had to match up with (Jaxsen Trager, who led Riverton with 14 points), who was having a heck of a game. We just bodied them up and made the right play.'
Carson Doran added eight points for the Bullets, while Brayden Saling added six and Jackson Sanders had three.
Shoufler, whose injury in December of his junior year put a major crimp in Williamsville's state title hopes (the Bullets still finished fourth in the state), said his team isn't getting big-headed despite a gaudy record.
'Our conference is tough, so every single day we know we're going to get teams' best shot,' Shoufler said. 'Every game is going to be the other team's biggest game of the season, so we've just got to be prepared.'
Said Beard: 'We lost to a good Auburn team, but we got back to work. Every night in this conference is going to be a battle. That's just how it is here.'
Riverton coach Matt Mead left before a reporter could catch up to him, and a phone call and text went unanswered.
Adrian Dater is a freelance writer for The State Journal-Register. He can be reached through the sports department at sports@sj-r.com.

title: 2025 Oscar nominations: How to watch and our predictions
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The 2025 Academy Award nominations are Thursday morning. Here is how to watch and our picks for the top awards.
content:
The nominees for the 97th annual Academy Awards will be announced Thursday by the Academy of Motion Pictures Arts and Sciences, revealing the contenders across 23 categories to mark the best in film for 2024.
Here is what you need to know about the 2025 Oscar nominations show and our predictions for the 97th annual Academy Awards:
When are the Oscar nominations announced?
The 2025 Oscar nominations will be announced 7:30 a.m. CT in a live show from the Samuel Goldwyn Theater in Los Angeles. The reveal is hosted by actor Bowen Yang of "Saturday Night Live" and actress Rachel Sennott. The nominations announcement were originally set for Jan. 17, but were moved because of the California wildfires.
How to watch 2025 Oscar nominations
The Oscar nominations for the 97th Academy Awards will air live on ABC's "Good Morning America," "ABC News Live," Disney+ and Hulu. The live show will also stream on Oscars.com, Oscars.org and all of the Academy's social media.
2025 Oscar nominations live stream
2025 Oscar predictions
It is a wide-open race in multiple categories this year, especially in the major awards. Here are our predictions and one to watch for each of the top seven awards: Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actress, Best Actor, Best Supporting Actress and Best Supporting Actor.
2025 Best Picture predictions

LAST IN:"A Real Pain," and "Sing Sing"
WATCH FOR: "Nickel Boys" and "September 5"

LAST IN: Coralie Fargeat, "The Substance."
WATCH FOR: RaMell Ross, Nickel Boys
2025 Best Actress predictions

LAST IN: Cynthia Erivo, "Wicked"; and Fernanda Torres, "I'm Still Here"
WATCH FOR: Marianne Jean-Baptiste, "Hard Truths"
2025 Best Actor predictions
LOCKS: Adrien Brody, "The Brutalist"; Timothee Chalamet, "A Complete Unknown"; and Ralph Fiennes, "Conclave."
LAST IN: Daniel Craig, "Queer"; and Colman Domingo, "Sing Sing."
WATCH FOR: Sebastian Stan, "A Diferent Man"
2025 Best Supporting Actress predictions
LOCKS: Ariana Grande, "Wicked"; Felicity Jones, "The Brutalist"; and Zoe Saldana, "Emilia Perez."
LAST IN: Isabella Rossellini, "Conclave"; Margaret Qually, "The Substance."
WATCH FOR: Jamie Lee Curtis, "The Last Showgirl"
2025 Best Supporting Actor predictions
LOCKS: Yura Borisov, "Anora"; Kieran Culkin, "A Real Pain'; and Edward Norton, "A Complete Unknown."
LAST IN: Guy Pearce, "The Brutalist"; and Jeremy Strong, "The Apprentice."

When are the 2025 Oscars?
The 97th Oscars are set for 6 p.m. CT Sunday, March 2, at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles.
