title: 'I miss them so much:' Coroner identifies man, boys killed in fatal house fire
author: Steven Spearie
description: A father and his two sons who died in a house fire outside of Springfield over the weekend have been identified.
content:
Sangamon County Coroner Jim Allmon released the names of two of the victims from Saturday's fatal house fire in Virden.
Kyle James, 34, and his son, Hunter James, 13, both were pronounced dead at Springfield Memorial Hospital on Saturday.
Both died of smoke inhalation, Allmon said in a news release Monday.
Jacob James, 10, was pronounced dead by Macoupin County Coroner Anthony Kravanya at the house in the 200 block of West Neal Street shortly after 10 a.m. Saturday. Kravanya said Monday in a separate press release that Jacob also died of smoke inhalation.
Jacob James was a sixth grader at Springfield SASED (Sangamon Area Special Education District). Hunter James, who was bussed to Auburn, was in eighth grade, Stufflebeam said.
Their home school district was North Mac.
Kyle James was a cook at Jo's Place, a restaurant in Virden.
The three had moved into the house, a rental, in November, said Barb Stufflebeam, Hunter and Jacob's maternal grandmother.
The boys' mother, Shelby Stufflebeam, lives in Lincoln, with their sister, Molly, 8.
"I miss them so much," Barb Stufflebeam said Monday. "I wanted to see them grow up as young men. Now, I can't see them grow up."
All North Mac schools, said Superintendent Kyle M. Hacke on Facebook, will have counselors on hand Tuesday. Schools were closed Monday for Presidents Day.
"Our hearts go out to the family and friends during this time of grief," Hacke said.
Michelle Clevenger stopped by the house Saturday to hang ribbons and place teddy bears in the front yard with her friend, Glenda Garrett. Both are from Virden.
Hunter James, Clevenger said, was the same age as her oldest grandson.
"Hunter always called my grandson his 'first best friend,'" Clevenger said.
According to a Virden Fire Department press release, the initial call about the fire came in just after 9:20 a.m. Saturday from a passer-by.
Several area fire departments were called in, including Chatham, Auburn and Girard.
Virden is about 35 minutes southwest of Springfield.

title: Illinois protestors rally at state capitol against President Trump
author: Tom Ackerman
description: One of the signs at the rally read "Trump is not a king" while another read "hate is not patriotic."
content:
Protestors again rallied at the Illinois capitol on Presidents Day against the Trump administration, despite freezing temperatures. The crowd of about 200 marched in the street to the home of Abraham Lincoln.
At a protest earlier this month, some of the same organizers helped draw a comparable number of demonstrators.
Monday's protest was peaceful. Springfield Police officers blocked off portions of the roads as the group marched to the Lincoln Home National Historic Site Visitor Center.
'I know a lot of people are of the opinion that standing out here with a sign and yelling into the void really doesn't do much. I disagree,' said Tristan Sites, one of the organizers. 'It gets people talking about it.'
Sites, who traveled about 45 minutes south to get to Springfield, said national coordination of the event is proof that talking about issues can lead to a larger presence.
The 50501 Movement is a grassroots movement, meaning there is no official, local organization in each U.S. state, though protests are taking place around the country.
'We understand that with our state government – we are in a very fortunate situation' Sites said. 'Our governor is our MVP right now. Gov. (JB) Pritzker is doing an incredible job standing up to the Trump administration…We want to hear more from the other people in positions of power in the state of Illinois. We want to hear that you are on our side.'
Some carried signs to the effect of 'Trump is NOT a KING.'
(This story has been updated to add a new video.)

title: Person dies in Jacksonville garage fire
author: Tom Ackerman
description: One person has died following a fire in Jacksonville Sunday while another person was taken to the hospital.
content:
One person has died following a fire in Jacksonville over the weekend.
Authorities were called to a garage fire at the 600 block of South Diamon for a report of a garage fire Sunday morning around 10 a.m. The garage was fully engulfed with flames by the time they arrived, according to a news release.
More: 'There are no words:' Three dead in house fire south of Springfield
Officers contacted the homeowner who told them that a woman was inside the garage. The Jacksonville Fire department put the fire out and found a woman dead inside. A man was also taken to Jacksonville Memorial Hospital for smoke related injuries.
The death and the nature of the fire are being investigated.

title: 'Just incredible': Chatham Glenwood wrestler Cody Moss wins Class 2A heavyweight state title
author: Bill Welt
description: Chatham Glenwood's Cody Moss' wrestling dream came true at the state finals on Saturday
content:
Chatham Glenwood junior Cody Moss became the school's second-ever boys wrestling state champion at the State Farm Center in Champaign on Saturday.
Moss jumped ahead 7-3 during the first period before withstanding East Peoria's Jose Del Toro (48-3) for a 9-7 decision for the Class 2A title at 285 pounds.
Former Glenwood standout Drew Davis won the school's first title at 106 pounds in 2022 before becoming a repeat champion at 113 pounds in 2023.
Moss was the only wrestler from the Springfield area to reach the championship round.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
"I've been dreaming of this since I was a kid: being a state champ," Moss said. "This is just incredible. Just incredible. It's so surreal to actually be here and experiencing it."
Moss (39-5) initially fell behind 3-0 in the first 30 seconds before registering a takedown and near fall for the lead. He opened the third period with an 8-4 cushion.
Moss said he needed to get control right away.
"I was trying to score early; I didn't want to have to come back at the end," Moss said. "I heard my coaches counting it down at the end and that excitement started to really build. It's just an incredible feeling."
Moss previously appeared at 215 pounds and finished 2-2 at last year's state finals after winning his first sectional title. He dominated this year's Lincoln Sectional in the heavyweight class and won two of his first three matches via pin to reach the championship match.
Moss, ranked No. 3 by Illinois Matmen ahead of the state finals, pinned Cary-Grove's top-ranked wrestler, Lucas Burton, in the third period, while Del Toro was ranked second.
Other state medalists in the area hailed from the Petersburg PORTA co-op in Class 1A. Junior Justin Zimmerman won an 8-2 decision over Olney Richland's Carson Bissey for fifth place at 157 pounds, while fellow junior Zach Bryant earned sixth at 132.

title: Contested housing project gets full approval from Springfield City Council
author: Claire Grant
description: Construction is expected to start on the homes by the spring of 2026. Here's what you need to know.
content:
A development project on the east side of town to build more than four dozen homes on the city's east side TIF district passed through city council, after vehement disapproval from local unions.
Ordinance 2025-063 and 064 would authorize a combined $1.5 million of Far East Tax Increment Finance funds, or TIF funds, and federal block grant funds for The Nehemiah Expansion project's redevelopment of the area in Ward 2 with 50 homes.
The homes will be two to four bedrooms in each unit while the project would tear down 11 abandoned homes in the district, improving 76 lots.
One after another, both ordinances were voted unanimously for approval with no discussion. The homes are expected to be started by early 2026.
'To the mayor and to alderman Gregory thank you for your support and agreement so 50 new affordable houses can begin,' Calvary Missionary Baptist Church Rev. Silas Johnson said. 'We look forward to working with the city and working with the PLA.'
The lack of discussion was a far cry from the committee of the whole meeting on Feb. 12 when union members packed the room.
The catch-all comes from a project labor agreement requiring local union involvement in large-scale projects from 2023 that developers say will raise costs too high to continue the project.
Nehemiah Expansion founder Rev. Johnson said at the Feb. 12 meeting the PLA would raise costs by more than $5 million and requested a modified version of the PLA for only infrastructure positions to be local union required. With both ordinances, a PLA is required so workers be paid at least Illinois prevailing wage for all work. The PLA must be signed into agreement as well, before the project will be provided the approved funding.
At the same meeting, contractor on the project Mike Niehaus pushed that the city code around PLA requiring union inclusion, barring the exception a labor agreement, would not advance the city's efficiency and labor stability.
Springfield consultant and retired manager of Laborers 477 Brad Schaive dissuaded the council from believing Rev. Johnson's $5 million price jump.
Schaive said the prior phases of the houses had been built were not made with a PLA and labor had been recruited from outside the city with primarily white employees. He then scolded Rev. Johnson for not having the detailed costs to reach that price point on Feb. 12.
"(Scheel's Sports Park) is being done under a project labor agreement, one of the largest projects the city has ever seen," Schaive said about mandatory labor agreements. "PLA in this area is the standard: not the rarity. The school district, the park district, the sanitary district, the city and the county all have PLAs. The state of Illinois mandates PLAs."
At city council the following week, if he had it, Rev. Johnson did not bring out the cost report to explain the cost jump Schaive had requested.
About the Nehemiah Project
The Nehemiah Expansion project spearheaded by Rev. Johnson, a former CWLP union electrician, and general contractor Niehaus would cost an estimated $23 million, with $18 million dedicated to construction.
This will be the fifth stage of the Nehemiah expansion project, and the first to be built with a modified PLA in place.
The previous four phases of the project created 120 homes and used over 300 vacant lots on the east side of Springfield since 2006, largely funded by the Illinois Housing and Development Authority. The last phase, started in 2023 and developed 40 homes along the intersection of Grand Avenue and Wheeler Street.
'Here in Illinois, housing is not a privilege—it's a right. And my administration is committed to ensuring that every family has access to a safe, affordable place to call home,' said Governor JB Pritzker in June of 2023. 'This latest project to build forty single-family homes in Springfield achieves exactly that— providing affordable housing opportunities for a community that has been underdeveloped and underserved for far too long.'

title: Punk rocker tied to neo-fascist group has private show set for Springfield area
author: Steven Spearie
description: Michale Graves was the lead singer for the punk band Misfits from 1995 to 2000. He also has ties to the Proud Boys.
content:
Michale Graves has had a number of concerts canceled because of his connection to the Proud Boys.
Graves' acoustic tour has three Illinois dates, including Sherman.
Graves testified in the 2023 trial of former Proud Boys leader Enrique Tarrio.
The lead singer of a re-formed version of the punk band Misfits from the 1990s has a show booked in the Springfield area despite a string of concerts being cancelled recently over his affiliation with the neo-fascist group, the Proud Boys.
The kickoff to Michale Graves' spring acoustic tour in Pittsburgh was nixed at three different venues and concerts in St. Louis, Chattanooga, Colorado Springs, Akron and Punta Gorda, Florida, also were called off.
Graves' website listed a March 6 stop in Sherman, though it is a "Private Event."
A message sent to the website seeking further information was not returned.
Graves has other Illinois shows in Darien on March 5, now the tour opener, and Dixon on March 7.
Graves was the lead singer of Misfits from 1995 to 2000, a later incarnation of the band founded by Glenn Danzig in 1977.
With Misfits and other bands, Graves performed in skull face paint.
Graves is no stranger to central Illinois. He played Pizza Records in Jacksonville as part of "One Man Roadshow" acoustic tour last February and performed at The Curve Inn in Southern View on Oct. 16, 2017.
In 2012, Graves was the lead singer in Marky Ramone's Blitzkrieg at Donnie's Homespun Pizza, which had just opened up in Vinegar Hill Mall, on Oct. 4, 2012.
Management from Afterlife, a concert venue in Akron, posted on Facebook that it was "unaware of Graves' involvement with the Proud Boys" and admitted the booking turned out to be "a mistake.
"We saw all the posts and messages you sent us to inform us of Michale Graves' recent history," the post read.
Via X, Graves said that groups were "actively pressuring the (Darien) venue to cancel me."
Graves has in the past endorsed the Proud Boys on platforms like Instagram and has backed conspiracy theorist Alex Jones.
In 2023, he testified at the trial of several Proud Boys members, including former leader, Henry "Enrique" Tarrio, who was charged with seditious conspiracy in the assault by President Donald Trump supporters on the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021.
Tarrio and other Proud Boys leaders who were convicted received pardons from Trump shortly after his inauguration.
Before Jan. 6, Proud Boys' members had been arrested and convicted of attacking, harassing or threatening civilians or political groups they disagreed with, including Black Lives Matter.
Graves was in Washington on Jan. 6 and briefly played on a stage near the Senate Building. Later that night, he was supposed to play a private show for Proud Boys members but left Washington.
In an interview earlier this week with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, Graves said he's "not a hateful person."
Graves added that the Proud Boys he knew were "just normal people...There's no coordinated effort to stamp out people who are different. That's not going on. I would immediately distance myself from it and call it out wherever I saw it."
Heather Smock, a co-owner of Pizza Records, said she was aware of possible problems in booking Graves last year.
"Nobody came and picketed or threw a fit about it," Smock said. "I'm sure there were people who didn't like it, but we didn't have any problems. Really, it was a great night.
"He's very humble and polite. He's not confrontational in person."

title: Duolingo's make-believe mascot, Duo the Owl, duped his death
author: Greta Cross
description: Two weeks after Duo the Owl's demise, Duolingo's language learning app's mascot admitted that "faking my death was a test."
content:
Duo the Owl, Duolingo's make-believe mascot, is alive. The language-learning app announced on Monday that the mascot had faked his death.
Duolingo announced two weeks ago that the mascot was fatally struck by a Tesla Cybertruck, resulting in his "death."
Duo, introduced with the app in 2011, has grown increasingly popular in recent years as he has parodied pop culture referencing and appeared in outrageous memes.
Nearly two weeks after Duolingo announced the death of their beloved mascot, Duo the Owl, fans around the world learned they had been duped all along.
In an Instagram video released on Monday, the language learning app quickly recapped the owl's death before the bright green bird is seen bursting from flames with a comic book-style text bubble that reads, 'I'm back.'
'Faking my death was the test,' Duo wrote in the caption, 'and you all passed.'
The quick-paced video shows the completion of several in-app challenges, implying that users' increased activity on the app may have brought the beloved mascot back to life.
In fact, the stunt was part of a global campaign in which the app pawned different countries against one another to see which could earn the most XP (experience points) to save Duo. As of Monday, the top three performing countries were the United States, Germany and Brazil, according to the Bring Back Duolingo website.
'Our favorite green owl has returned − though how he came back varies across different markets,' a Duolingo spokesperson told USA TODAY. 'As always, we love leaning into creative storytelling that keeps our learners engaged, and this campaign was a fun way to do just that. We're not done telling this story just yet − more details on what really happened to Duo will be revealed soon.'
How is the internet reacting?
Many of the top comments on the TikTok video were left by brands, weighing in on the news.
'What was it all for tho?' mobile game Subway Surfers commented on the video. 'This Monday got so much better,' replied Microsoft Surface.
'So are my missed lessons forgiven or nah'? Tide Rescue said, followed by, 'It's magic fr (for real). Corpo (corporation) brand magic,' commented cereal brand Magic Spoon.
Who created the comeback video?
Video editor Mikey, known online as Kiuzr, began working with Duolingo to create social media videos in December. Mikey's first project was the brand's annual Duolingo Year in Review. This video is visually similar to the recent one announcing Duo's 'resurrection,' featuring fast-paced edits. Mikey, who is based in the Philippines, wished to be referred to only by first name for privacy reasons.
Duolingo became aware of Mikey's work after Mikey posted a 'silly, bored edit' they did that featured Duo the Owl last year.
'I then went to bed as soon as I posted it, not expecting anything crazy in return. I then woke up to Duolingo following me and telling me to check (my) DM (direct message) and there I was, offered ... multiple editing projects with them,' Mikey said. Today, Mikey is a contract video editor with the brand.
Who is Duo the Owl?
Duo Keyshauna Renee Lingo, more commonly known as Duo the Owl, was born in 1000 BC, according to an X post made by Duolingo. The silly, animated green owl is known for quite aggressively reminding users to complete their daily lessons.
While Duolingo jokes its mascot was born in 1000 BC, Duo actually debuted in 2011, the year the app launched, according to Apple Developer. But Duo looked different then. The original Duolingo logo featured a 2-D owl whose eyes and mouth spelled out 'DUO.' A year later, the first 3-D version of Duo was released with a realistic owl body and two wide eyes that seemingly stared right into a user's soul.
In 2014, Duolingo decided to 'gamify' its mascot, making him cuter and more animated, according to Apple Developer. By 2018, the Duo the Owl users know and love (or fear) was released.
In recent years, Duo grew increasingly popular as he parodied pop culture references, appeared in outrageous memes and even partnered with Netflix to promote 'Squid Game.'

title: Is there an election on Tuesday in Illinois? Depends on where you live
author: Tom Ackerman
description: You may have heard Tuesday is an election day in Illinois. Or maybe you haven't, but it could be because of where you live. Let us explain.
content:
Residents of Illinois in some counties next week will have an election.
Do you have an election in your county, and what is on the ballot?
Here's what you need to know.
What election is on Tuesday?
Less than 20 counties on Tuesday will hold a Consolidated Municipal Primary Election.
Those elections could decide aldermanic positions or village trustees, for example, depending on your city's form of government. This primary is usually only held for municipal governments that are nonpartisan, which is a slim portion of Illinois.
Is there an election where I live?
Elections will take place in the following counties and city:
Adams (42 precincts are holding primaries for both Republican and Democrat offices)
Boone (21 precincts are holding primaries for Republican offices)
Champaign (23 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat offices)
Cook (114 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat and nonpartisan offices)
DeKalb (24 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat offices.
DuPage (105 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat offices)
Grundy (12 precincts are holding primaries for Republican offices)
Kane (68 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat offices)
Kankakee (11 precincts are holding primaries for the Bourbonnais Citizens Party)
Kendall (36 precincts are holding primaries for Republican offices)
Lake (55 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat offices)
Livingston (10 precincts are holding primaries for Republican offices)
Logan (13 precincts are holding primaries for Republican offices)
McHenry (130 precincts are holding primaries for Republican offices)
Peoria (65 precincts are holding primaries for Republican and nonpartisan offices)
Rock Island (34 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat offices)
Will (24 precincts are holding primaries for Republican and nonpartisan offices)
Winnebago (21 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat offices)
City of Rockford (86 precincts are holding primaries for Democrat offices)
What are these counties voting on specifically?
To learn what office is up for a vote, residents should contact their local County Clerk's office.
Why are nonpartisan offices on the list?
That could mean more than four candidates are vying for a single, non-partisan office.
'If you have five candidates seeking the office of mayor, then in the consolidated primary, that's where they narrow that down to two candidates,' said Matt Dietrich, who is the spokesperson for the Illinois Board of Elections.
The label could also mean there are more than four times the number of candidates when there are multiple vacancies. For example, there may be two open seats on a park board and nine people filed to run. The primary would narrow the field to four candidates.
Isn't there an election in April?
Yes, the Illinois Consolidated Municipal General Election takes place Tuesday, April 1.
Who's on the ballot can depend on what cycle a given county government is on, but it can include local government offices like village trustees and village presidents, village clerks, school board trustees, fire protection district trustees, and public library trustees, among others.
To see who is running in your county, consult your local County Clerk.
There also can be county-wide referenda, which can be searched for on the Illinois State Board of Education website.

title: 'It doesn't feel real sometimes': Calvary's Josh Long begins to thrive again after family tragedy
author: Ryan Mahan
description: Josh Long lost his father at age 8, and his mother less than a year ago. The Calvary Academy basketball player is slowly finding new family, and a new path for life by trusting himself and his faith.
content:
AI-assisted summary
Josh Long, a 16-year-old high school student, has faced immense tragedy, losing both parents in a span of eight years.
Despite the hardships, Josh has found solace in his faith and basketball, excelling both on and off the court.
Josh is musically gifted and plans to pursue a career in ministry and leadership, inspired by his faith and desire to help others.
After Josh Long went through the untimely death of a parent for the second time last summer, the 16-year-old can't always control when those memories, and the emotions that come with them, will return.
'It's definitely different, because I'll be driving and then I'll just think about her and memories, or I'll just be chilling and memories (rush back),' Josh said. 'It doesn't feel real sometimes.'
In 2016, when Josh was 8 years old, his dad, Raymond Long, died from kidney failure. Eight years later, Josh, and the Calvary Academy community, were jolted by the death of Josh's mom, Misty Long, who was allegedly stabbed to death on last June by Josh's twin brother Jonathan.
As the winter heads toward spring, the 16-year-old junior at Calvary is thriving, now living with longtime friend and Calvary teammate Luke Blackford, assistant coach Matt Blackford and his wife, Lesley.
Josh will always keep Misty and Raymond close in his heart, and they are also physically close — the Roselawn Cemetery where they are buried together is near the Blackford residence.
'She was a really good mom,' Josh said. 'She would always care for people and liked to help take care of people.'
Following Misty's death, the Blackfords stepped up for Josh. Lesley and Matt had an extra bedroom — their older sons, Alec, 28, and Isaac, 25, are grown and out of the house.
'I've just seen him change as he's just been more comfortable around here, knowing that he's not a guest,' Matt said of Josh. 'He's now family, forever.'
Fond memories of family
Josh and Jonathan Long were adopted by Misty and Raymond Long when they were infants. From the short time between their birth until adoption, they had been fostered by the grandparents of current Calvary basketball teammate Josiah Reynolds.
'My mom and my dad babysat us, and they really wanted us,' Josh said.
The Blackfords remembered seeing the boys at slow-pitch softball games as Raymond umpired.
'I remember the double strollers, coming to the softball games, Misty would be pushing them while Raymond was umping,' Matt said. 'She'd push the stroller up with them.'
Eventually, Misty and Josh found shared passions.
'She loved Disney and when we went to Disney World, it was awesome,' Josh remembered. 'We split up at Disney World; my mom's friend took my brother somewhere and it was just me and my mom at Disney, and it was just nice. We walked around the park and talked and had food.'
The Long household could sound like a symphony at times, too. Jonathan Long participated in musical productions at The Muni and at the Hoogland Center for the Arts.
'I would always hear soundtracks and stuff like that in the car, because they'd be playing it 24/7,' Josh said of rides with Misty and Jonathan. 'I got into that music kind of, too.'
Coping through losses
As he dealt with his mother's death, Josh focused on two things: God and basketball.
'I really locked in and tried to get closer with God,' Josh said. 'I remember my Bible teacher, the year before, he said something like, 'God's going to test you to see if you're going to run away from God or seek guidance from God.'
'And that's really what I did when it happened. I was in the (interrogation) room just praying to God ... and I said, 'No matter the outcome, I'm still going to trust you and stay by your side.''
Just days later, Calvary was to play in a summer basketball event.
'At first, I wasn't going to play, and then I realized I'd need to play to get my mind off stuff,' Josh said.
Matt wondered if it was a good idea.
'I'm not going to lie, I was nervous about him playing that first game — not about his skill, but that's a lot,' Matt said. 'He had to deal with an awful lot for a high school kid. And then you have a physical game. But he was amazing, and he played great, and he was doing really well. I was worried about nothing.'
Josh not only turned to basketball, he elevated himself, on the court and off.
'I think he's a better basketball player now, because his focus is where he wants it to be, he's not so focused on points,' Lesley said. 'I've also noticed less anger, too; really focused on the floor, very calm and collective, very self-assured (and) playing for God.'
Luke said he's seen how much work Josh has put into the game.
'He's a good teammate,' Luke said. 'He's worked hard and he's a good example for everyone else, too.'
Settled in
Moving in with the Blackfords, Josh brought his 2-year-old dog Bruce, a Husky and German Shepherd mix. Bruce gets along with everyone — except the Blackfords' dog, Tank. Old and set in his ways, Tank wasn't pleased to share his domain with an energetic rookie.
That might've been the toughest transition.
Josh and Luke get along, though they occasionally bicker — like siblings.
"Only if we're playing one-v-one; we just go back and forth,' Josh said. 'Connor (Brown, a 2024 Calvary graduate and former teammate) would work out with us, too, and he'd have to stop us because we'd start yelling at each other.'
With a college basketball game on the television, Josh was asked how tall he was. 'Six foot,' he said with a smile, 'they don't believe me. I'm 6-foot.'
When asked his own height, Luke said 'Six-four,' before Lesley jokingly said, 'If (Josh is) saying he's 6-foot, (Luke's) 6-5.'
Life with the Blackfords is slowly becoming routine.
'Kind of feels like it's like back to normal,' Josh said. 'When it all first happened, it was weird, it didn't feel real, but like now it feels normal.'
Lesley is called by her first name, while Matt, who teaches math and history at Calvary, remains 'Mr. B.'
'At first it felt like he was staying here, but it wasn't his house,' Lesley said. 'He would ask, like, 'Can I get a drink,' and I was like, 'Stop asking, you don't have to ask.''
Josh splits time on holidays with family members of Misty and Raymond.
'It's kind of like part of our family now, too,' Lesley said and later added: 'We wanted him to still be part of his family and every single one of them would have taken him in. They just didn't want his life to be so uprooted. They knew Calvary was very important to him, and that was our goal, was to keep things as close to the same as possible.'
That hasn't been easy. Josh said having so much media attention on the events of late June was odd, but Matt and Lesley said Josh coped with more maturity than expected from a 16-year-old.
'It was just weird that everybody knew because it's like stuff you see on movies,' Josh said. 'It did not feel real at all.'
Plans to give back
Religion has meant a lot to Josh throughout his life, but that relationship has taken on further significance over the last year. Josh sings and plays music for the church's worship team; on Wednesdays, he sings or plays drums in the Calvary youth group.
Josh plans to study ministry and leadership. He said he received that calling as a freshman but was nervous to sing in front of other people.
'After everything happened with my mom, I was like, 'Yeah, I've really got to do this,'' Josh said. 'I would always only sing in my room. I was really nervous, but I had to remind myself I wasn't doing it for the people, I was doing it for God and to glorify Him.'
His talent impresses Lesley, who whipped out a phone to proudly show a video of Josh's singing ability.
'He's going to be modest, but he's very good. He's definitely gifted,' Lesley said.
After basketball season, Josh plans to work at Calvary alongside Luke, working with kids who are dropped off before school begins.
'That's what I like doing, knowing my mom worked in a daycare, I was always around kids and kids would be attached to me,' Josh said. 'I was a teacher's assistant, and I would always talk to kids and kids would always come up to me and give me hugs at school. I'm just good with kids, I guess; I think that's also from my mom, too.'
It's also a little bit of personal experience.
'I was not a good kid growing up,' Josh said, 'and when there's kids that are getting in trouble, I see myself, and (know) they could change.'

title: Rochester girls continue resolve in season-ending loss to Mahomet-Seymour
author: Ryan Mahan
content:
CHATHAM — Though Rochester's girls basketball team didn't complete its comeback on Tuesday in the Class 3A Chatham Glenwood Sectional semifinals, there were similar themes to the Rockets' entire run throughout the postseason.
Rochester, which entered the Taylorville Regional quarterfinals with just eight wins, bucked the odds to win three games and a regional championship. On Tuesday, down 18 points in the first half, Rochester battled to get within eight points late in the third before Mahomet-Seymour regained control and won the sectional semifinal, 54-32.
Brandon Rose was proud of everything his team gave.
'It's just the mindset of those girls,' Rose said. 'With our regular season, they could've thrown in the towel before that first game against Lanphier (a 63-22 win for Rochester on Feb. 15). To go and do what they did, it says a lot about their character and the fact that they weren't going to be done.'
In the process, Rochester upended No. 2 seed Chatham Glenwood in the semifinals, 42-33. The Titans, though without Katelyn Lehnen and Makaela Diamond to injuries, were still the regional favorites after finishing second in the Class 3A state tournament a year ago.
In the Taylorville title game, the seventh-seeded Rockets beat the host Tornadoes. Taylorville, the No. 3 seed, was without an injured Addison Tarr but still had senior leadership — and talent — in Mazie Fleming and Kyleigh Heimsness. Tarr, Fleming and Heimsness all scored more than 1,000 points each in their respective careers.
'Winning the regional the way we did, that's a big deal,' Rose said.
All that positivity didn't diminish the pain the Rochester players experienced with their season-ending loss. Nearly every player emerged from the locker room with obvious signs of recent tear-shedding.
Senior Taylor Offer was one such player. Courtney Fonte hit a 3-pointer to put Mahomet-Seymour up 33-19 with 5 minutes, 7 seconds left in the third. But junior Alaina Stock scored a transition layup, Cami Tinder knocked down a 3-pointer and Offer drained a free throw to pull within 33-25 with 2:05 left in the period. Stork (nine points) and Offer (eight) led the scoring for the Rockets.
Offer said the team just doesn't panic.
'I've learned about mental toughness since my freshman year,' Offer said. 'The game isn't over until that last buzzer hits.'
The Bulldogs hit eight 3s in the game by five different players using a five-out offense. It turned out to be just too much firepower for the Rockets (11-23).
'We knew they were going to be a good-shooting team,' Delaney Farris said. 'We had to slowly chip away at it and I think us keeping our composure, we know that's the main key, especially from our last two big games.'
While there were more than double the losses of the Rockets' wins, the players will try to remember the fun that came with ending the seasons of three teams.
'We weren't really expected to get this far, but it feels great that we at least had the opportunity to get here,' Offer said. 'Our teamwork brought us here.'
Kylie Waldinger led the Bulldogs with 24 points. Mahomet-Seymour (20-11) will face Quincy Notre Dame (31-3) on Thursday in the sectional championship game. QND beat Decatur MacArthur 62-53 in Tuesday's other semifinal.

title: DoorDash to pay millions to dashers after company pocketed tips
author: Natalie Neysa Alund
description: The city's top prosecutor said if you were a DoorDash delivery worker in New York between 2017 and 2019 you may be entitled to restitution.
content:
New York's top prosecutor on Monday announced a nearly $17 million settlement with the delivery platform DoorDash for "misleading both consumers and delivery workers" by using tips intended for its drivers to subsidize their pay.
The online delivery platform, headquartered in San Francisco, used the wage model between May 2017 and September 2019 to pocket drivers' tips, according to court papers filed in the case.
New York Attorney General Letitia James said an investigation conducted by her office found DoorDash misled customers by pocketing tips intended for its drivers, dubbed Dashers, and added the funds to the driver's base pay, instead of providing them the full tips they earned.
'This is just fundamentally unfair,' James said during a news conference in Manhattan. 'Customers had no reason to believe that these tips were being used by DoorDash to reduce its costs...They knew it wasn't right and they did it anyway."
DoorDash responds
On Tuesday a DoorDash spokesperson told USA TODAY the company "remains committed to making sure that Dasher earnings are always fair and transparent."
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
"The allegations settled were related to an old pay model that was retired in 2019," the spokesperson said. "While we believe that our practices properly represented how Dashers were paid during this period, we are pleased to have resolved this years-old matter and look forward to continuing to offer a flexible way for millions of people to reach their financial goals.'
'Delivery workers are integral to our communities'
Under the settlement, DoorDash will now provide Dashers "with an accessible disclosure that explains the disclosures that a Dasher will see in their mobile application before the Dasher chooses to accept a delivery order."
'Delivery workers are integral to our communities, working tirelessly to bring food and other essentials directly to our doorsteps in all conditions,' James said. "This settlement returns millions to the pockets of hardworking Dashers and ensures transparency in DoorDash's payment practices going forward.'
'We have your back': How to file a claim in New York DoorDash settlement
In the coming weeks, James said her office will provide information about how eligible delivery workers can file a claim to receive money from the settlement.
James said an administrator would set up a website regarding the claim.
"If you were a Dasher or delivery worker in New York between 2017 and 2019 you may be entitled to restitution. I urge all of you to file a claim," James said. "We have your back."

title: Joann Fabrics closing all locations—including Illinois stores
author: Claire Grant
description: The news has gotten much, much worse for arts and crafts fans nationwide.
content:
AI-assisted summary
All 800+ Joann Fabrics stores will close after the company was auctioned off to a new ownership group.
Going-out-of-business sales are underway at all locations, but gift cards are no longer being accepted.
Weeks after announcing the closure of 500 stores, Joann Fabrics announced it will be closing all of its 800+ locations.
The shift in store operations to absolute zero comes after the fabric and craft retailer was auctioned off to a new ownership group. Retail liquidator GA Group and Joann's term lenders won the bidding for the bankrupt company on Feb. 22, when the remaining assets of the company were put up for auction.
"JOANN leadership, our Board, advisors and legal partners made every possible effort to pursue a more favorable outcome that would keep the company in business," the company statement reads. "We are committed to working constructively with the winning bidder to ensure an orderly wind-down of operations that minimizes the impact on all our stakeholders."
The GA Group has a stretching history with Joann and helped the craft company buy competitor, House of Fabrics, in the 1990s.
The new ownership plans on "multimillion-dollar retention plan" for Joann's around 19,000 employees, including organizing job fairs and granting workers time off so they can interview for other jobs.
In collaboration with the new ownership group, the Hudson, Ohio-based retailer announced it will shut down operations at all stores after conducting going-out-of-business sales at each location.
Federal court records show the action results will be formally approved on Feb. 26 at the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.
When the company announced the closure of 500 locations, it included 26 Illinois locations. Originally, stores across the state, including Springfield, Rockford and Peoria, were set to remain open. Now, all of those locations will be closing.
Last week, Joann began its going-out-of-business sales at the roughly 500 stores already set to close. Now, the sales are set to be rolled out across all locations. Gift cards will no longer be available for use, however.
The auction for the final assets of the company came from a trailing downfall for Joann. The retail giant first filed for bankruptcy in March 2024. The craft company then secured around $132 million in new financing to put towards its $1 billion debt. Then, the craft giant restructured into a private company, delisting from the U.S. stock exchange.
Less than a year first filing bankruptcy, in the first two weeks of January this year Joann closed more than eight stores across Iowa, North Carolina, Maryland, Pennsylvania, New York and Massachusetts before filing a second time for Chapter 11 bankruptcy the same month to "facilitate a sale process to maximize the value of its business."

title: See Gene Hackman's star-studded cast of co-stars: Clint Eastwood, Denzel Washington, more
author: Mike Snider
description: Gene Hackman, who was found dead on Feb. 26, along with his deceased wife, shared the screen with an admirable list of co-stars.
content:
In the wake of Gene Hackman's Feb. 26 death, a who's-who of Hollywood have offered tributes to his greatness.
Among them: Clint Eastwood, who directed and co-starred with Hackman in "Unforgiven," said of him in a statement to USA TODAY: "There was no finer actor than Gene. Intense and instinctive. Never a false note. He was also a dear friend whom I will miss very much."
Need more proof of his talent? During a five-decade career, Hackman held his own with a grand gallery of co-stars.
Hackman started early co-starring with Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in 1967's "Bonnie and Clyde" – he got a supporting actor nomination for his role of Buck Barrow – and in 1970, Hackman got another supporting actor nod in "I Never Sang for My Father," which starred Melvyn Douglas.
But he would win a best actor award the following year for perhaps his most famous role and his co-star would get a nomination, too. Here's that combination and some more of Hackman's co-stars.
1971: Roy Scheider in 'The French Connection'
Hackman and Scheider play New York City detectives in the 1971 film, directed by William Friedkin. Hackman who won his first Oscar as best actor for his role as James "Popeye" Doyle; Scheider, in the role of Buddy "Cloudy" Russo, earned a supporting actor nomination. Friedkin, who would go on to direct "The Exorcist," won the Oscar for best director and the film won best picture.
"(Popeye) was a man who was very driven," Hackman told USA TODAY in 2005. He would return as Doyle four years later in the 1975 sequel, "French Connection II."
In "The Poseidon Adventure," one of a slew of '70s blockbuster disaster films, Hackman played a reverend who led fellow passengers/co-stars including Shelley Winters, Ernest Borgnine, Stella Stevens, Red Buttons to the upper reaches of the capsized ship.
Lee Marvin plays a mob enforcer sent to Kansas City to collected a debt from Hackman, whose role is that of a crooked slaughterhouse operator. Also in the film: Sissy Spacek.
1973: Al Pacino in 'Scarecrow'
In "Scarecrow," Hackman's just-released convict, Max, finds a kindred soul in the optimistic sailor Francis (Al Pacino). To prepare for their roles, the actors "literally dressed in old raggedy clothes and hung out on Market Street," in San Francisco, Hackman said.
1974: Robert Duvall and Harrison Ford in 'The Conversation'
The late film critic Roger Ebert in "The Great Movies II," wrote Hackman delivered "one of the key performances of a great career," as a surveillance expert in the Francis Ford Coppola-directed thriller.
Hackman's wiretapper worries that two people he is spying on will be killed. "You see that this compulsion to do this has left him a shallow guy in ways, and troubled. (He's) not a leading man but a character," he told USA TODAY. "Unfortunately, we don't see those anymore."
Also in the film: Duvall, Ford, John Cazale, Teri Garr and Frederic Forrest.
Hackman's Lex Luthor served as the foil for Superman (Christopher Reeve) in three "Superman" films including 1980's "Superman II" and 1987's "Superman IV: The Quest for Peace."
Also in the films: Margot Kidder, Jackie Cooper and Marlon Brando ("Superman II").
Hackman is a middle-aged man who has a fling with a married woman (Streisand).
Also in the film: Dennis Quaid and Diane Ladd.
Hackman, who played a steelworker, and producer/director Bud Yorkin both drew on their real-life recent divorces in this film about a man who separates from his wife (Ellen Burstyn) to live with his new flame (Ann-Margret). "We were two men working closely together, going through that same experience," Hackman told USA TODAY.
Also in the film: Ally Sheedy and Amy Madigan.
A coach with a checkered past (Hackman) leads a small-town Indiana basketball team to the state finals with the help of reformed town drunk played by Dennis Hopper, who got a supporting actor Oscar nod.
Also in the film: Barbara Hershey.
Hackman and Dafoe play FBI agents investigating the disappearance of three civil rights workers. "I remember someone high in the civil rights movement telling me how disappointed they were in the movie that it didn't tell all the truth," said Hackman, who earned a best actor nomination. "I told them that movies are compromises."
Also in the film: Frances McDormand, who was nominated for best supporting actress, and Brad Dourif.
1992: Clint Eastwood, Morgan Freeman in 'Unforgiven'
Hackman as Sheriff "Little Bill" Daggett stands between Eastwood and Freeman, who are out to collect a bounty. The film won the Oscar for best picture.
Also in the film: Morgan Freeman and Richard Harris.
Gene Hackman:
1993: Tom Cruise in 'The Firm'
As the head of a prestigious law firm, Hackman welcomes newcomer Cruise in this film based on a John Grisham bestseller. But Mitch (Cruise) soon learns the firm has a secret client.
Also in the film: Hal Holbrook, Holly Hunter, Ed Harris, Jeanne Tripplehorn, David Strathairn and Gary Busey.
International intrigue leads to a faceoff on a submarine between its captain (Hackman) and new executive officer (Denzel Washington). Also in the film: James Gandolfini and Viggo Mortensen.
1996: Robin Williams in 'The Birdcage'
Gay drag club owner Armand (Robin Williams) and the venue's star Albert (Nathan Lane) are a couple who must play it straight when meeting the family of Armand's son's wife-to-be which includes conservative U.S. senator Hackman. Also in the film: Dianne Wiest, Calista Flockhart, Hank Azaria and Christine Baranski.
1996: Chris O'Donnell in 'The Chamber'
In another film based on a John Grisham novel, O'Donnell is a young attorney seeking to prevent the execution of his grandfather, who is in prison for a past Ku Klux Klan bombing.
Also in the film: Faye Dunaway and Bo Jackson.
1997: Clint Eastwood in 'Absolute Power'
Clint Eastwood directed and starred in this film as a jewel thief who witnesses a murder involving the president (Hackman).
Also in the film: Ed Harris, Laura Linney, Scott Glenn, Dennis Haysbert, Judy Davis, E.G. Marshall and Penny Johnson Jerald.
1998: Will Smith in 'Enemy of the State'
Smith is a lawyer and Hackman is a surveillance expert who unknowingly get embroiled in the coverup of a politically motivated murder. Also in the film: Jon Voight, Regina King, Loren Dean, Jake Busey, Barry Pepper and Gabriel Byrne.
1998: Paul Newman in 'Twilight'
A retired private detective (Newman) is pulled into a long-buried crime by friends played by Gene Hackman and Susan Sarandon. Also in the film: Reese Witherspoon, Stockard Channing, James Garner, Giancarlo Esposito, Liev Schreiber and Margo Martindale.
2000: Keanu Reeves in 'The Replacements'
Hackman is hired to coach a team of replacement pro football players when the starters go on strike. He recruits Reeves as quarterback.
Also in the film: Jon Favreau and Orlando Jones.
2001: Gwyneth Paltrow, Ben Stiller, Danny Glover, more in 'The Royal Tenenbaums'
The patriarch of an dysfunctional family (Hackman) returns hoping to reconcile with his children (played Gwyneth Paltrow, Luke Wilson and Ben Stiller) and wife (Anjelica Huston).
Also in the film: Bill Murray, Danny Glover and Owen Wilson, who also co-wrote the script with director Wes Anderson.
2001: Danny DeVito in 'Heist'
A jewel thief (Hackman) who had planned to go into retirement is forced to complete another job by his fence (DeVito).
Also in the film: Sam Rockwell, Rebecca Pidgeon, Delroy Lindo and Patti LuPone.
2001: Sigourney Weaver in 'Heartbreakers'
Hackman is a rich man who gets caught up in a romantic con game run by a mother and daughter, played by Sigourney Weaver and Jennifer Love Hewitt.
Also in the film: Ray Liotta, Jason Lee, Anne Bancroft, Nora Dunn, Sarah Silverman and Zach Galifianakis.
2003: Dustin Hoffman in 'Runaway Jury'
Dustin Hoffman is a lawyer in a jury trial pitted against a jury consultant (Hackman) who is trying to guide the proceedings in favor of a firearms maker.
Also in the film: John Cusack, Rachel Weisz, Bruce McGill and Jeremy Piven.
2004: Ray Romano in 'Welcome to Mooseport'
Hackman plays the president again, but this time he's a former president running for mayor against hardware store owner Romano.
It was Hackman's last role. "Reality stares you in the face when you get to be my age," he said a year after the film came out. "You are playing the grandfather or the great-grandfather, and you're not used to playing those roles, and although I could, it just doesn't appeal to me."
Also in the film: Maura Tierney, Marcia Gay Harden, Christine Baranski, Fred Savage and Rip Torn.

title: Springfield eatery will allow you to build-your-own charcuterie board
author: Natalie Morris
description: Whether you're at this Springfield business for breakfast or lunch, you can now get some snacks while you're hanging out.
content:
AI-assisted summary
The Wakery in Springfield, Illinois will begin serving a limited food menu on Monday.
The online auction for the former Hooters building in Springfield has been delayed until March 10-12.
Nesty's Burger Joint in Rochester has completed its transformation into Los Chimis Mexican Bar & Grill.
The Wakery is inviting patrons to linger a little longer over their drinks with a new line up of nosh joining the previously liquid only menu.
Nibbles will be joining the downtown business's offerings Monday.
'I'm not aiming to be a full restaurant but want to provide more snack options that make it conducive to staying a little longer,' operator Elizabeth Wake said. 'This has always been a part of the original business plan. We just wanted to phase things in.'
The business began as an alternative to the downtown bar scene in 2023, serving non-alcoholic cocktails at the 5 W. Old State Capitol Plaza. Caffeinated beverages joined soon after.
New breakfast selections feature a variety of pastries, avocado toast, overnight oats and smoothie bowls. Afternoon selections include a daily soup, build-your-own charcuterie board, baked brie and spinach-artichoke dip.
Hours are 7 to 11 a.m. and 4 to 10 p.m. weekdays. Dine in and take out available. Mobile ordering will be added in the near future.
Hooters sale delayed
The shuttered Hooters building on Springfield's east side will be on the market a little longer, thanks to the recent cold snap.
The online auction for the property at 4321 Horizon Drive – originally set to wrap up Feb. 26 – has been rescheduled for March 10-12.
'Due to weather, our interior photos and videos were delayed, as well as the clean out of the interior to allow for tours,' Michael Kaplan, vice president for SRS Real Estate Partners, wrote in an email. The Dallas-based commercial real estate advisory firm is overseeing the auction.
'So, we pushed the date back to ensure out-of-state buyers could see the interior of the space prior to the auction period.'
The 4,262-square-foot building has been vacant since June, one of roughly 40 locations the Atlanta-based restaurant chain shuttered throughout the country at the time.
A Hooters spokesman cited 'current market conditions' as the cause for closing 'a select number of underperforming stores.'
The starting bid remains set at $190,000.
Rebrand complete
The rebranding of Nesty's Burger Joint to Los Chimis Mexican Bar & Grill in Rochester is complete.
Operators Nestor and Megan Lopez are still behind the dining establishment at 312 Sattley St. in Rochester, swapping its extensive burger selection for a traditional, full-service Mexican restaurant.
More: Springfield-area burger bar rebranding. Here's what we know
There are no plans for a similar rebranding at the original Nesty's Burger Joint in Taylorville.
Los Chimis' menu features an extensive menu of Mexican cuisine standards, ranging from quesadillas to fajitas, nachos to enchiladas. Birra – stewed meat in a spicy sauce – can be ordered stuffed in tacos and quesadillas or atop ramen. Vegetarian offerings available.
And for the gringos, Nesty's classic smash burger is still on the menu, as well as a traditional horseshoe and a slimmed down variety of the non-boozy milkshakes.
Operating hours are 4 to 9 p.m. Monday through Wednesday, 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Thursday, 11 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday and 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Sunday. Phone: 217/498-1008. Dine in, take out available.
St Patrick's Day parade is preparing to roll through downtown Springfield March 15 while the official day falls on March 17. A la Carte will run a list of local St. Patrick's culinary specials March 9. Deadline to submit information is March 3.

title: Seeing double: Bard, Folkes give Illini Central top-tier deep-shooting threat
author: Ryan Mahan
description: When David Bard and Brody Folkes are on fire, Illini Central fans are in for quite a show, and opponents are likely in for a headache.
content:
When Mason City Illini Central senior David Bard is in the zone, the Cougars have a chance at winning.
When Illini Central junior Brody Folkes' shots are on target, the Cougars also have a winning chance.
When the two of them are on fire, coach Ryan Burks and the Cougars' fans are in for quite a show, and opponents are likely in for a headache.
The pair of 3-point lethal shooters combine to score 37.7 points per game, both hitting 33% of their shots from outside and Bard, Folkes, Burks and the Cougars are in the Class 1A Brimfield Sectional semifinals, the deepest run for Illini Central since winning the 2013 Class 1A state championship.
'I think early on in the summer, we kind of realized that we were going to be pretty tough to guard with David Bard and Brody Folkes,' Burks said. 'Just both being really good scorers and kind of having the green light. I think our biggest challenge was trying to figure out how to defend and get some of the younger guys to be able to play at the varsity level. Honestly, some of the guys came on a lot quicker than we thought and were able to put us in that position.'
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
No. 3 seed Illini Central (17-16) faces No. 1 Peoria Christian (25-9) in the Class 1A Brimfield Sectional semifinals on Wednesday at 7 p.m.
'This season's been incredible; it's been awesome,' Folkes said. 'We were underrated at the start of the season, weren't supposed to win a championship, that's for sure.
'The whole town, everywhere we go, everyone's just congratulating us. It's been awesome.'
Prolific shooters
Bard leads the Cougars with 19.9 ppg with 78 made 3s (33.9%) and 42.2% shooting overall from the field. Folkes has connected for 102 3s (33.4%) and 37.6% from the field.
Illini Central lost four straight games as the Cougars headed into the Illini Central Regional quarterfinals. In the first game, IC beat Astoria South Fulton 69-39 before a nail-biting 52-51 win over Manito Midwest Central — where Burks graduated from in 2005 — in the semifinals. On Friday, the Cougars beat Mendon Unity, 46-37. Being one of the smallest schools in the Sangamon Conference means IC is facing some of the strongest teams in the state in 2A. The players and coach agree that those regular-season challenges can payoff in the smallest postseason class.
'That was actually my biggest thing with the team all season, was telling them that all these times that we're getting beat by 40, we're getting better,' Bard said on Saturday, minutes after getting off work at a local landscaping company. 'No matter what, we're getting better at something.
'Everything will be easier in regionals coming out of the Sangamon Conference because that's a conference for 2A schools.'
As Bard's career advanced each season, Burks could see Bard, who moved from Ohio in first grade, taking the steps necessary to shoulder the responsibility of driving the team with his talent, shot making and leadership.
Burks saw fearlessness in Bard when Bard was a sixth grader playing up on the seventh and eighth grade teams. He saw a kid who didn't mind taking the ball and letting it fly.
"I'm like, holy smokes, this isn't normal,' Burks said.
Last year, due to a couple of injuries, Bard's role on the team took on a bigger importance.
"He was scoring, going one-on-one and making shots and I thought, 'Man, this is going to be fun next year,' Burks said. 'Watching him all summer and watching how hard he worked. He just did really good, and I knew he's a winner, so, you combine a lot of talent with a kid that just refuses to lose — it's going to be fun to watch.'
Seeing is believing
When Burks arrived to take control of the IC program 2019, he was told there was a fifth grader he needed to check out named Folkes. Fine, Burks thought, but the kid is in elementary school. How good could he be? What Burks saw left him excited for the future.
'I'd go watch and he'd make six 3s as a fifth grader; he's just always been an unbelievable shooter,' Burks said. 'As a freshman, he was able to just hit open shots right away. He's tough to guard because he's kind of taller and lankier and he's left-handed. So that's kind of awkward for people (to guard).
'And he's more kind of calm and collected and just kind of the silent guy. This year, he's had to take on a bigger role, and (Friday) night, he just took over the game and just kept hitting deep 3s.'
Burks describes Folkes as quieter than Bard, but the two players have much more in common than not. They describe the other as great friends and the two not only split the shooting guard and point guard duties, but their chemistry with each other — and their teammates — is superb.
'When we're both going, we're very hard to stop, and we don't like to lose,' Bard said. 'I think our competitiveness takes us a long way.'
Both players would love to play college basketball. Bard said the interest just hasn't come yet, but he remains hopeful.
For now, though, the players are focused on just one thing: Peoria Christian.
'We're just going to go to this game and leave it all on the court, give it all we got,' Folkes said. 'I think an upset ... anything's possible when we're all leaving it out on the court.'

title: Wild Coast Raw recalls frozen cat food due to potential bird flu contamination: See products
author: Greta Cross
description: The recall is for Wild Coast Raw's 16-ounce and 24-ounce frozen Boneless Free Range Chicken Formula raw pet food for cats.
content:
Wild Coast Raw issued a recall on Saturday for "lots" of its frozen Boneless Free Range Chicken Formula, as the raw cat food may have been contaminated with bird flu.
Wild Coast Raw initiated the recall after sampling by the Oregon Department of Agriculture and Washington State Department of Agriculture revealed Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1, commonly known as bird flu, in affected cats and the products, according to the recall.
The recall comes after Wild Coast Raw issued a similar one in February after two cats that ate the brand's cat food grew severely ill of bird flu and died.
Here's what to know about which products are affected and where.
Which products are listed in the recall?
The recall is for Wild Coast Raw's 16-ounce and 24-ounce frozen Boneless Free Range Chicken Formula raw pet food for cats. The product is in a small, round white plastic container with a green label.
The affected lot numbers are #22660, #22653, #22641, #22639, #22672, #22664, #22660 and #22664. The best buy date for the affected products is December 2025.
Where were the products sold?
The recalled products were sold in Washington and Oregon.
What should you do it you have the recalled product?
Do not feed the recalled product to pets or any other animals. Securely discard the product to prevent animals and wildlife from consuming it. Contact your place of purchase for a full refund.
For more information, contact West Coast Raw by email at info@wildcoastraw.com or by phone at 360-591-3543 between 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. PST.
How can bird flu affect cats?
Pet owners who fed their cats the recalled products should watch for the following symptoms:
Fever
Lethargy
Low appetite
Reddened or inflamed eyes
Discharge from the eyes and nose
Difficulty breathing
Neurological signs like tremors, stiff body movements, seizure, lack of coordination or blindness
Owners whose cats exhibit these symptoms, after eating the recalled product, should contact their veterinarian.
Can bird flu be fatal for cats?
Yes. The mortality rate for cats infected with bird flu is 67%, according to the University of Maryland's School of Public Health.
Can bird flu be transmitted from cats to humans?
Though human infections have not been identified among people handling raw pet food products, humans can become infected if the virus gets into their eyes, nose or mouth.
People who have come in contact with the recalled products should wash their hands thoroughly and sanitize all contact surfaces, like countertops, fridges, bowls and utensils.
Common bird flu symptoms in humans include:
Eye redness or irration
Cough
Sore throat
Sneezing
Runny or stuffy nose
Muscle/body aches
Headaches
Fatigue
Fever
Trouble breathing
Seizures
Rash
Diarrehea
Nausea/vomiting
People exhibiting these symptoms, who have been exposed to the recalled products, should contact their healthcare provider and local health department.

title: Group of Taylorville radio stations will stay in local hands with sale. What we know
author: Steven Spearie
description: Randy Miller of the Miller Media Group is expected to be retained for the next year.
content:
The sale to Hart Media Group includes WTIM AM-FM.
The sale is subject to approval by the FCC.
In all, the sale includes eight radio stations, three online platforms and a digital division.
The Taylorville-based Miller Media Group is selling all of its assets, including WTIM AM-FM and two online daily newspapers, to a Rochester media group.
Matt Hart, who owns Hart Media Group, LLC, is a Taylorville native and was a former part-time announcer on WTIM in the 1990s, according to a news release.
The deal is subject to approval by the Federal Communications Commission.
Terms of the deal were not announced.
In all, MMG owns eight radio stations, three online platforms and a digital division.
WTIM is a popular sports talk station that is affiliated with CBS Sports Radio.
It carries local high sports and is part of the St. Louis Cardinals Radio and Fighting Illini Sports networks.
The station, which will mark its 75th anniversary in 2027, concentrates on local news and agriculture news.
MMG's Miller Communications division has owned the six Taylorville radio stations, and its online daily newspaper, taylorvilledailynews.com, since 1992, while its Kaskaskia Broadcasting division has owned the two Clinton radio stations, and its online daily newspaper, dewittdailynews.com, since 2008.
According to the release, Hart will retain Miller for a year during the transition.
Hart said that MMG has done "an amazing job of serving local communities in central Illinois for decades. Hart Media Group is excited to have the opportunity to continue to connect people, and to serving these local communities with local media."
The new ownership expected to take over sometime this summer.

title: Williamsville returns to Class 2A sectional finals with defensive clinic against Staunton
author: Bill Welt
description: The Williamsville boys basketball team vexed Staunton with the 1-3-1 to return to the 2A sectional final against Auburn
content:
GREENVILLE — The Williamsville boys basketball team summoned the 1-3-1 defense to devastating effect — perhaps not unlike Auburn the previous night.
The Bullets raced to a 21-0 lead behind a gamut of turnovers and 3s and never eased up in a 57-35 running-clock victory over Staunton in the Class 2A Greenville Sectional semifinal on Wednesday.
Williamsville (30-3) will vie for its second straight sectional title against fellow Sangamo Conference foe Auburn (30-4) on Friday at 7 p.m. The Trojans defeated Pleasant Plains 50-39 on Tuesday also using the 1-3-1.
"We were getting steals and forcing turnovers," Williamsville senior guard Carson Doran said. "That just led to offense and good shots for us."
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
Staunton (28-5) turned the ball over on its first seven possessions and wound up with 12 by the end of the first quarter for a 23-3 deficit. Williamsville also converted 11 of its 12 3s in the first half for a 46-14 halftime advantage.
Doran certainly contributed to the early onslaught not only at the point defensively, but he also scored 14 of his game-high 17 points before the break.
"We haven't played it a lot this year, but we pulled it out and it really helps us speed the game up, speed them up and lead to points for us on the other end," Doran said of the 1-3-1.
Senior guards Blake Shoufler and Brayden Saling delivered 13 and nine points, respectively. Senior forward Reid Bodine added eight points, while junior guard Garrett Timm had two 3s for six points. Doran, Shoufler and Saling poured in three 3s apiece.
"It started yesterday," Williamsville coach Nick Beard said of the team's hot shooting. "We had the best practice of the year and shot the heck out of it in practice. I was so confident coming into tonight that we were going to shoot the ball well because guys got in the gym after Friday night (against Quincy Notre Dame) and weren't content."
The Bulldogs were making their first sectional appearance since 2009 with just two seniors on the roster. Senior Ethan Sharp led Staunton with 14 points and eight rebounds.
"All the years I've been coaching, I've never coached a kid like that," Staunton coach Ty Laux said of Sharp. "Just every single play he gives you everything he has. We can't replace him, you can't. It's going to have to be a team effort and hopefully our kids saw how he played and learn from him.
"You could not take Ethan Sharp off the floor this year, he was at times our absolute best player and just shows if you really outwork everybody what kind of impact you can have. He had a major impact this year."
PEORIA CHRISTIAN 61, MASON CITY ILLINI CENTRAL 30: David Bard led the Cougars with 14 points, while Brody Folkes had 11 in the Class 1A Brimfield Sectional semifinal loss.
Trae Brickner ushered 21 points, while Malachi Persinger had 18 for Peoria Christian. The Cougars finished 17-17 overall.

title: Here's what to know about Ash Wednesday, Lent season
author: Steven Spearie
description: Christians will get one last nibble on their paczkis and king cakes as Mardi Gras and the Carnival Season give way to Ash Wednesday this week.
content:
Lent is a penitential season in the church year leading up to Good Friday and Easter.
Ashes, usually placed on the forehead as a sign of penitence, come from burned palm fronds
Christians will get one last nibble on their paczkis and king cakes as Mardi Gras and the Carnival Season give way to Ash Wednesday this week.
Many Catholics and Episcopalians and some in Protestant denominations, including Lutherans, Methodists and Presbyterians, will mark the beginning of Lent with the receiving of ashes, usually on the forehead in the shape of a cross.
Ashes, which typically come from burned Palm Sunday fronds, are a sign of penitence and a reminder of mortality.
Lent is the principal penitential season in the church year leading up to commemorations of Christ's crucifixion and resurrection.
Orthodox Christians and Eastern Rite Catholics began Lent with Clean Monday. This year, Easter, or Pascha, is celebrated in both the Western and Eastern churches on April 20.
During Lent, Christians are urged to develop and maintain a voluntary program of self-denial, serious prayer and the performing of deeds of charity and mercy, including the giving of alms.
Catholics between the ages of 18 years and 59 are required to fast on Ash Wednesday and Good Friday (April 18). Only one full meatless meal is permitted. Two other meatless meals, sufficient to maintain strength may be taken according to each person's needs, but together these two should not equal another full meal. Eating between meals isn't permitted, but liquids are allowed.
Pope's Lenten message
In his Lenten message, an ailing Pope Francis said that humans are "pilgrims in this life" and that that journey that bears critical reflection.
'Am I really on a journey," he said, "or am I standing still, not moving, either immobilized by fear and hopelessness or reluctant to move out of my comfort zone?'
The focus of the Lenten journey, he added, is "toward the victory of Easter.'
The text was released Tuesday but dated Feb. 6, about a week before he was hospitalized in Rome with a complex respiratory infection and pneumonia.
The pope experienced "two acute respiratory crises" on Monday and was placed back on a ventilator.

title: Six students arrested following separate fights at Lanphier High School
author: Steven Spearie
description: Police officials told The State Journal-Register six students were arrested after separate fights broke out Wednesday afternoon. Here's what we know.
content:
Six students were arrested following two separate fights at Lanphier High School, 1300 N. 11th St., around 12:50 p.m. Wednesday.
Responding officers, said Commander Sara Pickford of the Springfield Police Department, were directed to the high school's atrium once they were on the scene.
The atrium is in the middle of the school and is a connector for students to take to get to different parts of the building, said School District 186 spokeswoman Rachel Dyas.
Lanphier security and administrators initially responded to two students engaged in a fight in the atrium.
While they were able to stop that altercation, four other students came up on the scene and became involved in a separate fight, Dyas said. Those students also were eventually separated.
Dyas confirmed that two school administrators were taken off the campus for medical evaluation. She did not say where they were taken.
Pickford confirmed that two ambulances were requested at the scene.
All six students were taken to police headquarters, where they were processed and then taken to the Sangamon County Juvenile Detention Center because of meeting system points, Pickford said.
Dyas said Lanphier faculty and staff and families were notified of the fight.
"Fighting and aggressive behavior are not acceptable and do not align with our values of respect, responsibility, and kindness," Lanphier principal Alicia Miller wrote in an email, which was provided to The State Journal-Register. "This type of behavior will not be tolerated.
"Our staff and students need to come to school without worry of injury or chaos caused due to reckless behavior."

title: Dana-Thomas house partnering with women overcoming substances for Women's History Month
author: Claire Grant
description: This Women's History Month, a local historical site is partnering with a program helping women get back on their feet.
content:
AI-assisted summary
The Dana-Thomas House State Historic Site in Springfield, Illinois is partnering with Wooden It Be Lovely, a local non-profit, for Women's History Month.
Wooden It Be Lovely provides transitional employment, housing and support services to women recovering from poverty, addiction and abuse.
This Women's History Month, a local historical site is partnering with a program helping women get back on their feet.
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources, which operates and preserves the Dana-Thomas house State Historic Site at 301 E. Lawrence Ave., is celebrating the month with Wooden It Be Lovely to exhibit six refurbished chairs at the site.
The chairs were hand-painted by the women at Wooden It Be Lovely, which offers transitional employment, housing and support to women healing from poverty, addiction and abuse.
The organization also offers jobs, mentoring, recovery tools, education, networking and a safe community.
The chairs will available for purchase at the Wooden It Be Lovely's spring furniture showcase in April.
'Wooden It Be Lovely is so honored to be invited to show some of our work at the Dana-Thomas House,' said the Rev. Margaret Ann Jessup, executive director of Wooden It Be Lovely. 'The women who painted the chairs feel so proud that their work will be recognized by the public. They have been telling everyone they know how excited they are. It's so empowering to them to be honored in this way. I believe this is something that these women will never forget.'
The women in the program are employed to refurbish and sell donated wooden furniture, sew unique products and craft hand-poured candles.
Wooden It Be Lovely said this transitional employment empowers women to move toward economic stability and enhanced well-being for themselves and their children.

title: Williamsville boys basketball bows out to Peoria Manual in 2A supersectional

description: Williamsville's historic season comes to end against Peoria Manual in Class 2A boys basketball supersectional
content:
Peoria Manual raced to a 20-0 lead en route to a 52-29 victory over Williamsville and its first state berth since 2019 in the Class 3A supersectional at the Bank of Springfield Center on Monday.
The Bullets (31-4) didn't convert their first field goal until Carson Doran's 3 with 5 minutes, 10 seconds left in the second quarter. Williamsville trailed 32-9 at halftime.
Senior guard Dietrich Richardson, who is committed to Bradley University, led the Rams with 18 points.
"Words can't even explain it," Richardson said. "My first time getting there, so it means a lot. All of the hard work we've been putting in is paying off and the job's still not done yet."
Williamsville, which took fourth place at last year's 2A state finals, summoned its most wins in school history and achieved its first repeat sectional title. Senior guard Carson Doran generated 11 points, while senior teammate Blake Shoufler had 10.
"That's what I told them in there ... the impact they've had on this community and this program — it's generational," Williamsville coach Nick Beard said, "I've got a six-year-old at home who lives for Bullet basketball and these kids are pretty good basketball players, but they're better human beings and they're going to be really successful in life."
