title: 'People are feeling galvanized': Anti-Trump protesters rally in cities across US
author: John Bacon
description: The protests by the 50501 Movement come days after rallies in opposition of Trump's immigration policies were held across the country.
content:
WASHINGTON − Groups opposed to actions by the Trump administration in recent weeks converged on cities Wednesday across the U.S. to loudly register their discontent.
The protests came days after widespread rallies and street marches against President Donald Trump's immigration policies that have led to sweeping ICE raids.
In the nation's capital two protests near the U.S. Capitol drew hundreds bearing signs and thunderous voices. The protesters marched from streets around the Capitol to the Department of Labor building on Constitution Avenue − where Elon Musk's DOGE officials were visiting for the day. Musk, a staunch Trump ally, has been executing Trump's cost-cutting initiative to reduce the size of the U.S. government.
Cars passing by the marchers honked in a show of support.
Earlier in the day a crowd several hundred deep gathered outside the Capitol for a demonstration against Trump's efforts to diminish the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID). Rallygoers bundled up in puffy winter coats, hats and gloves held up signs against Trump.
'Don't let democracy die,' 'Elon cheats on video games,'' 'Checks and balances make America great,' some of the signs read. Demonstrators also chanted at Democratic lawmakers who spoke at the rally, telling them, 'Do your job!'
Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine said Democrats plan to fight the changes in court, in state legislatures and in Congress. Fellow Virginia Sen. Mark Warner urged protesters to take their concerns to GOP lawmakers as well.
"Don't just show up here," Warner said. "We are only going to break this when we have Republicans willing to stand up as well. Put the pressure not just on us but on everyone, every elected official."
Trump has signed a flurry of executive orders and taken other actions since his Jan. 20 inauguration to remake and reduce the size of America's 2.2 million-strong federal workforce. Diversity programs have been targeted; government web pages have been scrubbed of gender references.
Developments:
∎ New Yorkers protested outside the Midtown Manhattan office of Sen. Charles Schumer, carrying signs such as "It's a coup, where R you?" and "Chuck, show us pluck."
∎ Protesters in Chicago were to rally in Daley Plaza and lobby Democratic Sens. Tammy Duckworth and Dick Durbin of Illinois to block Trump's efforts.
Musk the target of ire from Austin protesters
Many of Musk's fellow residents of Austin, Texas, vociferously expressed their disapproval of the multibillionaire at a protest Wednesday in front of the state Capitol and in a march through downtown Austin.
Thousands participated in the demonstration against Trump's attempts at remaking the federal government and the country's immigration system, and a large number of them took aim at Musk and his associates at the Department of Government Efficiency.
The clamor from the rally could be heard from inside Capitol offices and the Senate chamber as protesters chanted, "No more Musk, stop the coup," "Reclaim our county, take back our rights," "All are welcome here."
Musk has brought numerous jobs to Texas by moving the headquarters of some of his businesses to the state, including Tesla and SpaceX, but his work in reshaping sections of the government has drawn strong backlash.
"Elon Musk has your number,'' said one sign, a reference to DOGE gaining access to federal employee data.
From NC to DC, one protester vows to 'be the Tiananmen tank guy'
Stewart Rabitz, 70, drove up from his home in Wake Forest, North Carolina, early Wednesday to attend the protest outside the U.S. Capitol. Rabitz isn't new to the anti-Trump protest circuit − he's been hitting the streets since the early days of Trump's first term and said he's faced off against the Proud Boys.
This time feels different, Rabitz said, because of the quick pace of Trump's executive orders. The sentiment among the opposition to Trump has also changed.
'I think a lot of people are now realizing that walking around with signs, people got to get their hands dirty,' he said.Asked about whether he feared retribution, Rabitz said: 'You can't be afraid. I'm willing to be the first one. I'll be the Tiananmen tank guy.'
Protests planned in every state
The 50501 Movement − 50 states, 50 protests, one day − planned demonstrations "supporting the free expression of regular Americans' dissatisfaction with the embrace of Project 2025."
Project 2025 is a lengthy list of proposals that would expand presidential power and impose an ultra-conservative social vision. Protest organizers say Project 2025 seeks to target marginalized groups, heighten surveillance, restrict reproductive rights and slash funding for crucial services such as education and health care while dismantling "the freedoms we cherish."
The 50501 group is also opposed to Trump's executive orders such as cracking down on illegal immigration and pardoning people involved in the Jan. 6, 2021, riot at the U.S. Capitol.
Columbus protesters take aim at Trump, Musk
Trump's policies and Musk's government-slashing efforts were at the heart of a demonstration that drew hundreds Wednesday to the Ohio Statehouse in Columbus, the Columbus Dispatch reported.
Protesters carried signs with messages like, "Worst. President. Ever'' and "I want my privacy back − arrest Elon Musk!''
Several of Trump's initial executive actions zeroed in on immigrants, as he revoked Temporary Protected Status for more than 300,000 Venezuelans and sought to end birthright citizenship.
"As a refugee to this country, naturalized, I recognize how lucky I am to have that security," Katja Ryabtseva, who hails from Azerbaijan, told the newspaper. "I can't sit at home knowing that there are families, children out there trying to get documentation again and are going to be kicked out."
− Donovan Hunt, Columbus Dispatch
Lawyer, nurse among those taking time off work to protest
Several attendees took off work to attend the USAID and 50501 rallies that converged outside the Capitol.
Ravenna Romack, a lawyer and military spouse, said she protested on the Capitol steps every day this week. Romack, 40, said she's most concerned about Musk's growing power in the federal government and his team circumventing Congress.
'People are feeling galvanized right now because it's become personal,' said Romack, who saw Wednesday's protest as a continuation of the resistance movement against Trump that has existed for years.
Nathan Alexander, a 32-year-old military veteran, stood at the edge of the crowd with a cart filled with first aid materials, water, granola bars, hand warmers and flask masks. Alexander said he works as a nurse at a hospital in Maryland but opted Wednesday to provide emergency service to anyone who needed it at the rally. He said he paid for all the supplies with his own money.
'That's how important it is to me to make sure that everybody knows … we're all in this together,' said Alexander, who was wearing a rainbow pin. 'Rising tides raise all ships.''
AFL-CIO rallies against Musk labor actions
One of the nation's largest labor unions, the AFL-CIO, rallied Wednesday at the Department of Labor in Washington, D.C., concerned Musk and his team may target the department next.
Users shared posts about the rally on social media, including on the Reddit section where Wednesday demonstrations across the nation were organized.
"Working people deserve a STRONG Department of Labor that works for them, NOT for billionaires and corporate CEOs,'' the AFL-CIO said in a post on the X platform, which Musk owns.
Among the speakers at the rally were AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler; Massachusetts Sen. Ed Markey, a Democrat; and Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton, a Democrat who represents D.C.
"This is where the movement begins, this is where the fight begins," Markey said.
'Deport Elon': Signs, Mexican flags at Denver rally
Several hundred people demonstrated outside the Colorado Capitol building in downtown Denver on Wednesday afternoon, some waving Mexican flags, according to local media reports.
One person held a sign that said "Deport Elon" in reference to Musk, a native of South Africa who is leading Trump's efforts to slash the size of the federal government. Another carried a sign reading "We are all immigrants."
Trump has targeted the Denver suburb of Aurora, saying it has been taken over by Venezuelan gangs.
− Trevor Hughes

title: How much will a Super Bowl spread cost in Springfield? We have you covered
author: Claire Grant
description: If you plan on hosting a Super Bowl party this weekend, there's a very good chance you're paying more than previous years.
content:
AI-assisted summary
Hosting a Super Bowl party in 2025 is slightly more expensive than in previous years due to inflation.
A Super Bowl spread for 10 people, including essentials like chicken wings, beer, and chips, is estimated to cost around $139, according to the Wells Fargo Agri-Food Institute.
If you plan on hosting a Super Bowl party this weekend, there's a very good chance you're paying more than previous years.
According to the Consumer Price Index, inflation rose nearly three percent from December 2023 to December 2024.
What's that mean if you're hosting a party this weekend?
The State-Journal Register took a trip to the County Market to get a gauge for how much hosting a party for the big game would cost you in town.
Methodology
The reporter visited County Market on Monroe Jan. 31, 2025. The dishes were chosen based on popularity at Super Bowl tables and were purchased with the assumption butter and spices were already in the pantry.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
City, grocery and state tax was applied to the total to create overall cost.
Chicken used in the buffalo wings category was three pounds frozen for savings. A 24-piece of fresh fried chicken with four pounds of sides will set back parties $49.99 before tax.
Jalapeno Poppers
At County Market, jalapeno peppers are $2.99 per pound and are a product of Mexico. Splitting and stuffing the peppers with one container of Philadelphia cream cheese at $3.80 per block, 12 ounces of Seitz applewood bacon will set your wallet back $5.79.
Total: $12.58 before tax.
Buffalo Chicken Dip
A 1.31 pound of pre-cooked, pre-pulled fresh chicken breast is $13.08 at County Market. Using the other Philly cream cheese block at $3.80 per block, one bottle of Bolthouse classic ranch is $4.99 – save a little for later to dip your veggies in!
Finally, mix in the Franks RedHot hot sauce for $6.29 to get that spicey tang with the ranch. A bag of chips for dipping settles around $2 at County Market.
Total: $30.16 before tax.
This one is pretty simple and really depends on what flavor you want for your table. Going with the most popular flavor for gameday: buffalo, a three-pound pack of TenderBird boneless chicken wings is $13.99.
Total: $13.99 before tax.
Vegetable Platter
One pint of La familia tomatoes, produced in Mexico, retail for $2.29. Wild Harvest organic celery hearts are $5.99 for one pound, while organic baby carrots are $2.69 per pound. Consumers already bought one bottle of ranch, so we aren't buying another here.
Burger Sliders
A twelve-count of Aunt Millie's Hawaiian rolls cost $3.99. 80% lean, 20% fat ground beef is $2.99 per pound. For this recipe, we will be using two pounds. Eight ounces of Dutch Farms Monterey Jack cheese will go on top, for $2.90.
Total: $12.87 before taxes – without all the fixings.
American as apple pie
A fresh made nine-inch lattice cherry or apple pie will finish the full meal spread for only $13.99 per pie.
Total: $13.99 before tax.
Total before tax: $94.56
With 10.75% sales tax: $104.73
How does this spread fare nationwide?
In a report released by the Wells Fargo Agri-Food Institute, a Super Bowl party for a group of 10 people including some key essentials like chicken wings, beer and chips will cost about $139, which is just 10 cents more than last year's prices.
Chicken wings are up 7.2% compared to last year because of high demand and low quantity on the market.
For the Super Bowl this year, alcoholic beverages like beer and wine are 2% more expensive than last year, the Wells Fargo report said.
On the flipside, the increasing popularity of weight loss drugs has led to a higher demand for vegetables. Cherry tomato prices rose 11.9%, the report found. Avocado prices rose 11.5%, peppers rose 7.4% and the price of carrots rose 3.4%, said the Wells Fargo report.

title: Springfield bar caught selling alcohol to underaged people for third time
author: Claire Grant
description: Five Sangamon County business sold alcohol people who were underage in January—including a bar which has been caught doing so for a third time.
content:
Show Caption
Five Sangamon County businesses sold alcohol to people who were underage in January, including a bar which has been caught doing so for a third time.
A total of 23 locations were tested on Jan. 29. During the testing, eight prior violations were re-tested after having previous violations.
The compliance checks, conducted by the Illinois Liquor Control Commission, enlisted high school and college students under the Illinois drinking age of 21 to visit bars and establishments across the country and order drinks to confirm if the location was in compliance with state law against selling alcohol to underage people.
What is Illinois Liquor Law?
The Liquor Control Act prohibits the sale of alcohol to anyone under 21 with businesses in violation charged with Class A misdemeanor and can be fined $500 suspension, or revocation of their liquor license.
What businesses sold alcohol to underage people?
Save-A-Lot, 2520 E. Clear Lake Ave., Springfield
Stoney's Gaming LLC, 501 N. Dirksen Pkwy., Springfield
Silver 777 Gaming Parlor, 718 N. Dirksen Pkwy., Springfield
Main Gate Bar & Grill, 2143 N. 11th St., Springfield (1 prior violation)
Crows Mill Pub, 1220 Toronto Rd., Springfield (2 prior violations)
Crows Mill failed previous compliance checks in 2014 and 2017, and most recently in a July inspection last year, making it a recurring location on the list.
Multiple businesses, including 709 Cut Rate Package Liquors, Miss Kimmees, The Winner's Circle, Taqueria El Dorado, Jaalsa and Lucy's Place IV, all passed compliance checks in January after having previous violations.
About the Illinois Liquor Control Commission
The Illinois Liquor Control Commission releases the results of underage compliance check operations throughout the state. Additionally, monthly summary reports are published that compile information from all details conducted in that month.
These operations are conducted in all regions of the state. Establishments that fail an underage compliance check and are cited for selling alcohol to minors.

title: Restaurant selling 'Illinois Hot Chicken' is opening first Springfield location
author: Claire Grant
description: The restaurant, which is known for selling "Illinois Hot Chicken", already has locations in Bloomington and Peoria.
content:
If you've been looking for some hot chicken, you may be interested in this new restaurant coming to Springfield.
Pop-Up Chicken Shop, a Bloomington-based fried chicken restaurant known for its "Illinois Hot Chicken", announced the restaurant is opening its first Springfield location in May.
Business owner Aaron Francis started the restaurant in 2018 and has since expanded the business model through simple menus.
The menu ranges from chicken sandwiches to wings and whole buckets. The menu also offers the classic Springfield horseshoe sandwich with dill pickle fries, smoked gouda chipotle cheese and two chicken tenders atop Texas toast.
Simplifying menus has been a growing trend for fast food businesses; cutting costs on stocking fridges with hundreds of ingredients, businesses are instead buying bulk in staple goods and streamlining operations for kitchen efficiency.
Raising Canes, which popularized the simple menu, offers chicken finger bundles with coleslaw, toast, and fries with a side of sauce. For the first half of 2024, Raising Cane's boosted revenues by 33% year over year to $2.3 billion and that upward swing is continuing to climb.
Prices at Pop-Up chicken range from $4 for drumsticks to $49 for a bucket and several sides, with meals pretty equal in price to Raising Canes, but offering cheaper a la carte options.
Pop-Up chicken in Bloomington opened in 2018, while the second location in Peoria opened in 2024.
The restaurant was featured last fall on America's Best Restaurants.

title: Former chamber of commerce CEO in central Illinois pleads guilty to theft
author: Tom Ackerman
description: The former CEO of the chamber of commerce has pleaded guilty after she was arrested for allegedly stealing between $100,000 and $500,000.
content:
The former CEO of the Taylorville Chamber of Commerce has pleaded guilty after she was arrested in 2023 for allegedly stealing between $100,000 and $500,000 from the organization over multiple years.
Patty A. Hornbuckle pleaded guilty last week to the charge of theft, which is a felony.
Hornbuckle, who was 63 years old at the time of her arrest, was sentenced to first offender second chance probation with 24 months.
Second chance probation is a sentence in Illinois that allows certain offenders to clear a conviction from their record after serving at least two years of probation.
The Taylorville Police Department previously said that they had been contacted by the Chamber several months prior to the arrest regarding the allegations of misconduct and theft against Hornbuckle.
During meetings with the Chamber's employees, they learned that her resignation in 2021 came after she had been questioned by members regarding the alleged misconduct.
The police department had opened an investigation and worked through the allegations until the Christian County Circuit Court found enough probable cause for an arrest warrant against Hornbuckle.
She was arrested and held in the Christian County Jail while detectives conducted a search of her home. She was released after paying a $10,000 bond.

title: Trump expected to pardon former Illinois Gov. Blagojevich, report says
author: Tom Ackerman
description: President Trump commuted the former Illinois governor's sentence back in 2020 after he had served 8 years of a 14-year sentence.
content:
President Donald Trump will pardon Democratic former Illinois Gov. Rod Blagojevich, according to the Associated Press.
The pardon is expected to be signed on Monday, according to the report.
President Trump in 2020 commuted Blagojevich's sentence after he had served eight years of his 14-year sentence.
While a pardon does not signify innocence, it removes civil disabilities such as restrictions on the right to vote, hold state or local office, or sit on a jury – imposed because of the conviction for which pardon is sought, and "should lessen the stigma arising from the conviction," according to the U.S. Department of Justice.
Politico reported President Trump is considering nominating the former governor to serve as the U.S. ambassador to Serbia.
The former governor gave support to the president during a visit to Mar-a-Lago last spring.
Blagojevich served as governor from 2003 through 2009 when he was impeached and ultimately removed for corruption from office by the Illinois General Assembly. His removal from office was prompted by two dozen charges including extorting a children's hospital for campaign funds and attempting to sell then-President-Elect Barack Obama's U.S. Senate seat.

title: Presidents Day is Monday. Here's what's open and closed in the Springfield area
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Remembering what's open and closed on Presidents Day and Lincoln's birthday can get confusing. Here's what's open in Sangamon County.
content:
Remembering what's open and closed on Presidents Day and Lincoln's birthday can get confusing.
Lincoln's birthday is Feb 12. Presidents Day is this Feb. 17, which was originally meant to celebrate the first U.S. President George Washington's birthday.
Here's what's open and closed on Presidents Day in Sangamon County.
What's closed on Presidents Day?
Presidents Day is a federal holiday, so federal buildings and courts will be closed, and there is no U.S. Postal delivery. Most banks are closed.
Federal offices and courts, State of Illinois offices and courts, and Sangamon County offices and courts are all closed in observance of the holiday.
School District 186 schools and offices are closed. The board of education meeting has been moved to 6:30 p.m. on Feb. 18. The board meets at 3063 Fiat Ave. in Springfield.
Ball-Chatham, Rochester and Lincoln public schools are also out of session.
There are no classes at Midwest Technical Institute on Presidents Day in Springfield.
What's open for Presidents Day?
City of Springfield administrative offices will be open. The Lincoln Library will also be open.
Colleges
The University of Illinois Springfield, Lincoln Land Community College, Illinois College and Blackburn College are all open and are in session for Presidents Day.
Transportation
Sangamon Mass Transit District buses will run regular schedules.

title: Popular fall festival won't be returning to Springfield after 14 years
author: Natalie Morris
description: An annual fall festival won't be returning to Springfield after 14 years. Meanwhile, two women-owned eateries have opened in the area.
content:
Organizers of the Springfield Oyster & Beer Festival announced last week that the annual fall event has been retired after 14 years.
'It is with mixed emotions the SOB Committee announces that the annual festival will not take place in 2025,' according to a press release issued Feb. 8 by Conn Family Community Works, a branch of Conn's Hospitality Group Inc.
'After 14 years of unforgettable memories, camaraderie and charity, we have made the difficult decision to retire this beloved event. Rising costs, increased oversight regulations and limited time to dedicate to the organization of the festival have contributed to this decision.'
The outdoor festival held at the Inn at 835 combined live music, craft beer and oyster dishes with all proceeds going to local charities.
Women-owned eateries open
Two locally based, women-owned eateries opened their doors this week.
In both cases, these new brick-and-mortar locations represent new milestones for the women owner/operators who already have an established track record in Springfield's dining scene.
My Harvest Kitchen + Bar filled the vacancy left by Sweet Basil Cafe at 4241 Conestoga Drive Monday. Mother-daughter team Vivian Dominguez and Odette Yobal are behind the new establishment serving up fresh American classics.
And Golden Hour Bake House officially opened its doors to the public at 11 W. Old State Capitol Plaza Feb. 8 after operating curbside service only from the downtown address since last fall. Sole owner Alli Donaldson was a recent Isringhausen DRIVE grant recipient.
'It's been a long time coming,' said Donaldson, who has been sharing her baking skills from online sales and a booth at the Old Capitol Farmers Market for years.
'A really long time coming. But we are really just so excited to be open.'
Of course, the menu highlights Donaldson's renowned cake donuts and other pastries, many available in gluten-free varieties. But the new address has allowed her to expand into breakfast and soon-to-be added lunch and beverage offerings.
Breakfast selections are elevated with unexpected twists and house-made specialties like the salted peanut butter, strawberry-basil jam and lime crema. The menu features signature and build-your-own breakfast sandwiches, specialty toasts and biscuits and gravy, as well as a fruit smoothie and quiche of the day.
Dine in and to go service is available, however the curbside service has been halted for now.
Posted operating hours are 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. Wednesday through Friday and 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. weekends. Phone: 217-717-1137.
My Harvest Kitchen + Bar is a departure for Dominguez, who owns La Fiesta Chatham in Piper Glen with her husband.
The Prairie Crossing establishment is serving up a fresh take on classic American diner fare. Regular operating hours are 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily. Phone: 217-717-1978.
Former businesses demolished
Two long-standing Springfield dining sites have been torn down.
Building permits to demolish structures at 700 W. Jefferson St., mostly recently home to Sgt. Pepper's Cafe, and 1325 S. MacArthur Blvd., were recently filed with the Springfield Building and Zoning Department.
The MacArthur property was home to a string of dining establishments operating from the mid-1970s to the mid-1990s. The Chinese restaurant Lichee Garden called the single-story brown wooden structure home from 1985 until relocating to Chatham Road in 1994.
But a franchise operator for the Los Angeles-based chain Sir George's Royal Buffet first constructed the building in 1974. The buffet – which advertised repeat trips to the salad bar – cost $1.85 for lunch and $2.75 for dinner when it opened. Sir George's was followed by two locally owned establishments: The Ranch House steakhouse and Orchid Inn Chinese restaurant.
It is unknown what might be next for the property near the intersection of MacArthur Boulevard and South Grand Avenue. Standard Investment Co. – listed as the property owner on the building permit – could not be reached.
Fire gutted the home to Sgt. Pepper's Cafe on Jefferson Street over a year ago, just shy of this spin-off location's first anniversary.
Muhammad Samara – whose parents own the original Sgt. Pepper's Cafe at 3141 Baker Drive – said he no longer owns the property. The building permit listed Specialty Risk of America as the owner.
The building was home to Ritz's Lil' Fryer, Christina's Subs & More, Rocky Rococo's Pan-Style Pizza and the original home to Farmers Market Growise Garden Center, which began as a fresh produce stand in 1980 before relocating to Wabash Avenue.
Subway Daily Special
The Subway Daily Special – a favorite local promotion throughout central Illinois for a decade – is back as a national campaign for the sandwich chain.
'The Daily Special was very popular before it was phased out,' local Subway franchisee Alyssa Furling said. 'We'd get a lot of repeat business on people's favorite special. Now corporate has brought it back as the Meal of the Day nationwide at all participating stores.'
Furling – with Fresh Fit Subs Inc. franchise, one of three franchise operators in the Springfield market – said the Daily Special promo was the brainchild of the advertising board of local Subway franchisees, which disbanded during the pandemic.
The special features the 6-inch sub of the day with a choice of chips and a small fountain drink or two cookies for $6.99.
Featured sandwiches are Monday, cold cut combo; Tuesday, chicken teriyaki; Wednesday, meatball marinara; Thursday, Baja Chipotle chicken; Friday, tuna; Saturday, Ultimate BMT; and Sunday, The Philly.
Restaurant hopes to reopen
A GoFundMe account has been set up for the Chestnut Family Restaurant in Chestnut after the restaurant closed indefinitely due to water damage from a broken pipe Jan. 20.
Owner Cesar Andrade said he hopes to reopen the business he and his wife Rosa have operated for 18 years. But their insurance has yet to approve reconstruction for the building and the restaurant is their family's sole source of income.
'My goal is to try to reopen,' Andrade said. 'Right now I can't make a decision. But for sentimental reasons, for the community we want to stay.'
This isn't the first challenge the Andrades have encountered in the nearly two decades operating in the rural Logan County community. Andrade recalls struggles during the pandemic and when construction on a nearby wind farm closed the most direct route to the village.
'The town, people have always helped us get through this,' he said.

title: Egg prices have climbed amidst an avian flu outbreak. Here's what it means for Illinois
author: Tom Ackerman
description: It's no secret that egg prices have gotten steeper, but what does that mean for Illinois producers and consumers?
content:
Show Caption
Egg prices are expected to increase about 20% in 2025, USA Today reported.
Illinois is not a major producer of eggs, but farmers and state agencies are taking precautions.
Egg prices may not drop until next year.
It's no secret that egg prices have gotten steeper, but what exactly does that mean for Illinois producers and consumers?
Avian flu is the main culprit for the rise in costs nationwide, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The disease is not widespread in Illinois, but the nationwide surge impacts pricing in the state. It also affects the producers who are trying to sell eggs and protect their animals.
Here's what you need to know.
Does Illinois produce a lot of eggs?
Illinois is not among the states that produce the most eggs.
1.883 million eggs were produced in Illinois in 2023, according to the USDA. By comparison, neighboring Iowa produced nearly 13.5 million eggs and Indiana produced 10.6 million eggs in the same year.
Is it safe to eat eggs currently?
Cooking poultry, eggs, and beef to the appropriate internal temperature kills bacteria and viruses, including avian flu viruses, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
How long might we expect to see the high prices?
It's unclear when the cost of eggs may drop, but it could be after 2025, as reported by USA TODAY. That may largely depend on how long it takes farmers and producers to recover their stocks of healthy laying hens.
What is avian flu?
Avian flu is caused by an influenza type A virus that can infect poultry such as chickens, turkeys, pheasants, quail, domestic ducks, geese, and guinea fowl, as well as wild birds (especially waterfowl). Avian flu virus strains are extremely infectious, often fatal to chickens, and can spread rapidly from flock to flock.
Has the bird flu been found in Illinois?
Only a handful of cases of avian flu have been reported in recent months for commercial and backyard flocks in the state. The two largest flocks to get sick were in Lawrence County, with around 41,000 turkeys affected – and in Livingston County – with nearly 41,000 turkeys affected. Those were both reported in December.
The disease appears to currently be most prevalent in Ohio with 48 affected commercial flocks, which means over 9 million birds reportedly got sick within the last 30 days, according to the USDA.
Missouri has seen 13 commercial flocks affected and two backyard flocks, with nearly 4.3 million birds affected.
What is being done to prevent spread in Illinois?
The avian flu has been an ongoing battle facing poultry producers, said Tasha Bunting, who is the Director of Commodity Programs and Farm Systems at the IFB.
No vaccines exist for the virus, but if one was created, it could complicate trade agreements with other countries who buy eggs from the U.S., she said.
Farmers currently rely on measures that aim to decrease the birds' opportunity for exposure to waterfowl or wild birds that are carriers of the disease.
The disease can spread in many ways, whether it be from droppings, from sharing water, or from sharing food. This is true from wild birds to poultry or within a poultry house.
Coordinating agencies are also suggesting producers wash their feed delivery trucks, too, or any trucks that travel from one farm to another.
The virus has affected cows in some places, according to the USDA, though there have not been any dairy outbreaks in Illinois. A Louisiana man died from bird flu in January, which is the first time that has happened in the U.S.
Bird flu has been traveling around the world since 1997. It was largely confined to wild birds until recent years.
What does the disease mean for Illinois' egg producers?
Once the disease enters a bird house, someone needs to euthanize the birds in that system or particular house to prevent further spread because it is a very fast spreading disease, Bunting said.
After, the space is disinfected and will sit idle until there is assurance that the virus is no longer living in the space before the producer can repopulate. That all can take up to six months.
Producers can seek out financial support programs under the federal government that intend to get producers back up to production.
IL Dept. of Agriculture suspends some poultry sales
The Illinois Department of Agriculture imposed a 30-day suspension, starting Feb. 11 on the exhibition or sale of poultry at swap meets, exhibitions, flea markets, and auction markets, in response to ongoing threat of the bird flu.
The move is intended to reduce and prevent the spread of the disease.
'Prevention is our most effective tool to mitigate the spread of avian flu," said Dr. Mark Ernst, IDOA State Veterinarian in the release. "By being proactive in biosecurity and limiting poultry movement and exposure, we are protecting the public as well as the poultry industry."
The department also encouraged poultry flock owners, managers, and veterinarians to report any unusual findings in domestic poultry to IDOA at 217-782-4944, or the U.S. Department of Agriculture at 866-536-7593.

title: Springfield's Hooters slated to have new owner by end of the month
author: Natalie Morris
description: The shuttered Hooters building on Springfield's east side is poised to have a new owner by the end of the month.
content:
AI-assisted summary
The former Hooters building in Springfield, Illinois, is being auctioned online.
The building has been vacant since June 2024 when the restaurant chain closed approximately 40 underperforming locations.
The shuttered Hooters building on Springfield's east side is poised to have a new owner by the end of the month.
Dallas-based SRS Real Estate Partners is orchestrating an online auction sale for the free-standing building at 3241 Horizon Dr., as well as the 1.16 acre lot it sits on and a second neighboring lot, for Feb. 24-26.
'Usually the week before is when we see the heaviest traffic,' said Michael Kaplan, vice president for the commercial real estate advisory firm. 'But we've seen good traffic already.'
The 4,262-square-foot building has been vacant since June – one of roughly 40 locations the Atlanta-based restaurant chain shuttered throughout the country at the time.
A Hooters spokesman cited 'current market conditions' as the cause for closing 'a select number of underperforming stores.'
The brand, known for its chicken wings and buxom wait staff, opened at the address just off South Dirksen Parkway in December 2000.
Kaplan said SRS Real Estate Partners is only handling the sale of the Springfield property, which is owned by a large real estate investment trust.
Sangamon County property records show the building and land is owned by NADG NNN HTRS IL LP, a division of the Florida-based, publicly traded North American Development Group.
The starting bid is set at $190,000. But the real estate is likely to go much higher, considering it rang up a $2.7 million price tag last time it was on the market in 2017, according to property tax records.
New ventures for Springfield businesses
Two familiar names in the Springfield dining scene have announced their intentions of opening new ventures in new spaces.
Tim and Emily Lewis of Three Twigs & Co. fame have announced plans for a new brand in the sole brick-and-mortar site at The Railyard at 2242 S. Sixth St., as well as serving as operating managers for the al fresco food court owned by Kirk and Marilyn Jefferis.
And Dalton Ingram, who co-owned and operated The Carriage House before a Christmas Eve court ruling gave sole ownership of the historic downtown property to his partner, has posted plans for a full coffee shop and brunch outlet to open in a yet-to-be-disclosed address.
This would be a separate venture than Java Junction, which Ingram opened in the center court of White Oaks Mall in January.
The Lewis' yet-to-be-named sophomore act will serve up sweet and savory pies (both whole and their signature hand pies), as well as craft cocktails and local craft beer.
'Three Twigs was known for its pies and poptarts,' Emily said. 'We're happy to get to bring a piece of that into our new venture.
'But this venture I'm going to be more behind the scenes doing the social media, bookkeeping. Things I can do from home. While Tim will be the face, running the day to day, booking events, working with the tenants.'
Already, the Lincoln-based Froggy's Groovie Goodies has signed a lease to operate from one of the four converted shipping containers encircling the open-air food court. Froggy's will feature flavored shaved ice, lemon shake ups and popcorn.
Lewis said they are on track to have leases signed for the remaining spaces by mid-March.
A May 1 opening date is planned for the seasonal operation that will create a family-friendly atmosphere offering live, local entertainment every weekend.
The Lewis' closed Three Twigs & Co.'s doors in Montvale Plaza Dec. 24 after announcing plans to scale back the popular cafe/bakery in an effort to rebalance their family life.
Ingram has yet to disclose the address of his latest venture or even whether he will be reviving The Carriage House name for it.
'While we will not reopen in The Carriage House building, we have secured a location and will be opening a new location in April,' Ingram wrote in a Feb. 13 Facebook post.
He cited issues with the foundation at 724 E. Edwards St. and a dispute between the partners as the cause for the move. The entire Carriage House staff, however, will make a reappearance at the new brunch space, the post read.
The historic house was constructed in 1840 by Springfield teamster John Zeller, who lived at the address for 20 years. The building was renovated in 2008 to house the sister businesses – The Carriage Co. and The Chuckwagon at the Springfield Carriage Co. from 2007 to 2011 across from the Abraham Lincoln home site.
The business was revived in 2019 by new owners who christened the eatery the Springfield Carriage Co. Ingram and Pritchett purchased the business in November 2023, operating under that name until Ingram reopened the business as The Carriage House last December after a month-long renovation.
The address appeared briefly on RE/MAX Professional Springfield's listings earlier this year. The property is currently labeled 'Off Market.'
Restaurant rebrands
As the State Journal-Register previously reported, Empire Korean Steakhouse and Bar on Springfield's west side is being rebranded as Japan House March 1.
Kevin Huang, who co-owns the steakhouse w/ his father, said he will serve as manager for the new Japan House at 2100 W. White Oaks Drive. The name change also brings a new menu for the restaurant that will replace its Korean barbecue selections with a hibachi menu and expand on existing sushi offerings, Huang said.
Empire's main feature – the smokeless tabletop grills – will be retired with all food prep now done by staff in the kitchen.
Operating hours are 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and 4 to 9 p.m. Monday through Thursday; 11 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday; and 11 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. Sunday. Phone: 217-670-1814.
St Patrick's Day parade is preparing to roll through downtown Springfield March 15 while the official day falls on March 17. A la Carte will run a list of local St. Patrick's culinary specials March 9. Deadline to submit information is March 3.

title: Rochester girls basketball realizes potential with another upset for 3A regional title
author: Bill Welt
description: Rochester girls basketball always knew it had potential and pulled off another upset for the 3A regional title over Taylorville
content:
Show Caption
TAYLORVILLE — Throw out the records.
The old playoff adage certainly rings true for the Rochester girls basketball team.
The No. 7-seeded Rockets reeled off another 42-41 upset win over No. 3 host Taylorville following Taylor Offer's go-ahead free throws with 2.1 seconds remaining for the program's first Class 3A regional title under second-year head coach Brandon Rose.
A Kyleigh Heimsness steal and subsequent Grace Rogers layup lifted Taylorville ahead 41-40 with under a minute left before Offer cut to the hoop to draw the shooting foul.
"We had to be careful and patient throughout the game," Offer said of attacking Taylorville's 1-2-2 zone defense. "I just went into it, took the contact and threw the ball up honestly."
Her first free throw cradled the front of the rim before falling in. Her next attempt was gravy.
"I've been shooting iffy on free throws the past few games, so it was really nice to hit those two," Offer said.
The 5-foot-5 senior point guard led the Rockets with 14 points, while junior guard Alaina Stock finished with three 3-pointers and 13 points. Cami Tinder and Delaney Farris each had seven points.
Tinder converted a key 3 to end the third quarter ahead 33-29 before Farris regained a 40-37 advantage from long range in the final two minutes.
"We always had it in us," Stock said. "We just really performed well. We executed very well, played good defense and shot the ball well."
Rochester (11-22) advances to the Chatham Glenwood Sectional semifinals against No. 1 Mahomet-Seymour on Tuesday at 6 p.m. The Rockets also knocked off 2024 state runner-up Glenwood, 42-33, in the regional semifinals on Monday.
"It's a wonderful feeling," Stock said. "I can't even put it into words. To see the team come together and perform this well against two very good teams, it's just great."
Taylorville (19-11) was without senior guard and NCAA Division I Southeast Missouri State commit Addison Tarr due to injury. Rogers, a sophomore, tallied 10 of her 13 points in the final period. Senior forward Mazie Fleming, a Division II University of Illinois Springfield volleyball recruit, contributed 15 points and nine rebounds. Heimsness had eight points.
Tarr, Fleming and Heimsness each achieved over 1,000 career points over their high school careers.
"You can't ask as a coach to have better players to work with," Taylorville coach Hayden Eldred said. "Them being here and playing varsity for four years, it's definitely going to be tough without them. They've been so great for us and leading these younger girls to pass the torch onto next year. I'm so proud of them and it was privilege to coach them."

title: Trump removes 150-year-old Resolute Desk from the Oval Office to be 'lightly refinished'
author: Greta Cross
description: President Donald Trump temporarily removes the 150-year-old Resolute Desk from the Oval Office to be refinished.
content:
President Donald Trump has temporarily taken the 150-year-old Resolute Desk out of the Oval Office for refinishing.
'A President, after election, gets a choice of 1 in 7 desks,' Trump wrote on social media. 'This desk, the 'C&O,' which is also very well known and was used by President George H.W. Bush and others, has been temporarily installed in the White House while the Resolute Desk is being lightly refinished —a very important job. This is a beautiful, but temporary replacement!'
When President Harry S. Truman first used the desk at the White House, it was brought into the Oval Office by President John F. Kennedy and became an iconic backdrop as his son, John F. Kennedy Jr., played inside the desk while his father was working.
What is the Resolute Desk?
Gifted to former President Rutherford B. Hayes by Queen Victoria in 1880, the Resolute Desk is a double pedestal partner's desk made from oak timbers of the British Shop HMS Resolute, according to The White House Historical Association.
For many years, the desk was used on the second floor of the White House, where the presidential offices were located before the addition of the West Wing in 1902.
In 1945, the Presidential Coat-of-Arms, the seal of the U.S. president, was fitted on the desk.
Between 1948-1952, the desk was moved to the Broadcast Room on the White House's ground floor and was used for a short period of time for radio and television broadcasts by former President Dwight D. Eisenhower, according to The White House Historical Association.
Former President John F. Kennedy was the first president to use the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office.
When former President Lyndon B. Johnson took office in 1963, he requested another desk for the Oval Office, according to The White House Historical Association. Between 1966 and 1977, the Resolute Desk was part of a traveling exhibition before it was put on display at the Smithsonian.
Former President Jimmy Carter requested the return of the Resolute Desk in 1977, where it has remained since − except by George H.W Bush who used the C&O Desk.
Per The White House Historical Association, before its arrival to the White House, the Resolute Desk was a part of a British arctic expedition in 1852. During the expedition, the desk was abandoned and became trapped it ice. In 1855, the desk was recovered by an American whaler and Congress appropriated funding to refit the ship that the desk was on to England, as a gift to Queen Victoria.
Queen Victoria reaffirmed the U.S. friendship and constructed a new version of the desk, which was then given to Hayes, according to The White House Historical Association.
What presidents have used the Resolute Desk?
Beginning with the 19th president, Rutherford B. Hayes, every president has used the Resolute Desk, except George H.W Bush, who only used it for five months before requesting the C&O, according to The White House Historical Association.
What is the C&O Desk?
The Georgian-style C&O Desk is made of walnut and features golden handles. The desk's acronym stands for the Chesapeake and Ohio Railway because the desk was built for one of the railway's owners and later donated to the White House, according to Realtor.com.
George H.W. Bush was the first and only president − up until Trump − to utilize the C&O Desk.
What other desks can a sitting president choose from?
Theodore Roosevelt Desk
The Theodore Roosevelt Desk was crafted for the former president in 1903. It resided in the West Wing until 1929, in which it was stashed until former President Harry S. Truman took it out of storage in 1945, according to Realtor.com. Former Presidents Eisenhower, Woodrow Wilson and William Howard Taft are among others who signed legislation on the desk.
Today, the Theodore Roosevelt Desk is housed in the Vice President's Ceremonial Office in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building.
The Johnson Desk
Upon taking office, Johnson requested that a new desk be made for the Oval Office by the Senate's carpenters, according to Realtor.com. Johnson was the only president to ever use the desk.
Today, The Johnson Desk is located at the Lyndon Baines Johnson Library and Museum.
The Hoover Desk
During former President Herbert Hoover's presidency in 1929, a fire severely damaged the West Wing of the White House, including the Oval Office. The president's desk survived the fire, but when new furniture was installed, so was a new desk.
A gift from the Grand Rapids Michigan Furniture Manufacture's Association, Hoover's desk was made of American wood and a Michigan maple veneer, according to the Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum.
When former President Franklin D. Roosevelt took the presidential office next, he continued to use Hoover's desk. On the desk he signed the New Deal, declarations of war with Japan and Germany and the GI Bill, according to the Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum.
The Wilson Desk
Despite what folks may think, The Wilson Desk was not named after former President Woodrow Wilson. Perhaps it was named after the early Vice President Henry Wilson, Realtor.com hypothesizes.
Former Presidents Gerald Ford and Richard Nixon both used the mahogany desk. Today, it is on display in the Vice President's Room in the U.S. Capitol.

title: Deadline to get a REAL ID looms for Illinois residents. Do you need one? What to know.
author: Tom Ackerman
description: After years of delaying the deadline the implementation of the REAL ID, the mandates will be enforced starting on May 7. Here's what you need to know.
content:
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias says travelers boarding domestic flights will start to receive warnings if they fly without a passport or REAL ID.
TSA will be fully enforcing the federal mandates in spring of 2027.
Real IDs are not mandatory.
This spring, some Illinois residents may need to obtain a REAL ID unless they have a valid U.S. passport.
Airports and certain federal facilities will soon require the updated identification throughout the country. Though the deadlines have been delayed since the first extension in 2008, the Transportation Security Administration says they will be fully enforcing the federal mandates in Spring of 2027.
Here are a few reminders about the REAL IDs.
What is the REAL ID?
Congress passed the REAL ID Act in 2005 to boost security in direct response to vulnerabilities highlighted by the Sept. 11 attacks.
The Act created standards for state-issued drivers' licenses and IDs that federal agencies would accept for boarding commercial aircraft and entering certain federal facilities.
Are the IDs mandatory?
No, if you have a valid passport, military ID or other federally approved identification, you don't need a REAL ID to board a plane or enter certain federal buildings.
You do not need a REAL ID to legally drive a vehicle if you have a valid driver's license.
You do not need a REAL ID to show identification.
You do not need a REAL ID for proof of citizenship.
'I don't want to discourage anyone from getting a REAL ID, but the fact is that not everyone needs a real ID on May 7, and in some cases might not ever need one,' said Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias said at a news conference Thursday.
Do I need to get one by May 7?
Giannoulias says no, but it would be wise to do so sooner than later if you know you will need the REAL ID.
Travelers boarding domestic flights may receive a warning soon if they do not have a REAL ID or passport, he said.
The TSA will soon begin its 'phased enforcement approach' that will ultimately lead to full enforcement of the mandates on May 5, 2027.
How do I make an appointment to get a REAL ID?
Make an appointment with the Department of Motorized Vehicles by calling or visting their website.
What do I need in order to get a REAL ID?
When applying for real ID, people should be prepared with:
Proof of identity such as U.S. passport or birth certificate
Proof of valid social security number, such as social security card or W2
Two forms of Illinois residency
Verification of your written signature.

title: Illinois lawmaker proposes bill to help teachers pay for school supplies
author: Tom Ackerman
description: In a release announcing the bill, the lawmaker said, "teachers shouldn't have to pay for classroom supplies out of their own pockets."
content:
An Illinois lawmaker has proposed a bill that would help teachers to pay for school supplies.
Jed Davis, R-Yorkville, introduced House Bill 3008 earlier this month that would provide teachers with a Classroom Supply Assistance Card that would purchase a list of preapproved items.
'Teachers shouldn't have to pay for classroom supplies out of their own pockets,' Rep. Davis wrote in a news release. 'No other profession expects employees to cover work expenses from their own salary. This bill helps teachers keep more of their hard-earned money and ensures students have the supplies they need to succeed.'
The bill proposed would provide teachers throughout the state, each school quarter with funds according to a 'needs-based formula, taking into account school district funding' among other factors, according to the text of the bill.
Do most teachers buy their own school supplies?
Over 90% of teachers spend their own money on school supplies, according to the National Education Association, the largest teachers union in the country, according to a 2022 report from the organization.
In a federal Department of Education survey that looked at the 2014 and 2015 school year; teachers who reported spending their own money on the school supplies spent $479 each on average.
What else does the bill say?
Purchases made on the card for school supplies would be tracked electronically and monitored to ensure compliance with the list of approved supplies, in addition to other ways described of preventing misuse.
Rep. Davis introduced the bill on Feb. 6, and it was referred to Rules Committee the same day.
The bill is one of 12 in Rep. Davis' Protecting Kids Bill Package. Other bills in the package would require online platforms distributing adult content to verify ages before granting access, and would require human trafficking awareness training for cosmetologists, barbers, bartenders, taxi drivers and teachers, to name a few.

title: Stepfather indicted on murder, torture charges of stepson in Springfield area
author: Tom Ackerman
description: A man in Sangamon County has been formally accused of prolonged abuse that led to the death of his 16-year-old stepson.
content:
A man in Sangamon County has been formally accused of prolonged abuse that led to the death of his 16-year-old stepson.
A Sangamon County Grand Jury indicted Steven Griffin on eight counts including first-degree murder in the death of Daniel Garza.
The indictment accuses Griffin of not adequately feeding or giving water to Garza and also causing blunt force injuries to his body and head that killed him.
Griffin, Garza, and Garza's mother, Kristin Griffin were living out of hotels in Springfield since they moved from the state of Washington in November 2024. Everything the jury has accused Griffin of happened in Sangamon County.
Garza died on Feb. 7 after being transferred to a hospital in Indianapolis for specialized care, according to a press release.
Garza was initially taken to the emergency room at St. John's Hospital on Jan. 27 by his mother and stepfather Griffin.
Garza was unresponsive, not breathing, had a body temperature of 86 degrees, and he weighed 94 pounds at that time. Garza also had a subdural hemorrhage in his head and burns to his face, neck and chest. He also had bruising covering most of his body and fractures to his shoulder blade and ankle.
Garza was first transferred to St. Louis Children's Hospital and then eventually to Indianapolis.
Griffin is additionally charged with aggravated battery which alleges that he threw hot water on Daniel, causing serious burns to his face, neck, and chest. The charge defines Griffin's actions as intentional and torturous.
Griffin also faces a charge of aggravated domestic battery that accuses Griffin of hitting Daniel in the back of the head with nun chucks and also stomping on Garza's ankle that caused a fracture.
Additional charges indicate that Garza had a disability.
Griffin charged in unrelated case
Griffin has also been indicted in an unrelated case that accuses him of aggravated criminal sexual abuse, indecent solicitation of a child, grooming, sexual exploitation of a child, and distributing material to a 16-year-old girl from Springfield.
The case was investigated by the Springfield Police Department and the Illinois Department of Children and Family Services.
Griffin is jailed in Sangamon County and his next court date is March 24. He had made a court appearance on both cases on Feb. 20.

title: Two people dead after head-on collision just north of Springfield
author: Steven Spearie
description: A driver headed east on Illinois 97 crossed the centerline, striking another vehicle. Here's what we know.
content:
Two people were killed in a head-on collision on Illinois 97, just west of Farmington Cemetery Road in rural Sangamon County, near 2:30 a.m. Saturday, according to Illinois State Police officials.
The site of the crash was about eight miles northwest of Springfield.
A driver in a Mitsubishi Outlander headed east on Route 97 crossed the centerline and struck the driver of a Hyundai Sonata traveling the opposite direction.
The reason for why the driver crossed the centerline, according to a report provided by Trooper Jayme Bufford of the ISP, was "unknown."
Neither vehicle had any passengers.
A 63-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene, according to Sangamon County Coroner Jim Allmon.
A 43-year-old woman was taken to Springfield Memorial Hospital where she later died.
The identities will be released after families are notified, Allmon said.
Bufford here were a couple witnesses that had stopped at the crash site, though no one witnessed the actual crash.
Traffic in both directions was shut down on Route 97 for about six hours Saturday morning, according to ISP.
The crash remains under investigation.

title: See our top photos from the girls basketball Waverly Sectional semifinals on Tuesday

description: Here are photos from the girls basketball Waverly Sectional semifinals featuring Pleasant Plains, Carlinville, Staunton and Camp Point Central
content:
