title: Matt Gaetz ethics report finds 'substantial evidence' of statutory rape, prostitution
author: Josh Meyer
description: Gaetz on Monday tried to block the report's official release, filing for a restraining order in Washington, D.C., federal court.
content:
WASHINGTON − The House Ethics Committee found "substantial evidence" former Rep. Matt Gaetz engaged in "prostitution, statutory rape, illicit drug use" and obstruction of Congress in a long-awaited report on alleged misconduct by President-elect Donald Trump's original choice for the next U.S. attorney general, according to a report released Monday.
Gaetz made a last-minute futile effort in federal court to prevent the release of the committee's report into allegations that have dogged the Florida Republican for years. He has strenuously denied paying for sex with a minor, and a years-long Justice Department investigation ended without the filing of criminal charges.
'The record overwhelmingly suggests that Representative Gaetz had sex with multiple women" at a 2017 Florida party, "including the then-17-year-old, for which they were paid," the report said.
"Victim A recalled receiving $400 in cash from Representative Gaetz that evening, which she understood to be payment for sex," the report said. "At the time, she had just completed her junior year of high school."
That witness told the committee she had not informed Gaetz she was younger than 18, "nor did he ask her age," the report said.
Gaetz was among speakers who addressed the conservative Turning Point AmericaFest 2024 in Phoenix on Sunday ahead of Trump. He didn't immediately respond to an email seeking comment. In a social media post on X, he said, "Giving funds to someone you are dating - that they didn't ask for - and that isn't 'charged' for sex is now prostitution?!?"
"There is a reason they did this to me in a Christmas Eve-Eve report and not in a courtroom of any kind where I could present evidence and challenge witnesses," Gaetz wrote.
Sex, cocaine, illegal favors and a free Bahamas trip
In its 37-page report and four appendices, the committee disclosed numerous bombshell findings, all of them unproven allegations about Gaetz's behavior in the years before he resigned from Congress.
They include:
From at least 2017 to 2020, Gaetz "regularly" paid women for sex.
From 2017 to 2019, Gaetz "used or possessed illegal drugs, including cocaine and ecstasy, on multiple occasions."
Gaetz "accepted gifts, including transportation and lodging in connection with a 2018 trip to the Bahamas, in excess of permissible amounts."
In 2018, Gaetz had his chief of staff help a sexual partner obtain a passport, "falsely indicating to the U.S. Department of State that she was a constituent."
Gaetz "knowingly and willfully sought to impede and obstruct the Committee's investigation of his conduct."
Gaetz: Report is 'unprecedented overreach'
In a post on X, Gaetz last week said he had sent money to girlfriends and women he dated, 'even some I never dated but who asked,' and acknowledged he "probably partied, womanized, drank and smoked more than I should have" when he was younger.
But, he insisted, 'I NEVER had sexual contact with someone under 18. Any claim that I have would be destroyed in court − which is why no such claim was ever made in court."
On Monday morning, he asked a federal judge in Washington, D.C., to stop the Ethics Committee from releasing the report.
He accused the Ethics Committee of "unprecedented overreach that threatens fundamental constitutional rights and established procedural protections."
Read the Gaetz report
A secret turnabout
The bipartisan committee voted in secret earlier this month to release the report over the objections of some Republicans.
The vote was an about-face for the committee, which had declined to release the report in November. Gaetz resigned shortly after Trump nominated him for Attorney General.
Trump had called Gaetz 'a deeply gifted and tenacious attorney" who had "distinguished himself in Congress through his focus on achieving desperately needed reform at the Department of Justice.'
The 10-member Ethics Committee is equally divided between Republicans and Democrats and meets behind closed doors.
Committee members previously had voted along party lines not to release their findings, which were based on a nearly four-year investigation.
House Democrats pushed to release the report in November, even after Gaetz resigned from Congress and bowed out of consideration to be Trump's attorney general.
Republicans had insisted the report should remain confidential because Gaetz was no longer in Congress. It was not known which Republicans changed their vote in order to allow the report to be made public.
A vote on the House floor to force the release of the report also failed when virtually all GOP lawmakers voted against it. A particularly vocal opponent was Johnson Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., who said publishing the report would set a "terrible precedent."
Ethics reports have been released previously after a member's resignation but only rarely.
The Justice Department previously investigated Gaetz for potential sex trafficking but closed the inquiry without charges, his lawyers told USA TODAY in February 2023.
Gaetz said in his Wednesday post on X that he had been fully exonerated, though federal authorities have never explicitly said that.
The Committee said evidence showed Gaetz sometimes paid women who attended parties with him and Joel Greenberg, a close friend who was later convicted of underage sex trafficking, wire fraud, and other crimes.
Greenberg "sometimes paid women for having sex with Representative Gaetz and was sometimes reimbursed by Representative Gaetz," the report said. "Witnesses indicated that there were times where a lump sum would be sent to one woman, who would then distribute the money evenly among others who attended the parties."

title: Find out The State Journal-Register's All-Area girls tennis player of the year and teams
author: Trevor Lawrence
description: Get to know the 12 players on the Springfield all-area girls tennis team for the 2024 season, plus the player of the year
content:
Chatham Glenwood's Samantha Shankland earned her first All-Area Player of the Year girls tennis award in the fall.
The senior — who finished with a 25-7 record and played in the Nos. 1 and 2 singles spots for Glenwood — hit her mark in the championship season by winning the Central State Eight Conference tournament with a 6-4, 6-3 victory over teammate Ellie Surges in the title match.
She followed that up with three wins and a second place showing in the Class 2A Chatham Glenwood Sectional at Washington Park. As the fifth seed, Shankland defeated fourth seed Gabi Hill of Edwardsville 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (3) in the quarterfinals and then knocked off No. 2 seed Natalie Spihlman of O'Fallon 7-5, 6-0 in the semifinals to reach the title match.
She lost to top seed Dia Kannan of Edwardsville 6-1, 7-5 for the championship, but avenged her previous season after losing in the quarterfinals as a junior and failing to reach the Illinois High School Association state tennis finals.
Shankland won a consolation match and went 1-2 at state by beating Vicky Lipinski of Palos Hills Staggs 6-1, 6-3.
Here is the rest of the all-area team separated by singles and doubles. The singles team is in alphabetical order by player and the doubles team is in alphabetical order by school.
Singles
Laney Aleman, Sacred Heart-Griffin
As SHG's No. 2 singles player, the senior finished with a 10-12 record and helped the Cyclones win the Class 1A Jacksonville Sectional.
She won a match at the sectional as a No. 6 seed and her season ended with a 7-5, 6-2 loss to No. 3 Alyssa Ley of Quincy Notre Dame in the quarterfinals of the draw.
Aleman took third place in the No. 2 draw at the Central Illinois Invite and placed sixth at the CS8 meet as a No. 4 seed.
Caroline Sheehan, Sacred Heart-Griffin
The top singles player for SHG won the Class 1A Jacksonville Sectional and was instrumental in the Cyclones claiming the team title by one point over second place Jerseyville 20-19.
She defeated second seed Kiley King of Jerseyville for the sectional title 6-2, 6-0 and reached her first state meet, winning a match in the championship bracket before finishing 1-2 in the tournament.
Sheehan put together some positive results throughout her senior season. She placed second in the No. 1 singles draw at the Central Illinois Invite and took third at the CS8 meet.
She finished the season 19-9.
Ellie Surges, Chatham Glenwood
The junior's improvement helped her spend some weeks as the top singles player on Glenwood's roster.
Surges started the season with an 11-0 record and had a signature win in a dual meet at Chatham over Rochester's Julia Musgrave, the 2023 All-Area Player of the Year. After her second-place finish at conference, Surges, playing as a sixth seed, mustered a 6-7 (1), 6-0, 6-3 win over No. 4 Toby Hawkes of Collinsville and advanced to the sectional semifinals, earning her a berth to state.
She settled for third place at the sectional after beating Spihlman, who retired in the third set. Surges went 0-2 at state and ended with a 24-7 record and accumulated a 12-3 mark in the No. 1 doubles spot primarily with teammate Lydia Ryherd.
Doubles
Leah Range/Abby White, Jacksonville
The sophomores won a three-set tiebreaker and took fifth place in the CS8 conference doubles draw as the Crimsons posted their best outcome in recent years with a fourth-place finish and 15½ points.
Range and White got to the quarterfinals of the 1A Jacksonville Sectional but fell short of making a state appearance with a three-set loss to SHG's Lucia Hassebrock and Catalina Mosquera.
The duo finished 20-12.
Julia Musgrave/Cora Haupt, Rochester
Musgrave, one of the top singles players, concentrated on doubles with Haupt during the championship season and the pair produced a third-place finish at conference and a second place showing at the 1A Jacksonville Sectional.
The finish at the sectional earned the Rochester duo a spot at state, but the senior Musgrave had an illness, and she was replaced by sophomore Molly Eichholz. Haupt, a junior, and Eichholz lost to the No. 1 seed in the first round at state and finished the tournament 0-2.
Musgrave and Haupt ended the season 13-9.
Lucia Hassebrock/Catalina Mosquera, Sacred Heart-Griffin
As the fifth seed, the duo also played a role in SHG's sectional title at Jacksonville. Hassebrock, a sophomore, and the freshman Mosquera got to the semifinals and eventually finished fourth to earn a spot in the 1A state finals.
They finished state with a 1-2 record, winning a consolation match. Once the tandem settled in as a team in early October, they took fourth place at the CS8 meet and finished the season with an overall 9-6 mark.
Myla Shannon/Madisyn Williams, Springfield High
They earned a sixth-place finish at the CS8 meet and had an overall record of 7-7.
Shannon, a senior, and Williams a sophomore, won two matches as an unseeded team at the 2A Chatham Glenwood Sectional before losing in three sets to O'Fallon in the quarterfinals.

title: PORTA girls adapt, persevere to beat Hillsboro, move into Riverton final
author: Ryan Mahan
description: Despite going 2-for-13 at the free-throw line in the third quarter and 12 of 29 overall in the game, the PORTA girls basketball team held on to beat Hillsboro.
content:
RIVERTON — Hillsboro threw all kinds of defensive strategies at Petersburg PORTA, but the Bluejays managed to survive scoring droughts to beat the Hiltoppers 51-39 in the Riverton Christmas Classic semifinals on Friday.
Seniors Carson Arthalony and Cassie Cox combined for 29 points and 18 rebounds to send PORTA into a rematch with Deer Creek-Mackinaw in Saturday's 7:30 p.m. title game after the Chiefs toppled Roanoke-Benson 58-37 in the other semifinal at the Hawk Center.
PORTA beat Dee-Mack 36-29 on Nov. 23 to win the Clinton Turkey Tussle.
Arthalony finished with 15 points and nine rebounds. Cox was 6-for-10 from the floor, also grabbed nine boards and finished with 14 points.
To make up for its size disadvantage against PORTA's pair of dynamic forwards, the Hiltoppers tried everything they could to make life difficult for Arthalony and Cox. And even when Hillsboro's defense committed eight fouls in the third quarter alone, PORTA missed 11 of 13 free-throws in the period.
Even Hillsboro's defense forced PORTA into turnovers in the second half. The Bluejays (12-3) had just four giveaways in the first half but lost that battle 14-13 with 10 in the second half.
'I thought we started the game off a little timid and were intimidated by their size,' Hillsboro coach Bret Tuetken said. 'After halftime, we came out and played more of the style of basketball we're accustomed to.'
Hillsboro (10-5) continued its push into the fourth. Delaney Adams and Tatum Christian each made a pair of free throws before PORTA's Regan Huebner, a freshman, scored a layup off an Aubrey Vogel assist as the Bluejays regained a 10-point lead. But Christian had a hook shot and a jumper to pull Hillsboro within 41-35.
That was as close as Hillsboro got. Cox, Arthalony and Vogel combined for the next seven points to push PORTA's lead back to double digits.
'When they doubled the post like that ... we talked about how we have to find our open teammates,' Arthalony said. 'We had our guards cut. When I was double-teamed and Cassie's (defender) came over, I did a good job dumping it off to (Cox) and she did the same thing for me.'
Because of the relentless defense Hillsboro played, PORTA's first-year head coach, Derek Schnapp, relied on three freshmen — Heubner, Rylee Boensel and Mackenzie Miller — to spell his starters.
'We needed to play a few more players than we normally need tonight,' Schnapp said. 'I think sometimes I'm unfair to our freshmen, and I tell them that, but they also need to get baptized by fire sometime and tonight was a game we got some freshmen get baptized by fire. That's OK; that will only make us stronger in the long run.'
Despite all that went in Hillsboro's favor, PORTA's defense also made the Hiltoppers struggle. Hillsboro shot 28% (14 of 50) and were just 1-for-16 from behind the 3-point line.
'We just couldn't get any 3s to drop tonight and that's a big part of our game,' Tuetken said.
Christian led Hillsboro with 14 points but fell to the floor in pain with 1 minute, 6 seconds left and had to be helped off the floor.
Hillsboro will face Roanoke-Benson in the third-place game at 6 p.m.
Fifth-place semifinals
MOUNT PULASKI 54, PANA 33: Elayna Marten led the Hilltoppers with 17 points and hit three times from behind the 3-point line to lead Mount Pulaski into the fifth-place title game.
Marten scored nine points in the third quarter as the Hilltoppers turned a 23-10 halftime lead into a 42-26 advantage after three.
Alyson Murphy and Claire Bobell each added nine points for Pulaski while Addison Brown had eight.
Pana's Delaney Hackler led the Panthers with 10 points.
PAWNEE 51, AUBURN 38: In the other semifinal, Greenlee Dust and Ava Rodriguez combined for 33 points to lead Pawnee into the fifth-place title game.
Dust led Pawnee with 18 points, with 16 coming in the middle quarters. Rodriguez finished with 15, including six in the first.
Addison Wheatley led the Trojans with 12 points.
Pawnee and Mount Pulaski will play at 4:30 p.m. on Saturday.
Consolation semifinals
MOWEAQUA CENTRAL A&M 53, LITCHFIELD 36: Adia Meichert scored a game-high 22 points, but it wasn't enough to prevent the Purple Panthers from falling into the consolation third-place game.
The Raiders got 14 points from Gwyn Hardimon, 10 from Lyndi Woods and nine from Kylee Snearly.
RIVERTON 44, NORTH MAC 42: Jordyn Durham poured in 26 points and led the Hawks in a spirited comeback win over the Panthers to move into the consolation title game against Central A&M.
North Mac led 18-12 at halftime, but Riverton chipped away in a third quarter that saw the lead change as the Hawks outscored the Panthers 24-10. During that run, North Mac coach Ross Bryll argued a call, received a technical foul, then proceeded to continue his protest to earn a second technical and an ejection. Durham, who was 12-for-15 at the free-throw line, made seven of nine in the third quarter, including the technical foul free throws, to give Riverton a lead.
'I think we brought the energy up, defensive-wise and offensive-wise,' Durham said. 'We were moving the ball around and were more playing as a team.'
It was the second win in a row for the Hawks since an 0-10 start.
Taylor Keirs led North Mac with 12 points, Brittnee Lange had 11 and April Waters added 10 in the loss.
'Going into this, we knew (Keirs) and (April Waters) were going to hurt (Riverton),' Riverton coach Russell White said. 'We went up 10 points at one point ... we started to lose it, but with a young team, I almost expected (Riverton's) run to stop and (North Mac) to catch back up.
'We did a lot of good things and when we execute, we can win.'
Riverton will face Central A&M in the consolation title game on Saturday at 3 p.m. North Mac will meet Litchfield in the consolation third-place game at 1:30 p.m.

title: Langfelder won't push for petition for full recount; not ruling out another run for office
author: Steven Spearie
description: Frank Lesko won the Sangamon County Recorder's election over Josh Langfelder by 31 votes with over 98,000 votes cast.
content:
Former Sangamon County Recorder Josh Langfelder maintained Thursday there was "enough information to substantiate a change in the (Nov. 5) election totals" separating current recorder Frank Lesko and him.
But a daunting court schedule and potential prohibitive costs made Langfelder decide not to pursue a petition for a full recount.
Langfelder, first elected to the office in 2008 and the only Democrat to hold onto a county-wide office, made the announcement via text around 8 p.m. Thursday. Langfelder's team would have had to file the court petition by the end of Thursday.
Langfelder said he consulted with his attorneys, Jim Morphew and Brian Lee of Sorling Northrup, in the process.
Lesko, who has held on to his position as Springfield Clerk, won the election by 31 votes with over 98,000 votes cast. He had a 68-vote lead on Nov. 5, but that shrank after provisional ballots and late-arriving vote by mail ballots were counted two weeks later.
Reached by The State Journal-Register Thursday, Lesko said he planned to submit his letter of resignation as clerk on Friday. The resignation would be effective at the end of the day on Tuesday.
Lesko, who was officially sworn in as recorder on Dec. 2, said he hasn't been taking a salary or benefits from the county since that time.
The decision by Langfelder, Lesko said, was "a positive step in the right direction for the citizens of Sangamon County. I believe in our political system, and I wanted my opponent to feel whole in our election and in the results. I'm happy it has come to an end, and I look forward to serving the people in Sangamon County."
The recorder's office is the official land records depository for the county. Instruments filed with the office include deeds, mortgages, releases and assignments, property liens, as well as assorted federal, state and local liens.
Langfelder on Thursday said he thought he had evidence gathered by volunteers during the discovery recount to present to the court. Langfelder was able to apply for a discovery recount because he lost by a margin of less than 5%.
"When you weighed that (the case) could potentially go for a year and cost in excess of estimates of $50,000, I felt I needed to move on," Langfelder said. "Elected offices are difficult on families, and I didn't want to put my family through that again."
While Langfelder said he felt he had a strong case, there were no guarantees the recount would flip the election in his favor.
The discovery recount, which lasted over a week and wrapped up Dec. 18, had volunteers from both camps looking at ballots, mail-in envelopes, voter rolls and signatures, among other things, from 25% of the precincts in the county, or 41 of the 166. Langfelder said it was "a mixed bag" of city and county precincts.
On Thursday, Langfelder presented evidence to the media that there was "a strong chance" 36 votes most likely could have gone into his column. He added there were also 10 rejected ballots for "no signature," but did have a signature on the white mailing envelope.
"With the other precincts (in a full recount)," Langfelder said, "they might have found more (votes) that went in favor (of Lesko) and it could have kept him in the lead, or it could have flipped the election going for me. That's the million-dollar question. What would it have been?"
Lesko, 64, touted in campaign ads"Hire me so you can fire me," a reference to a plan to merge the recorder's office with the clerk's office. Lesko said no one would lose his or her job and that the recorder would leave the office at the completion of the merger.
Leading up to the election, Langfelder, 54, derided the talk as "a terrible idea" and "a political gimmick."
Lesko's decision to stay on as city clerk caused some consternation among alderpersons, among them, Ward 3 Ald. Roy Williams Jr.
"One of my issues was that (Lesko) was sworn in (as recorder)," Williams said recently "That changes everything. I think (the city council is) not being responsible for allowing this."
Langfelder said it was Lesko's prerogative to hold both offices, "though I don't think it's right."
City attorney Gregory Moredock said while Mayor Misty Buscher can receive interested inquiries about Lesko's successor, "it is ultimately up to the city council to select and appoint a new clerk."
The discovery recount, Langfelder admitted, "opened my eyes to a lot. The staff I dealt with in the county clerk's office, I appreciate them and what they did."
The extra work Clerk Don Gray's staff did reinforced, Langfelder said, why it wasn't beneficial to merge the two offices.
Langfelder said he did not contact Lesko on Thursday. The two shook hands and wished each other good luck after mail-in ballots were counted Nov. 19.
"I wish Josh and his family nothing but the best in their lives," Lesko said Thursday.
Langfelder, whose only other job other than in the recorder's office has been in the banking world, said he would be applying for jobs, but wouldn't rule out another run for office "whether that be a county-wide office or a city-wide office.
"The only way I get to run for another office is if my family allows me to do that. This has been a rollercoaster ride not just for me but for my family."

title: What's weather for New Year's Day in Springfield? We have you covered
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Hitting the town New Year's Eve? You may want to bring a jacket. Here's what to know about the forecast for New Year's Eve and New Year's Day.
content:
Warm weather over the holidays and the lack of a white Christmas may have left you either joyous or disappointed.
New Year's Day will bring cooler but overall sunny weather. Here's what you need to know.
Springfield weather
In Springfield, New Year's Eve will see scattered flurries between 9 p.m. and 3 a.m. It will be mostly cloudy with a low around 26, according to the National Weather Service. There will be gusts as high as 25 mph.
New Year's Day will be mostly sunny with a high near 33. There will be gusts as high as 23 mph.
Wednesday night will be partly cloudy with a low around 23. Winds could gust as high as 16 mph.
How about in Chicago and St. Louis -- for travelers?
At Chicago O'hare International Airport, New Year's Day will be partly sunny with a high near 30. Gusts will be as high as 30 mph.
Wednesday night in Chicago will be partly cloudy with a low around 21. Gusts will be as high as 20 mph.
At St. Louis Lambert International Airport, Wednesday will be mostly sunny with a high near 40. Gusts will be as high as 23 mph.
Wednesday night will be mostly clear with a low around 27.

title: Family-friendly event voted best place to spend New Year's Eve in Springfield
author: Steven Spearie
description: We asked our readers where the best place to spend New Year's Eve was in the area. Here's what readers voted for.
content:
More than half of the respondents to a State Journal-Register poll said the best place for a New Year's Eve date in Springfield is at First Night at the Hoogland Center for the Arts.
That outdistanced "staying at home/on the couch" in the SJ-R poll.
First Night, the family-friendly celebration of the arts put on by the Springfield Area Arts Council, is now in its 38th year.
It kicks off at the Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum at noon with children's crafts and live performances. There are other First Night-related events at Union Square Park and the Dana-Thomas House.
Among the performers at the Hoogland Center area the Lincoln Ring of Magicians, Central Illinois Irish Dancers, Lotus Fire Belly Dancers and Capital City Improv.
There's a fireworks display, with the Illinois Capitol Building as the backdrop, at 8 p.m.
Tickets are $25 (youth 15 and under attend free) and available at the SAAC website or the Hoogland box office.

title: Is Dollar General open or closed on New Year's Day 2025? Here's what to know
author: Mike Snider
description: Even though Wednesday, Jan. 1, 2025, is a federal holiday, many retailers including Dollar General are open.
content:
New Year's Day is a holiday but many retailers are open. Among them: Dollar General.
On the first day of 2025, you may need groceries, a snack or just want to go shopping. The good news is that you have plenty of options because most restaurant, grocery and retail chains will be open on Wednesday, Jan. 1, although some may have adjusted hours.
However, banks, post offices, shipping services and the stock market are not open because of the federal holiday.
Dollar General, which has more than 20,500 stores across the U.S., will be open. You can check for Dollar General store hours on the Dollar General website and in the Dollar General app.
For the holiday season, Dollar General began offering a new same-day delivery service called DG Delivery at a few of its stores.
You can check to see if that's still available at a Dollar General near you on the Dollar General website or mobile app. On the website, click the dropdown menu at the top of the website for which store you'd like to select. Then, click "Find delivery store." Then, input the delivery address to see if the retailer offers the service nearby.
Contributing: Greta Cross and Gabe Hauari.

title: Watching the Rose Parade on New Year's Day? Keep an eye out for the float from Illinois
author: Tom Ackerman
description: For the third consecutive year, the state of Illinois is building a float and participating in the Rose Parade on New Year's Day in California.
content:
Illinois will brightly and loudly represent at a major parade this week in California.
For the third consecutive year, the state of Illinois is building a float and participating in the Rose Parade on New Year's Day in Pasadena. Wednesday will mark the 136th annual parade.
Illinois' 22-foot-tall float boasts nearly 12,000 volunteer hours and more than 34,000 roses that recreates state icons with floral sculptures. The efforts are spearheaded by the state's Office of Tourism.
"Play Hooky in Illinois" is the theme of the float this year, with elements of the float tying to the 1986 film, "Ferris Bueller's Day Off."
What is the Rose Parade?
The Rose Parade travels five-and-a-half miles along Colorado Boulevard, featuring four main types of entries: floral-covered floats, equestrian units, marching bands, and Tournament Entries. Many of these participants have long-standing ties to the Tournament of Roses, helping to keep the event's traditions alive, according to the parade's site.
What's on the Illinois float?
Most of the featured elements of the float are from Chicago, though Central Illinois has been prominently featured in years past, and multiple central Illinoisians are billed as performers.
Performers on the front of the float will pay tribute to a scene in the movie where Ferris finds his way onto a float in Chicago's Von Steuben Day Parade on Dearborn Street in 1985.
Illinoisians are warming up to sing and dance to the songs 'Danke Schoen' and 'Twist & Shout." Like in the film, there will be dancers accompanying the tunes like Bavarian festivalgoers, office workers and construction crew workers.
Floral sculptures, to name a few, make up the Federal Plaza's Flamingo statue, crafted from red strawflowers; the Wrigley Field marquee, designed with large lima beans navy beans and pink strawflowers; and the iconic 'Save Ferris' water tower created from white mums and black bean lettering.
Enjoy Illinois has partnered with Paramount Pictures to create the float.
Central Illinois performers
Accomplished jazz musician Brian Culbertson, who is from Decatur, will sing and perform the two songs on the float.
Ferris Bueller lookalike and dancer Tyler Lankston, who grew up in the Germantown Hills area, will lip sync and dance to the two songs from the movie.
When is the parade?
The parade begins at 10 a.m. central time on Wednesday, Jan. 1.
How to watch it
The Rose Parade will be aired on ABC and NBC, among other channels. The program can also be streamed on Christmas Plus, Fubo, and Pluto TV.

title: 11 teenage boys in Illinois accused of luring men with dating app, beating them
author: Jonathan Limehouse
description: Eleven teenage boys have been charged with multiple felonies for allegedly using an online dating app to lure men to locations and beating them.
content:
Eleven teenage boys in Illinois have been charged with several felonies for allegedly using an online dating app to lure unsuspecting men to meetups and beating them, police said.
Ten 17-year-old boys, and one 16-year-old boy, have been charged with multiple felonies, including aggravated battery, mob action and criminal damage to property, the Mount Prospect Police Department said in a news release. One of the 17-year-olds is facing an additional two felony counts of a hate crime, according to the department.
The teenagers were arrested and charged between Nov. 11 and Nov. 20, 2024, police said.
Mount Prospect police's investigation found that some of the teenage suspects got the idea to lure the men through a viral social media trend they saw online, according to the department.
'We are asking parents to take these incidents as an opportunity to talk with their teenage children about the seriousness of actively participating in these types of trends they see on social media,' Police Chief Michael Eterno said in the release.
Mount Prospect is a village in Cook County that is about 24 miles away from Chicago.
Police: Teenagers lured men through dating app, beat them
Police reported the first incident occurred on July 8 at 9:45 p.m. and involved a 41-year-old man. The man reported to Mount Prospect police that he had been beaten earlier in the evening by a group of teenagers in the parking lot of a 7-Eleven on West Northwest Highway, police said.
The man told police that he used an online dating app to arrange to meet someone at the convenience store, according to the department. Once he arrived, the man said he was approached by a group of teenage boys who "confronted him verbally and battered him." The police also said the teenagers had damaged the man's vehicle.
According to the department, the man managed to leave the location in the damaged vehicle as the teenagers attempted to follow him in their cars.
The second incident occurred on the same day around 9:54 p.m., and it involved a 23-year-old man allegedly being lured and beaten by the group of teenage boys, police said. Like the initial report, the man told police he also used an online dating app to arrange to meet someone but he encountered the teenagers who battered him, according to the department.
As the man was being beaten, one of the teenagers slashed the tires on his vehicle, according to the department. Police said the man got back into his vehicle and drove away, but he eventually stopped the car once he realized what had happened to his wheels. The man then approached a home and asked them to call 911, and when emergency responders arrived they took him to a hospital to be treated for non-life-threatening injuries.
Police identified teenage boys through video surveillance
Mount Prospect police detectives were able to identify some of the teenage suspects through video surveillance footage of the incident at the 7-Eleven, the department said. A lengthy investigation determined that 11 total teenagers took part in one or both incidents, police said.
The investigation also determined that the 17-year-old boy charged with two counts of committing a hate crime yelled a racial slur and another derogatory term during one of the incidents, according to police.
Once the Cook County States Attorney's Office approved the charges, all the juvenile offenders willingly turned themselves in between Nov. 11 and Nov. 20, police said. They were taken to the Cook County Juvenile Detention Center in Chicago, according to the department. It is unclear if they are still in custody.

title: The viral Walmart Birkin bag keeps selling out: We found ones you can buy today
author: Kasey Caminiti
description: The viral Walmart Hermès Birkin bag dupe is sold out in almost every color. We found Wirkin bags available to buy today. Shop the bags before they sell out.
content:
Shop the Hermès Birkin bag dupe at Walmart while you still can.
— Recommendations are independently chosen by our editors. Purchases you make through our links may earn us and our publishing partners a commission.
Are you ready for the designer dupe of a lifetime? Walmart has recently made headlines by offering the legendary Hermès Birkin bags for insanely low prices ranging between $60 and $100, with inflated prices becoming available as the bags continue to sell out. The original bag that went viral on TikTok was available for less than $80 and sold out immediately. There are now similar bags at Walmart that are available for a fraction of the original cost and they are selling out just as fast. The bags at Walmart are aptly referred to as "Wirkins" and we found a couple of versions available from brands like KINGSS, SXXT and Lartappy that you can actually shop today.
Shop in-stock Walmart Birkin Bags
This bag from SXXT is available for $58.88 in several colors, including khaki, brown, black and red. This bag in particular has sold out several times and Walmart has restocked it periodically over the last day. We suggest adding this designer dupe to your cart immediately before it is too late!
For fashion enthusiasts and collectors alike, having access to a Birkin dupe like this is unheard of. The Birkin bag typically sells for thousands of dollars, making it accessible only to a select few. However, Walmart's jaw-dropping offer has pretty much democratized luxury, allowing everyone to own a version of fashion iconography without breaking the bank.
How much do authentic Hermès Birkin bags cost?
A real Hermès Birkin bag starts at around $10,000, with rare models selling for upwards of $500,000.
The brand famously requires customers to build a purchasing history and relationship with their Hermès sales associate. You are expected to buy several other products before being considered for a Birkin bag. Waitlists are common, and availability is deliberately kept mysterious.
Hermès Birkin bag dupe from Walmart went viral for its surprising resemblance to the iconic bags that retail for thousands of dollars.

We'll continue monitoring Walmart's site for Wirkin bag restocks.
How can I become a Walmart+ member?
You can sign up for a Walmart+ membership on the Walmart website. Membership includes benefits like free shipping, member prices on fuel, and early access to special promotions.

title: Here's a recipe for how to lighten up in 2025
author: Sheridan Lane
description: We all tend to look to make improvements at the start of the new year. Here's a recipe to how to lighten up in 2025.
content:
According to history.com, humans have been setting New Year's resolutions for some 4,000 years dating all the way back to the ancient Babylonians.
Ringing in a new year with celebration and a mindset to make improvements was central to even those early New Years' celebrations; yet from Forbes to U.S. News and World Report, statistics indicate that most of the resolutions we set in the modern-day are foiled by the end of February.
Why do we place so much emphasis on doing something to which we fail year after year? Psychologists, scholars, researchers and the like suggest that it is because we are bad at making realistic goals.
Since we are bad at setting goals for ourselves, I turned to AI for some help with my resolution this year rather than think one up on my own. AI's response gave me quite a chuckle.
'Lighten up' was its advice. Ironically enough, that phrase has echoed in my ears for years as it is something my parents used to say to me as a kid when I was too wrapped up in one thing or another.
While AI may know me mysteriously well, its recipe for how to achieve its proclaimed New Year's resolution to 'lighten up' is one in which we might all be able to enjoy and find success. I can even weave in AI's suggestion for 'top five food trends of 2025' right along with the ways in which I can accomplish a life that is a little lighter.
AI's recipe for how to lighten up in 2025
Practice 'digital minimalism' while enjoying 'functional hydration.'
Certainly, I am guilty of the so called 'doom scrolling' on social media, binge shopping on Amazon and of never drinking enough water; but I do believe I can achieve this mini goal in 2025 on my way to lightening up. My phone tracks just how much time I am on each of those apps, so I will just set a specific goal, which is the recommendation for actually achieving the goals we set. And while I like seeing posts with pictures of people I don't see often enough, I am going to enjoy a hot cup of tea from Whimsey Tea to wind down before bed instead of my nightly 'thumbs up,' 'likes' or 'hearts.'
'Laugh more,' and 'move more.' I am going to accomplish this goal by trying to incorporate a comedy series into my daily commute and by actually standing at the standing desk I got two years ago for my office. These two little things are just that — little things that AI suggests will help us in our overall mission to lighten up in 2025.
'Delve into experiences,' 'rediscover creativity' and enjoy 'experiential dining.' These two mini goals as well as the one top food trend are easy for all of us to achieve. Just join us at Lincoln Land Community College during the spring semester for Bistro to Go, Bistro Verde (www.llcc.eldu/bistro-verde) or one of LLCC Community Education's many culinary offerings that are available (www.llcc.edu/culinary-offerings). Make a plan to join us with a friend and/or to book at least one class or dinner, and we can check off this mini goal as complete!
Best wishes for a joyous and light 2025 from all of us at LLCC Hospitality Management and Culinary Arts.
Sheridan Lane is director of culinary programs and operations at Lincoln Land Community College.
Lincoln Land Community College offers credit programs in Culinary Arts, Hospitality Management and Baking/Pastry, and non-credit cooking and food classes through LLCC Community Education.

title: Southeast-Lanphier boys basketball game ends after first quarter fracas
author: Trevor Lawrence
description: A kerfuffle broke out in the first quarter of the Lanphier-Southeast boys basketball game. Both teams went to the locker room and the game was stopped.
content:
The crosstown rival game between Lanphier and Southeast renewed but the nonconference contest never finished at Lober-Nika Gymnasium.
With Lanphier leading 3-2 in the first quarter, senior Lions guard JaiQuan Holman scored a basket and was fouled, and a skirmish ensued that spilled over to the sidelines. Both benches emptied until the altercation was broken up. Southeast coach Wayne Hamilton sent his Southeast team to the locker room and Lanphier coach Blake Turner quickly did the same.
Both administration officials gathered to discuss the situation, and the game was called off with 4 minutes, 44 seconds remaining in the period.
The quick ending dampened Shaun Hatchett's ceremony before the game. Hatchett, a Lanphier senior forward, was honored for recording his 1,000th career-point when he scored a game-high 26 points in a 67-59 Lions victory over Collinsville on Saturday.
An update on a future playing date is not yet available. A text message sent to athletic directors of both schools was not responded to by press time.

title: Start the new year off with this sweet treat
author: Channing Fullaway-Johnson
description: The new year is a perfect time to try some new recipes. Check out this easy and tasty cinnamon swirl quick bread recipe.
content:
The new year is a perfect time to embrace fresh beginnings and explore new opportunities. Whether it's learning a new skill, such as playing an instrument, mastering a new language or finding a new hobby, the possibilities are endless. It's also a chance to experience new places, reconnect with friends or make new friends. No matter how big or small, taking steps to do something new can make this year something to remember.
Growing up as a homeschooler, learning wasn't just about books; it was about life skills. Whether I was watching my mom sew yards of welting in my parents' small business or whipping up something in the kitchen, my curiosity led the way. I have always enjoyed learning new things and challenging myself to continue to grow. Between the two crafts, I definitely excelled more with cooking than at sewing. One craft may have taken me to the ER as a child (a story for another day), and the other craft did not.
Before I even worked here at Lincoln Land Community College, I loved how many opportunities were offered through LLCC Community Education. There is a wide array of new and favorite non-credit classes, workshops, events and travel opportunities.
Of course, I have become very fond of the culinary offerings and love teaching and working with many great local chefs to bring new and fun classes to the community. These include hands-on cooking and baking classes suitable for all skill levels. You can learn to craft exquisite pastries, master international cuisines or enjoy themed dinners like Mardi Gras-Cajun inspired evenings. Even special nights out and youth cooking classes add to the culinary adventures that can be found.
Whether you are 5 or 105, learning should be fun and in a comfortable place to be with friends or meet new ones. So, what's something you've always wanted to try? Whether it's cooking, painting or traveling, this year could be the year you make it happen, right here with LLCC Community Education opportunities. The new year is a blank page. Why not fill it with adventure, growth and delicious memories?
Speaking of delicious memories … while sewing once sent me to the ER, baking has always been a safer and much sweeter adventure. If you're looking to bake something different, give this simple yet irresistible cinnamon swirl quick bread a try. It's a sweet start to a great year of possibilities!
Cinnamon Swirl Quick Bread
Ingredients:
Cinnamon Swirl
1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
1 Tablespoon ground cinnamon
Bread
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking soda
1/2 teaspoon salt
1 large egg, at room temperature
3/4 cup granulated white sugar
1/3 cup vegetable oil
1/3 cup sour cream, at room temperature
2/3 cup whole milk, at room temperature
1 1/2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract
Instructions
Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray a loaf pan with nonstick spray.
Cinnamon Swirl: Mix the 1/2-cup granulated sugar and 1 Tablespoon of ground cinnamon together.
Bread: Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt together in a large bowl.
In a medium bowl, whisk the egg and 3/4-cup granulated sugar together until combined.
Whisk in the oil, sour cream, milk and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and then whisk to completely combine. Avoid over-mixing.
Pour/spread half of the batter into prepared loaf pan. Sprinkle almost all of the cinnamon sugar evenly on top. It's a very thick layer of cinnamon sugar.
Carefully pour/spread remaining batter evenly on top. The top layer of batter will want to stick to the cinnamon sugar filling, making spreading a little tougher to do, but use a spoon to carefully spread it out as best you can.
Sprinkle with the rest of the cinnamon sugar. Using a knife, make a large swirl down the loaf pan. Try not to over-swirl, which will mix the layers together too much.
Bake the bread for 50-65 minutes, covering loosely with foil about halfway through to prevent the top from over-browning. Poke the center of the bread with a toothpick. When it comes out clean, the bread is done. Remember, baking times vary between ovens.
Remove from the oven. Allow the bread to cool in the pan set on a wire rack for 1 hour. After that, remove the bread from the pan, and let it cool directly on a wire rack.
Once cool, slice and serve. Cover and store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
Channing Fullaway-Johnson is the culinary coordinator at Lincoln Land Community College.
Lincoln Land Community College offers credit programs in Culinary Arts, Hospitality Management and Baking/Pastry, and non-credit cooking and food classes through LLCC Community Education.

title: Rochester school board hires law firm to investigate superintendent on leave
author: Steven Spearie
description: The Rochester Board of Education has hired a law firm to investigate the district superintendent who was placed on paid administrative leave.
content:
The Rochester Board of Education has hired an Monticello, Illinois-based law firm to investigate the district superintendent who was placed on paid administrative leave.
Board President Amy Reynolds didn't detail following Thursday's special board meeting why Dan W. Cox was being investigated.
Miller, Tracy, Braun, Funk & Miller, Ltd. was hired by the board, Reynolds said at the meeting. The announcement followed a two-and-a-half hour executive session.
The firm specializes in education law. Reynolds didn't immediately disclose how much the firm was being paid.
Normally, grievance investigations take 30 days, although it can ask for an extension, Reynolds said.
Reynolds and board vice president Todd Hannah met with Cox Monday.
Cox's salary is $201,500 annually, according to the district website.
While details from Rochester officials have been scant, a letter to the editor in the Rochester Times last fall from the district's former director of business services and treasurer, Robert "Bob" McDermott, raised issues about questionable business trips, budget overspending to the tune of $500,000 and other issues.
Jon Hansen, the district's director of communications and engagement, refuted some of McDermott's claims earlier this week.
McDermott, interviewed by The State Journal-Register several times in November and over Monday and Tuesday, maintained that details in the letter might have led directly to Cox's leave or prompted other questions about him.
"In my head, if someone's placed on administrative leave, there's something that they need to investigate and obviously it has to be serious," said McDermott, who spent 22 years with the district before retiring on June 30, 2023.
McDermott now lives out of state.
During public comment, Sarah Manning Kerley praised the board and its work, but also urged it to be as transparent as possible.
"Please know that you have community support as you work through the next several difficult weeks," said Kerley, a candidate for one of three board seats up on April 1.
Cox has been with the district since 2020, coming from the superintendent position in Staunton. Cox also was the superintendent with the Jasper County Community Unit School District in Newton.

title: Fundraising underway for Springfield woman who was killed on New Year's Day
author: Tom Ackerman
description: A fundraising campaign is underway for a Springfield woman who was shot and killed on New Year's Day.
content:
A fundraising campaign is underway for a Springfield woman who was shot and killed on New Year's Day.
Kilanna Gladney, 31, died from a single gunshot wound, the preliminary findings from an autopsy showed.
Now, a GoFundMe fundraiser is looking to raise $9,000 to help the family travel and make funeral arrangements. As of Tuesday night, $2,000 had been raised.
Gladney's mother, Linda Pughsley organized the fundraiser. Pughsley lives in Florida and will travel to Springfield to start caring for grandchildren in Springfield, according to the GoFundMe.
'This is a mother's worst nightmare," she wrote on the fundraiser's page. "I thought my kids would bury me. I have a very long, hard journey ahead of me. This is that example of it takes a village. I need my village to please help me."
Authorities said Gladney was shot just before noon on New Year's Day in the 1600 block of South 17th Street. She was taken to HSHS St. John's Hospital where she later died from her injuries.
No arrests have been made, and police have not announced any suspects at this time. The shooting is being investigated as a homicide.
A spokesperson for GoFundMe verified the campaign.

title: Springfield Flea Market among 5 things to do this weekend in the area

content:
If you are looking for something to do this weekend, there's plenty to do in the Springfield area this weekend.
Here are five things to do.
Springfield Theatre Center
What: The Springfield Theater Center is offering Springfield this weekend an event of comedy, love and fireworks in "You Can't Take It With You." Directed by Kim Shafer, this three-act play takes place in busy New York with an eccentric family consisting of a fireworks expert to a ballet master. When the daughter of the family falls for her boss on Wall Street, chaos ensues, and the question remains to be answered: what matters more than money? Premiered in 1936, the play was one of the most popular of its time and went on to win the 1937 Pulitzer Prize for Drama as well as an Academy Award for its film version in 1939.

Wicked Week at Bloom Wine Bar
What: Starting Wednesday but running until Saturday, Bloom is hosting a trip to the Emerald City with wine tastings and floral arrangement classes. While Wednesday and Thursday focus on floral arrangement classes, Friday is a Wicked Wine Tasting featuring seven wines and pairings. Saturday will be a Wicked Women Pop-Up party featuring women in the community who defy gravity with music, cocktails and special vendors for every witch.

Springfield Flea Market

Tuesday, Jan. 21
Girls Basketball
Anna Weber, Pleasant Plains: The junior forward poured in 21 points in a 53-21 win over Pawnee to advance to the Sangamon County Tournament championship game on Thursday at 7 p.m. Bailey Leach and Madison Burke contributed nine and seven points, respectively. Monday, Jan. 20

Lanphier 65, Waukegan 61: Lanphier erased a nine-point halftime deficit and senior guard JaiQuan Holman scored a game-high 31 points in the finale of the MLK Showcase at Lober-Nika Gymnasium.

Tyjuan Hunter delivered a game-best 28 points on 8 of 17 shooting and was 11-for-15 from the foul line for Chicago Hope.

A 22-10 third quarter for Eisenhower opened up a 48-35 lead heading into the final period. Antoine Hunter was the other player in double digits for Calvary with 10 points.

title: Protestors in Springfield marched on Inauguration Day against the new administration
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Around 50 protesters braved the bitter cold Monday to make their voice heard on Inauguration Day.
content:
Around 50 protesters braved the bitter cold Monday to make their voice heard on Inauguration Day.The Party for Socialism and Liberation mainly organized the event, though they were joined by the Prairie Liberation Center, Students for Socialism UIUC, Students for Socialism EIU, Graduate Employees Organization at UIUC, and Springfield Families for Ceasefire, among others.
The group met within The Wakery at 5 W. Old State Capitol Plaza. After people spoke to the crowd inside, the group marched downtown, including past the capitol, around 2:30 p.m.
Protestors carried picket-signs containing a variety of messages, and they chanted. A person led them with a megaphone.
The event was billed in a press release as a fighting back and a protest to defeat 'Trump's extreme right-wing billionaire agenda.'
Marches were organized across the U.S. in protest against the incoming administration.
What all were they protesting?
Organizer Derek Biles, one of the organizers with the PSL, told the SJ-R that the point of the gathering was not specifically to be 'anti-Trump' but rather to provide direction, encouragement, and coordination for organizers to operate within the second Trump administration.
'So rather than being anti-Trump, hopefully it's more pro-working class and laying out sort of a road map for the future beyond what the Democratic party can provide, which is very little,' he said.
Who were the speakers?
One of the speakers was Salem Addison King, a University of Illinois-Springfield student who aims to support and to organize people in his community. King said he saw the impact from President Donald Trump's first presidency on people he cared about, but he was a teen at that time and less politically inclined.
'Back then, I wasn't really able to do anything about it -- both because of me being a teenager and because of a lack of personal development. This time, I'm not going to let that happen again. I'm going to make sure we have a strong enough community here to protect the people of Springfield, Decatur, Champaign, and just protect as many people as we can,' King said.
King is an officer with the Central Illinois Democratic Socialists of America, and he studies environmental science at the UIS.
'Speaking as someone who was 13 years old and had just become part of a queer friend group when this [expletive] was elected the first time… you should be worried,' he told the crowd, adding that the incoming administration will bring dangers surrounding climate change.

title: Trump's sweeping pardon of Jan. 6 defendants includes two men from Springfield area
author: Steven Spearie
description: A Springfield man found guilty of breaching the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, was among the 1,500 or so people President Donald Trump pardoned Monday.
content:
A Springfield man found guilty of breaching the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, was among the 1,500 or so people President Donald Trump pardoned shortly after his inauguration Monday.
Thomas B. Adams Jr. has already served his sentence for obstruction of an official proceeding and aiding and abetting entering, both felonies, and remaining in a restricted building or grounds, a misdemeanor.
He was found guilty during a stipulated bench trial on Jan. 31, 2023.
Also pardoned was Shane Jason Woods of Divernon.
The Associated Press reported that Trump "pardoned, commuted the prison sentences or vowed to dismiss the cases" of all those charged with crimes in the Jan. 6 riot.
Nearly 1,600 people were charged with various crimes, from misdemeanor trespassing to assaulting police officers with weapons. According to the Justice Department, about 1,270 had been convicted and 1,100 had been sentenced.
Former Proud Boys leader Henry 'Enrique' Tarrio and Oath Keepers founder Stewart Rhodes were among those who received clemency from Trump. They were released from federal prisons on Tuesday.
U.S. Senate Minority Whip Dick Durbin, D-Ill., called Trump's action "a national embarrassment."
In a 2023 interview with The State Journal-Register, Adams said he traveled to Washington, D.C. because it was supposed to be "an Occupy Movement, like Occupy Wall Street." Adams said he voted for Trump and didn't believe "there was 100% legitimacy with the vote" won by President Joe Biden in 2020.
Adams and another man from Springfield, Roy Nelson Franklin, listened to Trump's talk on the Ellipse, near the White House, on Jan. 6 and afterwards followed the crowd towards the Capitol "because that's where everybody else was going."
Adams entered the Capitol through the parliamentarian door, which is a fire door. He admitted walking among Senators' desks and while on the Senate floor, took photos with his cell phone while carrying a Trump flag.
Adams said in the interview that he wouldn't "change anything" he did that day.
Franklin died on Oct. 15, 2023, two months before he was set to plead guilty.
Woods, who also goes by Shane Castleman, pleaded guilty to charges of assaulting a law enforcement officer and a media member during the breach and was sentenced to four-and-a-half years in prison.
Woods is in Sangamon County Jail on first-degree murder charges for his part in a fatal wrong-way collision on Interstate 55 near Springfield on Nov. 8, 2022. His jury trial is set to begin April 28.
According to court documents, Woods knocked a female U.S. Capitol Police officer off her feet by lowering his shoulder and ramming into her. It sent her crashing into a bicycle barricade.
Woods also tossed around media equipment and tackled a Reuters photojournalist, knocking him to the ground and causing him to drop his camera.
Deborah Anthony, professor and chair of the legal studies department at the University of Illinois Springfield and director of its pre-law center, said a pardon doesn't erase or expunge the conviction or clear a person's record, nor does it indicate any determination of innocence.
"It is more like a presidential granting of forgiveness for the crime," Anthony said. "What it accomplishes for a person who has already been released is the removal of any later consequences for the conviction, such as the ability to vote, possess firearms, hold office or sit on a jury."

title: Day 1 recap: Spartans go Rollen to a wild win over SHG in City Tournament opener
author: Ryan Mahan
description: Southeast led for just 1.6 seconds in the game as the City Tournament opened with a pair of girls basketball games on Wednesday. See how they won.
content:
Ja'Maria Rollen will remember that moment for the rest of her life.
With 3.6 seconds left in a tie game, her Southeast girls basketball teammates were on attempt No. 2 trying to inbound the ball underneath the Spartans' own basket. The first try was deflected out of bounds by a Sacred Heart-Griffin defender.
Who was Southeast senior Chloe Crawford going to look to pass the ball? Zaria Weston, who had 14 points? Navehua Collier, who had 11?
Instead, it was Rollen streaking down to the right of the lane. She snuck past her SHG defender and Crawford found her for the layup. With 1.6 on the clock, her following free throw gave No. 3 seed Southeast a 41-38 win over No. 2 SHG on the opening night of the City Tournament at the Bank of Springfield Center on Wednesday.
Rollen finished with just five points, but the last three are worth a lifetime of memories.
'I'm not going to lie: I was hoping it didn't come to me, it did and what happened, happened,' said Rollen, who was still basking in the glow from the celebration. 'I'm glad for the outcome. I knew it was in when it was leaving my hands.'
Crawford passed the ball to Rollen then quickly got into position to take a possible pass.
'It means everything for us to get started on the next part of our season,' Crawford said of the exciting finish. 'It keeps momentum good and the motivation to keep going. I think we really showed who we are as a team, especially winning in the final seconds tonight.'
The Southeast locker room was loud and in a celebratory mood following the win. It wasn't just because of Rollen's heroics or for an upset win based on the tournament's seeds: SHG beat Southeast 62-36 on the Spartans' home floor on Jan. 11.
'We didn't feel like we played our best game when we lost by (26),' second-year Southeast coach Jasmin Woolfolk said. 'We got defeated early with a couple of bad calls and we learned from that. All this time, we worked on that — not just for this game, but just every game. We cannot lose focus just because things don't go our way. We've been talking about it, we've been working on it and the girls stuck to the game plan that we've been prepping on all week.'
That defeat was fresh on the minds of the Spartans (13-8, 1-0 City) before, during and especially after the game.
Collier said the team's mindset was different before the game even began, which saw SHG take a 2-0 lead when Southeast was hit with a pre-game technical foul because the Spartans wore the wrong uniforms.
'(Confidence) kicked in when we first got on the court ... in warm-ups before the game even started,' Collier said.
SHG first-year coach Dave Andrews said Southeast kept its composure, and that was part of the Spartans' undoing in the earlier matchup.
'They were more composed this time,' Andrews said. 'They got a little rattled the last time we played them, and I knew coming in that they were going to give us fits. They are a good team; very fast, they like to drive a lot.'
On Wednesday, SHG led 19-6 early in the second quarter and either led or were tied all game until Rollen's three-point play. The Cyclones opened up a 28-21 lead with 4 minutes, 12 seconds left in the third quarter, then again had a seven-point lead, 38-31, with 3:44 remaining in the game.
Crawford jump-started the Spartans' final run with a basket 16 seconds later before Weston knocked down a 3-pointer from the wind with 2:41 left to pull Southeast within 38-36. With 39 seconds left, Collier tied the game with a jumper in the paint.
After Southeast's first inbound attempt, Andrews had a feeling the Spartans would change their strategy and instead try to find Rollen.
'We knew they were looking to get it to Navehua (on the first try), we knew they were looking to get it in her hand,' Andrews said. 'We also knew Chloe would come back in (after the inbound pass) and hit that outside shot. It's their go-to shot for what I've seen. The next one ... I kind of knew it was coming to (Rollen) because they saw what we did the previous (time) and she just made the play.'
Sophie Murphy led SHG (11-13 overall, 0-1 City) with 13 points while Izzy Hassebrock had 12.
The boys tournament begins on Thursday with No. 2 SHG against No. 3 Lanphier at 6 p.m., followed by No. 1 Springfield High and No. 4 Southeast. The Senators are looking for their first boys title since 2009.
No. 1 SPRINGFIELD HIGH 70, No. 4 LANPHIER 20: In the second game on Wednesday, Keziah Toran led the Senators with 12 points and Aniyah Rhinehouse added 11 as the Senators cruised to the victory. Springfield led 42-4 at halftime. Lovely Jackson led Lanphier with 10 points.

title: Fired-up Lions: Lanphier rallies past No. 1 Springfield, will play for outright City title
author: Ryan Mahan
description: Blake Turner might be the master of using any small perceived slight as motivation for his Lanphier boys basketball team and it worked on Friday as the Lions beat SHS in the City Tournament.
content:
Blake Turner might be the master of using any small perceived slight as motivation for his Lanphier boys basketball team.
Whether it's an off-hand remark, a seed that's lower than he thought his team deserved or even an opposing coach trying to talk positively about his own team, Turner looks for anything to hang on the proverbial bulletin board.
On Friday, Turner had his third-seeded Lions prepped for its City Tournament game with that motivation against top-seeded Springfield High. In an article earlier this week in The State Journal-Register, Springfield High coach Marques Warfield said he believed his team was the best in the city, even if the individuals themselves may not have that claim.
'Me and my staff and my players took offense to that,' Turner said after Lanphier beat SHS 54-48 at the Bank of Springfield Center. 'We feel like we have the best team: we have the best record, we're the defending city champions, and we wanted to make a statement tonight.'
Turner said he had no issue with Warfield's comments, and understood their meaning, but he used it nonetheless.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
'I think that a lot of times coaches are willing to say any and everything to try to motivate their players,' Turner added. 'I'm just going to attribute it to that. But it was definitely bulletin-board material for us, and we were fired up for 32 minutes tonight.'
If Lanphier made a statement, it was senior Shaunassey Hatchett Jr., who had the exclamation mark.
Hatchett was on a mission, especially in the second quarter when the Lions' captain threw down three dunks en route to a 21-point, nine-rebound stellar performance to put Lanphier on the precipice of a second-straight City Tournament championship. All Lanphier (14-8 overall, 2-0 City) has to do is beat Southeast (2-19, 0-2 City) in the 4:45 p.m. game on Saturday to lay claim to another outright title.
'There's always people that have a role,' Hatchett said. 'Some people have good games, some people have bad games like me — I've had plenty of bad games. They pick me up and they put me on their back. So, I feel like if something like that going on (with other players), I need to put them on my back as a captain and really help us lead us to a championship game.'
Soriano Hayes battled through foul trouble for most of the game and finished with 10 points while JaiQuan Holman finished with 12 but was 2-for-10 shooting from the field. However, the senior and reigning SJ-R Large School Player of the Year was 8-for-10 at the free-throw line.
Warfield said Holman's impact went beyond the box score.
'They have who I think is the best guard in the city, and he didn't necessarily wow you offensively, but he was clutch,' Warfield said. 'He was seasoned, and he did what a senior was supposed to do. He went to the line ... and he didn't force himself into the game or none of that nature. Just stayed composed, kept his team composed.'
Nearly midway through the third quarter, Mayango Jallah gave Springfield High its biggest lead, 36-28. Holman completed a three-point play with 4 minutes, 54 seconds left in the period before Amari Anderson found his way into the scoring column with a 10-foot floater. Anderson had a putback basket with 4:06 left in the fourth to give Lanphier a 46-41 win.
Anderson agreed that his floater gave the Lions a needed spark.
'I felt like it was, too,' Anderson said. 'I just got to where I could get my shot off and help my team, then hurried to get back on defense because Springfield (likes) to run.'
Springfield's undoing came in part from its 20 turnovers, even though the Senators held a 21-14 edge in points off those giveaways. The Senators also went seven of 14 at the free-throw line.
Warfield said his team needs to clean up some of those mistakes.
'Man, we had a lot of mental lapses, like just throughout the game on both ends,' Warfield said. 'Offensively we had mental lapses, taking ill-advised shots, just not really sticking to the gameplan. Defensively, not making the proper rotations.
'Key closeouts that we missed, like we gave up multiple free-throw rebounds. We didn't hustle after the 50-50 balls. Defense is something that we take pride in and is a staple for our program, and we didn't live up to the standard.'
Warfield has plenty to improve on before the Senators face No. 2 Sacred Heart-Griffin in the City Tournament finale on Saturday.
'Listen, if you can't protect the basketball and you don't have a good guard play, you'll lose every time,' Warfield said. 'For us, we go 50% from the free throw line, we have 20 turnovers, and we didn't do the things that I just mentioned as far as the intangibles. So, that's a recipe for destruction.'
Noah Wade led Springfield High with 13 points while teammate Valor Komolafe had 12 with eight rebounds.
Sacred Heart-Griffin 56, Southeast 30
Guard Myles Montgomery scored the first two points of the game, and he finished with a game-high 17 as the Cyclones improved to 1-1 in the tournament.
Montgomery made a 3-pointer in the first period and had seven points. His fast start was joined by sophomore guard Terrion Wallace, who hit two 3s and scored all six of his total points in the period. SHG, the No. 2 seed, led 15-10 after one quarter.
Montgomery described one of the challenges he faces with his game.
'Being confident in myself because my mentality is, if I put it up it's going in,' Montgomery said. 'I've got good teammates around me to pass me the ball. It's good all the way around.'
After losing to third seed Lanphier 62-56 on the first night of the tournament, Montgomery explained the Cyclones' game plan.
'Playing with energy,' he said. 'As long as we play with effort, we play with energy, and I think it's hard to beat us. Once we fire into that energy, it hypes up people that are not usually hyped so we get going and that's when we are really dangerous.'
Southeast had an inkling of energy too, when the Spartans got within one point while holding SHG scoreless in the second quarter until center Chuck Lanier made a pair of free throws to give the Cyclones a 17-14 lead with 1 minute, 10 seconds remaining in the half. SHG finally closed the half on an 8-0 run for a 23-14 halftime advantage.
It was all SHG in the second half as Montgomery scored 10 more, including eight in the third stanza. Lanier went 6-for-7 from the foul line and finished with 12 points.
'It's really a blessing to come out and play in front of everybody in the city,' Montgomery said. 'It's what all kids want to do when they get into high school.'
Aaron Holman and Josiah Turner led Southeast with seven points apiece and point guard Inigo Angeles added six. Turner finished with nine rebounds and Holman had six boards.

title: Three the hard way: SHG beats SHS to force three-way tie for Girls City Tournament trophy
author: Bill Welt
description: Sacred Heart-Griffin found itself down eight with 5:45 left, but went on a big run to beat Springfield High and force a three-way tie for the Girls City title.
content:
A stunning 17-0 run catapulted Sacred Heart-Griffin to a share of the City girls basketball title at the Bank of Springfield Center on Saturday.
The Cyclones trailed Springfield High 37-29 with under six minutes left in the fourth quarter before reversing the tide with a spell of 3s and steals to escape with a 49-40 victory.
SHG (13-13) won a share of the crown with SHS and Southeast. Springfield High (13-10) clinched its second straight title following Friday's 51-39 win over Southeast. The Spartans (14-9) won their first City trophy since 2008.
Hassebrock, Mantei trigger SHG comeback
Senior guard Izzy Hassebrock converted her only 3 before sophomore guard Alyse Mantei drained back-to-back 3s for her only points to grab the lead with under four minutes remaining.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
Hassebrock, The State Journal-Register's back-to-back Large School Girls Golfer of the Year, said Mantei makes all her 3s in practice.
'Alyse is a great young player,' Hassebrock said. 'I love her so much, I'm so glad she got to see some playing time and she definitely did her part.
'She's a really good shooter for our team and here at the BOS Center with all of these fans, it's such a difficult atmosphere and to come off the bench and bang 3s like that, I was really happy for her.'
Hassebrock led the Cyclones with 14 points, while senior center Sophie Murphy had 12 points. Hassebrock also had six of the team's 13 steals. Senior guard Reese Watson summoned five points and four steals.
'We definitely wanted this one because we have four seniors on this team,' Hassebrock said. 'It's our last City tournament, so we just turned up that intensity. We saw the light at the end of the tunnel, we started to get ahead and we just started jumping those passes and getting them a little flustered.'
SHS senior guard Keziah Toran converted two 3s and finished with a team-high 12 points. Senior forward Ariana Williams supplied 10 points and six rebounds. Freshman guard Morgan Leininger delivered three 3s for nine points off the bench.
The loss ended the Senators' seven-game winning streak.
'We've got some tough young ladies, we'll bounce back,' SHS coach Brad Scheffler said. 'It's a tough one for the seniors and their last City game, but they'll bounce back and we'll get going on Tuesday again.'
Southeast savors moment
Southeast opened the tournament by nicking SHG on a Ja'Maria Rollen and-1 with 1.6 seconds left and ended the week with a 38-27 win over Lanphier.
It is Southeast's 12 th title overall.
'Even though it was a three-way tie, I feel like it's a good motivator for next year to take it outright,' Southeast coach Jasmin Woolfolk said. 'But shout out to all the teams, everybody played well and played hard. It feels good.'
Junior guard Zaria Weston led the Spartans with 13 points and nine rebounds. Rollen added six points as a reserve. Lanphier's Shawntiana Walker had 10 points.
Woolfolk turned to the bench to close out the final minutes of the game. They held their own, Woolfolk said.
'I know at times I may not play a lot of kids, but we're really deep,' Woolfolk said. 'Everybody's coming to practice and works hard. The way I like to coach is next man up. When your number is called, I want you to get out on the floor and do what you have to do and be able to carry the team.
'We're only as strong as the weakest player. I like to say from 1-15, 15-1, we are all together, all for one, one for all.'

title: Music's biggest night: Where to watch the red carpet for the 2025 Grammy Awards
author: Amaris Encinas
description: The Recording Academy and other outlets will stream exclusive Grammys content, including red-carpet arrivals hours before the awards show kicks off.
content:
Music's best and brightest will make their red-carpet descent before the 67th Annual Grammy Awards, where excellence in the music industry across genres and the globe is recognized.
Despite the ongoing devastation brought to Southern California by multiple wildfires in recent weeks, the Recording Academy announced earlier this month that the star-studded awards will go on.
"The 67th Annual GRAMMY Awards will carry a renewed sense of purpose: raising additional funds to support wildfire relief efforts and honoring the bravery and dedication of first responders who risk their lives to protect ours," the Recording Academy shared in a statement.
This year's Grammys will be held on Sunday, Feb. 2 at the Crypto.com Arena, formerly known as the Staples Center in downtown Los Angeles.
Before the awards show kicks off, heavy hitters like Beyoncé and Taylor Swift, and even newcomers have the chance to strut and pose on the red carpet in their designer regalia. The practice has become a highly anticipated component of most, if not all, major awards shows.
Here's how and where to watch the pre-show telecast, including all red-carpet arrivals.
When are this year's Grammy Awards?
" Music's biggest night" will take place Sunday, Feb. 2 at Crypto.com Arena in downtown Los Angeles. The awards show will go from 8 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. EST, or 5 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. PST.
Grammys red carpet: Where to watch, stream
Various news outlets will offer red carpet coverage on Grammys day.
The Recording Academy will offer exclusive Grammys content, including interviews and red-carpet arrivals that will be livestreamed by the Recording Academy at live.GRAMMY.com.
E! News will be hosting "E! Live From the Red Carpet," which can be watched live on cable television or through live streaming provider FuboTV. The Associated Press will also stream the three-hour red-carpet show, which can be streamed live on YouTube and APNews.com.
The awards show is set to air live on CBS from 8 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. ET/ 5 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. PT.
Paramount+ subscribers with the Showtime add-on can also stream the 2025 Grammys live as it airs on CBS. And Paramount+ subscribers with any plan can stream it the day after it airs. Live streaming services that include CBS in their lineup, like Hulu + Live TV, YouTube TV and FuboTV.
