title: Settled-in Cyclones: SHG uses big plays to erase deficit in win over Jacksonville
author: Ryan Mahan
description: Jacksonville ate up clock in the first half and led after 24 minutes, but SHG found its winning recipe with big third quarter.
content:
Now, Sacred Heart-Griffin's football team has a two-running back system.
Trent Caldwell started the season as the Cyclones' quarterback. Now, he shares the running duties with Mikey Groesch while sophomore Cam Brinkman has taken over as QB.
It seems to have worked.
Brinkman's back-up outing last week in a 43-22 nonconference win over Mascoutah gave SHG coach John Allison the confidence he needed to make the switch. On Friday, the sophomore got his first start at quarterback and Caldwell turned into a running back and a receiver out of the slot.
While the first half was a mixed bag for the Cyclones, Caldwell and Groesch each scored a pair of touchdowns in the third quarter to give Sacred Heart-Griffin a 35-10 win over Jacksonville in the Central State Eight Conference's west division opener for both teams.
'Credit to our offensive line, opening up those holes for me,' Groesch said. 'We just came out and played well that second half. Our mentality was just completely different up front. The first half, we were a little timid; the second half, we came out strong.'
Groesch sprinted for two touchdowns, covering 67 and 51 yards, totaling 120 yards on just three carries. Caldwell carried the ball nine times, gaining 106 yards, which included a 68-yard touchdown run and a 4-yard score.
Clock management
SHG took a 7-0 lead with 3 minutes, 41 seconds left in the first quarter. With Jacksonville's offense back on the field for its second time, junior quarterback Braden Hutchison completed two third-down passes as the Crimsons mainly focused on its ground game. Just 89 seconds into the second period, freshman running back Jeremiah Jackson scored a 5-yard touchdown to pull Jacksonville into a 7-7 tie.
After the Cyclones were forced to punt twice, the Crimsons ate nearly six minutes off the clock and senior kicker Brandon Sims kicked a 29-yard field goal to give Jacksonville (2-1, 0-1 CS8 West) a 10-7 lead with 42 seconds left in the half.
On paper, Sacred Heart-Griffin (2-1 overall, 1-0 CS8 West) trailed 10-7 for just 61 seconds. But with halftime accounting for nearly a 20-minute stoppage, the deficit probably felt like it lasted forever for the Cyclones' players.
Coach John Allison said they didn't change much during the stoppage. Instead, he spent the time trying to reassure the players they would be OK.
'You've got to be assignment strong,' Allison said. 'You can't worry about anything but your job against that offense, and I think we had some guys who were not doing that early and we did in the second half.'
Off to the races
SHG got the opening kick to start the second half. Two plays later, Groesch turned on the jets to sprint to the end zone for a 67-yard score. When the Cyclones got the ball back on a Jacksonville punt, it was Caldwell's turn for a highlight-reel run for a 68-yard score.
'We said we had to play like we play,' Caldwell said of the halftime discussion. 'We can't be anybody: we're SHG and that's what we have to play like. We play hard; we play physical. I was talking with my guys, Mikey and Cameron, the rest of the team, and said we need to come out and punch them in the mouth and we did that. I can't be more proud of them.'
When Groesch got his second TD, on a 51-yard first play of the possession, it gave SHG three touchdowns in a four-offensive snap span.
'Second half, we gave them three big plays up the middle and then, you can see the wind kind of go out of the sails,' Jacksonville coach Mark Grounds said. 'That's what happens sometimes with young kids. There's still some positives in the second half, but we've got to learn how to not put ourselves in that situation. If we do that, it's going to make us a better team down the stretch.'
Brinkman's first start
Brinkman finished 5-for-11 with 79 yards and a touchdown in his first start. Allison said the stats don't tell the entire story.
'Cam in the passing game, he threw a couple of great balls that should've been caught,' SHG's second-year head coach said. 'He did just a fine job and I think he's going to be great (but) we've got to help him out a little bit in catching those balls.
'Him in the passing game will give us a little more vertical stretch going forward. If we can stretch the defense a bit, it's going to help our run game even more.'
Allison knows the sophomore still has plenty of room to grow, but Brinkman's ability to meet the moment caught Allison's eye during the Class 3A Lanphier Regional basketball tournament earlier this year when the then-freshman scored 14 points as SHG upset Lincoln in the regional semifinals.
'I just go out there and try to play my game and block out what people say,' Brinkman said. 'It doesn't really get in my head. I just focus on me, do my thing.'

title: Springfield's newest sports park should open in 2025. Here's what to expect
author: Claire Grant
description: The Scheels Sports Complex will be a place for basketball, volleyball, soccer, turf training and more. Here's what's in store.
content:
SCHEELS Sports Park is one step closer to opening, and work on the planned 70-acre multisport outdoor and indoor sports park is now being headed by a general manager new to Springfield, but not the business.
Meet Brandon Doherty, who SCHEELS Sports Park developers and The Sports Facilities Companies announced on Sept. 10 will oversee operations for the park.
Doherty has a master's degree in recreation administration from Aurora University and has served as an instructor at the Outdoor Wisconsin Leadership School and helped launch a leadership school in Carlisle, Pennsylvania.
Doherty comes to Springfield from Starkville, Mississippi, where he served as the general manager of the Cornerstone Sports Complex. Before SCHEELS, Doherty has spent over a decade as a director, educator and coach in the recreation administration industry.
'I am thrilled to be in Springfield, and I'm already rolling up my sleeves to help make this the best sports park in the region,' said Doherty. 'I have seen how these sport complexes can transform communities, and I am excited to help in all the ways I can getting things set up so we're ready to play in 2025.'
Doherty is joining the site post-groundbreaking. Since last year, many local crews have been working hard to prepare the ground and install more than two miles of underground water main, storm and sanitary sewer.
Construction already has started on a new hotel, Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott, at Legacy Pointe. It will be located next to the SCHEELS Sports Complex. The multi-million-dollar hotel will have 91 rooms with amenities for families and business travelers.
This month and as long as weather permits, crews will begin work on the foundation for the Springfield Clinic Dome, parking lots, fields and electric work, according to SCHEELS. The dome is a 190,000 square-foot indoor dome which can be configured into a basketball court, a volleyball court, soccer field, or turf training area. The outdoor facilities will include six lighted turf fields set up for a variety of sports including baseball, and two full size football fields.
Springfield area athletes and their families should anticipate usage of the DOME and outdoor fields after their completion, which is planned for fall 2025. Tournaments will be planned to begin in spring 2026.
'We are so grateful for all of the work that continues to happen in this remarkable public-private partnership to make this sports park a reality for Springfield,' Mayor Misty Buscher said. 'I believe this sports park and the families it will bring to our beautiful city will be a boost to our local businesses, economy, and we will all get to enjoy everything that this sports park will bring to the capital city.'

title: Fall is approaching, here's what to do with your final summer harvests
author: Channing Fullaway-Johnson
description: While it may be a bit warmer this week, fall is still quickly approaching. Here are some ideas for what to do with your summer harvests.
content:
We've seen signs throughout the past week that summer is coming to an end, and fall is quickly approaching. As much as I love the fall — with watching the leaves change to vibrant warm colors of orange, yellow and red, drinking mulled spiced cider and enjoying the warm spices that influence our food and drink choices — my garden is as happy and thriving as ever. This sparks the question of what can I do with my final harvests?
There are many ways to preserve your harvests of fruits and vegetables in the forms of jams, jellies, pickles and canned foods, but an often-ignored preservation option is the freezer, particularly with tomatoes. While other approaches have advantages, freezing is very simple and quick, and it requires less knowhow and equipment.
Don't get me wrong — there is nothing better than a fresh tomato, but freezing will give you a chance to make spaghetti sauce in January that tastes like you just picked the tomatoes yesterday. They lose the structure for slicing for sandwiches, but they are an excellent choice if you want to use them in stews and sauces throughout the harsh winter months.
Instead of puréeing and canning, you may put them directly into freezer bags. Yes, that's right! It's an easy, yet clever method of preserving tomatoes. Months later, their vibrant flavor and delightful acidity will still be evident, giving you the impression that you've traveled back in time to the summer months. To make things even easier later, cut an 'X' shape on the bottom of each tomato with a paring knife. This will allow them to peel quickly. As the tomato starts to thaw, the skin will peel right off.
Summer squash freezes very well, and there are several easy ways to do so. If you want to sauté, roast or add to a stew, chop into thin, medium-to-large rounds or chunks. Next, blanch the squash to soften the flesh and quicken the cooking process later. To blanch, submerge the pieces in salted, boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain the squash, and immediately place it in an ice bath to halt the cooking process. Freeze in a single layer on sheet pans, and then place the pieces in freezer-safe bags once frozen.
Another great way is to shred the squash using the biggest holes on a box grater or the shredding attachment on a food processor. Squeeze the excess liquid from the squash with a cheese cloth, and pack it into freezer-safe bags. It is handy to premeasure the shredded squash in each bag, so you know exactly what you have for your recipes later. This is perfect for zucchini bread, fritters, frittatas, cornbread, casseroles, sauces and even soups.
Don't forget to wash all your produce and to label and date the freezer bags! Here are a few easy recipes using frozen or fresh vegetables.
Tomato Sauce
Ingredients:
2½ lb. fresh ripe tomatoes (or whole frozen tomatoes, thawed)
2 tablespoons tomato paste
2 ounces white wine
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
1 small onion, chopped
4 garlic cloves, minced
Salt and red pepper flakes (to taste)
1 tablespoon sugar
2 tablespoon chopped fresh basil
Directions
Take your frozen tomatoes from the freezer and allow them to mostly thaw. Using the X-sliced end, peel your tomato. For each tomato, place it on cutting board, cut in half, remove seeds and chop remaining tomato pulp.
If using fresh tomatoes, bring a large pot of water to a boil. With a paring knife, cut an 'X' shape on the bottom of each tomato.
Set up an ice bath by putting several cups of ice in a large bowl and pouring in a cup or two of cold water. Set ice bath aside. Once water boils, carefully lower tomatoes into boiling water with a slotted spoon. Boil for 30 seconds. Remove tomatoes and place in ice water for several minutes. Once tomatoes are cool enough to handle, peel the skins off. For each tomato, place it on cutting board, cut in half, remove seeds and chop remaining tomato.
To make tomato sauce, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large, heavy pot over medium heat. Add onion. Cook, stirring often, until tender (about 5 minutes).
Add garlic. Cook, stirring until fragrant (about a minute), and add tomato paste. Stir for another minute. Then add the chopped tomatoes, salt, red pepper flakes, wine and sugar. Increase heat to medium-high. When tomatoes are bubbling briskly, stir and reduce heat to medium. Simmer, stirring often, until tomatoes have cooked down and are beginning to stick to pan (about 30 minutes, depending on consistency). Stir in chopped basil, taste and adjust seasoning.
Zucchini Cornbread
Ingredients:
½ cup yellow cornmeal
1 ½ cups all-purpose flour
⅓ cup granulated sugar
2 teaspoons baking powder
¼ teaspoon baking soda
¾ teaspoon salt
1 cup buttermilk or milk
2 eggs, lightly beaten
4 tablespoons (half a stick) salted butter, melted
2 cups unpeeled shredded, drained zucchini
Directions
Preheat the oven to 350F. Lightly grease a 9-inch square baking pan with cooking spray. Set aside.
In a large bowl, stir together the dry ingredients cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Make a well in the dry ingredients, and add the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and shredded zucchini. Stir just until combined.
Spread the batter in the prepared pan and bake for 30-35 minutes until the top springs back lightly to the touch and/or a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Channing Fullaway-Johnson is the culinary coordinator at Lincoln Land Community College.

title: CS8 football notebook: Rochester has options to replace injured Zulauf
author: Ryan Mahan
description: Friday's 28-10 nonconference loss to Cardinal Ritter was costly for Rochester in more than just the win-loss column, but Rockets have options to replace injured QB.
content:
Rochester coach Derek Leonard was forced to pivot during Friday's Week 2 28-10 loss to St. Louis Cardinal Ritter at Rocket Booster Stadium when quarterback Bryan Zulauf went down with a leg injury.
The Rockets (1-1) got the news they feared: Zulauf, a senior who helped Rochester win its ninth state championship in last year's Class 4A state title game, is out for the season with a leg injury.
On Friday, Tanner Beal came in as Zulauf's backup, hit fellow junior Kaiden Stout for a 75-yard touchdown pass and finished 6-for-12 with 93 yards, one TD and one interception.
Leonard said he's been giving looks in this week's practice to three QB options: Beal, senior Eli Carlson and sophomore J.P. Leonard.
Derek Leonard has used two-quarterback systems before and found success. But as of Wednesday, the Rockets' nine-time state champion coach wasn't quite sure how the signal-caller position would look going forward, including in Friday's road Central State Eight Conference game at Lincoln (2-0).
'We're playing a few people there,' Derek Leonard said. 'Tanner's going to be playing some defense still. We've got Eli Carlson, we've got J.P. Leonard.
'I don't know who we're going to play, to be brutally honest. Tanner's definitely going to play some, but we're going to play Eli and J.P ... maybe by committee some, like we've done in the past. Tanner did a great job coming in last week.'
Speaking of Carlson, Leonard said his senior has done everything's that been asked of him.
'I think Eli Carlson has done well,' Leonard said. 'He's always been that Swiss Army knife for us. Defensively, I think he's done a really good job and surprised us the first two weeks. Obviously playing running back and receiver and a little quarterback, I think he's done a great job.'
Leonard also had positive things to say about Lincoln coach Matt Silkowski, who last season ended the Railers' playoff drought which dated back to 1984.
'Offensively, they've changed a little bit, but coach (Silkowski) does such a great job,' Leonard said. 'I'd say they're maybe a little better defensively than last year. They're a legit 2-0 and we're going to their place. Coach has done a great job turning that thing around. They have a bunch of seniors. I think they're as good as last year.'
Defense has been Jacksonville's key to success
Jacksonville coach Mark Grounds has liked what he's seen through the Crimsons' 2-0 start, but the CS8's most-senior coach knows that he still wants to see big steps forward.
The Crimsons can do that at SHG on Friday.
'We've played some pretty good defense so far,' Grounds said. 'We've played some new kids; they're starting to jell a little bit. We'll face a more veteran squad with (SHG) this week.
'We faced a traditional I-formation team in Week 1 and a spread team with some athletes in Week 2. I think we'll face a complete team in Week 3, but I like what our defense is starting to jell as: our communication, our enthusiasm, our hustle. I think that the coaches have done a really good job with the game plans through two weeks and we continue to get better.'
After Jacksonville's 4-5 record precluded the Crimsons from the postseason last season, Grounds knew the path to the playoffs this year would depend on his defense preventing big gains.
'We've been better tacklers through two weeks than we were last year, and that was a point of emphasis,' Grounds said. 'We're concentrating hard on making sure that we don't have any alignment errors that beat us pre-snap.
'We've got a really good pursuit and hustle mentality with this squad and that's what it takes to start laying the foundation of a good defense. They're doing the work in the film room; they're doing the work on the practice field. We've got a long way to go to be where we want to be, but we feel we've taken some positive steps from last year.'
SHG coach John Allison credited the Crimsons on both sides of the ball and said this will be a challenging team to face.
'They've got about three kids who are really quick kids who can score from just about anywhere on the field,' Allison said. 'Those kids are quick on defense and, I don't think I've seen a team's (defense) line that averages 270 to 310 in quite a while. They're big up front, they've got those skill kids, they love to run the ball. They'd be happy to get four yards a play and they'll grind it out and keep the ball from you. That helps their defense quite a bit.'
Cyclones' get Caldwell back
Breathe easy, SHG fans. Quarterback Trent Caldwell, who exited last week's 43-22 nonconference home win against Mascoutah, is fine.
'It was all just cramps,' Allison said. 'He had a hamstring and he kind of got a side pull a little bit. He's back, he's healthy, he's looked great (and) he's been running strong.
SHG's second-year coach John Allison said Caldwell suffered cramps during the game. And Allison got an infusion of optimism at the same time by watching sophomore Cam Brinkman fill in for the senior QB.
Allison said he was very happy with Brinkman's effort in that moment.
'He's a great player and from watching him on the basketball court last year, I knew at varsity quarterback, that he wouldn't be fazed by the pressure,' Allison said. 'That cemented the game (an 18-play, 96-yard drive) and he converted a couple of third downs on that drive.'
It was also a good moment for the team to get its first win under its belt with a 43-22 home victory against Mascoutah.
A look at the standings
After two weeks of nonconference play in the CS8, there are three undefeated teams, but not the usual suspects.
In the conference's six-team east division, Lincoln is 2-0 after wins over Lanphier and Southeast. Chatham Glenwood, Decatur MacArthur, Normal U-High and Rochester are all 1-1. Decatur Eisenhower is 0-2.
In the west division, Jacksonville and Springfield High are both sitting at 2-0 after the Crimsons beat Pittsfield and Eisenhower while the Senators prevailed over Champaign Central and MacArthur. Quincy Notre Dame and SHG are 1-1 while Lanphier and Southeast are still looking for their first wins.
The next five weeks will determine the conference's divisional champs, starting Friday with six CS8 games.

title: Your turn: Investing in public education means more than minimum spending
author: Dan Montgomery
description: Underfunding has long been an issue in Illinois public schools, and it's time for something to be done about it.
content:
In our ever-evolving society, education stands as the cornerstone of progress and prosperity. Yet, despite recognizing its paramount importance, we find ourselves in a perpetual cycle of underfunding, which preserves the systemic challenges that hinder our students' potential – and hits our Black, Brown, and low-income students the hardest.
Studies indicate increasing funding for education, particularly for our Black, Brown and low-income students, correlates with enhanced academic performance and higher graduation rates. It is also associated with elevated earnings and favorable life trajectories.
Established in 2017, Illinois' Evidence-Based Model (EBM) for K-12 education was designed to equitably and effectively distribute resources. However, it falls short of its promise; it is not expected to meet adequacy standards until 2040—13 years behind schedule.
Since adopting the EBM, Illinois has only provided the statutory minimum of about $350 million annually, leaving a funding gap of $2.3 billion. Amid record inflation and shrinking government grants, this funding is increasingly insufficient.
This shortfall was highlighted in the latest legislative session when minimal funding increases proved inadequate for Chicago Public Schools (CPS) and other districts across the state, underscoring a deepening crisis in educational investment as student needs grow.
This is especially troubling as Illinois ranks 37th among the 50 states in funding public education, further illustrating the systemic neglect and urgent need for reform.
Under Illinois' school funding formula, Chicago Public Schools (CPS) is owed over $1 billion per year from the state to meet adequacy standards. Elgin schools would need $219 million to reach adequacy, Peoria School District 150 would need $55 million, Cahokia CUSD 187 would need $10.5 million, Mahomet-Seymour CUSD 3 would need $14.5 million, and Carterville CUSD 5 would need $10.1 million to reach adequacy.
These districts, among many others across the state, are short-changed by inadequate state funding. Additionally, Chicago faces unique financial burdens that either disproportionately or exclusively affect CPS.
This is a pivotal moment for our lawmakers, who have the opportunity to be real heroes for our students by rectifying these disparities. Our plea to the governor and legislators is clear: we cannot afford to wait decades for adequate funding. The urgency of the situation demands immediate action to break free from this cycle of underinvestment.
We must close the gap between our well-resourced districts and those whose needs aren't yet being met. An increase beyond the mandated minimum is imperative to ensure that our schools in every district, regardless of zip code, have the resources that students need to thrive.
While this conversation often centers on PreK-12, we must not overlook the critical importance of higher education.
Western Illinois University recently announced that the university intends to layoff an undetermined number of contingent and tenure/tenure track faculty and academic support professionals.
The need for funding in our colleges and universities is desperate; last year, three state universities were forced to go on strike due to underfunding that resulted in skyrocketing tuition, program cuts and understaffing.
Decades of severe underfunding have left our state universities struggling to meet the needs of their students. To address these pressing challenges, Illinois must adopt a higher education funding formula akin to the Evidence-Based Model. Such a model would ensure that resources are allocated based on identified needs through evidence-based practices, fostering a more equitable and sustainable higher education system.
In times of fiscal constraint, investing in education is not an expense, but an investment in our future. Failure to adequately fund higher education perpetuates a cycle of inequality, hindering social mobility and economic progress.
As stewards of our state's future, we cannot afford to let another generation of students bear the brunt of underfunded public schools and unaffordable higher education.
The time for action is now. Let us rise above partisan divides and prioritize the well-being and future success of our students in every district. By investing in education today, we sow the seeds for a brighter tomorrow for all.

title: Sangamon County Board Chairman announces nomination to replace Campbell as sheriff
author: Claire Grant
description: If approved by the full county board on Wednesday, the appointment will be effective immediately with the term expiring in December 2026.
content:
A nomination is being made to fill the vacancy left by the retirement of former Sheriff Jack Campbell.
Sangamon County Board Chairman Andy Van Meter will nominate Paula Crouch to serve as sheriff at Wednesday's special county board meeting, according to Sangamon County spokesman Jeff Wilhite.
Crouch, 51, would become the county's first female sheriff.
Crouch was named a finalist with six others last week. Overall, there were 15 applicants.
According to Wilhite, interviews with the finalists began last week, with each candidate undergoing a comprehensive background check by former Seventh Judicial Circuit Judge Patrick Kelley, who conducted an extensive review before recommending Crouch for the role.
"Paula Crouch's extensive experience and deep roots in our community make her the ideal person to lead the sheriff's office," Van Meter said in a news release issued Tuesday. "As a former victim of sexual harassment and a working single mom who overcame financial difficulties, Paula knows what it is like when life knocks you down. She understands that justice is the application of human understanding to the laws designed to protect all of us from the worst of us.'
Crouch resides in rural Williams Township with her husband, Robert, and two children. Robert Crouch is the police chief of the Village of Riverton.
If approved by the full County Board on Wednesday, the appointment will be effective immediately, with the term expiring in December 2026. Crouch would be able to run in the Nov. 3, 2026 election.
The news release did not include any information on the proposed compensation for Crouch. In a call to the county, Wilhite said that information would be available at a later time.
Who is Paula Crouch?
According to the news release, Crouch is a lifelong resident of Sangamon County, graduated from Auburn High School and has dedicated nearly three decades to public service. She holds degrees from Lincoln Land Community College and Benedictine University Springfield and a master's in law enforcement and justice administration from Western Illinois University.
Before becoming a police officer, she was a Sangamon County 911 dispatcher. She later joined the Springfield Police Department in 1999, retiring in 2023 as a lieutenant.
'I am incredibly honored and humbled to have been chosen to serve as the Sheriff of Sangamon County,' Crouch said in the release. 'My career in law enforcement has given me the opportunity to work with a diverse range of people and tackle complex challenges, and I look forward to bringing those experiences to this role. Protecting the safety and well-being of our citizens will always be my top priority, and I am committed to building on the foundation of the Sheriff's Office to continue improving public safety in our county.'
Crouch held multiple roles in the Springfield Police Department, including serving as the Sangamon/Menard County Crime Stoppers Coordinator, a neighborhood patrol officer and a detective.
Crouch was also assigned to the Child Advocacy Center before her retirement, where she investigated cases of child abuse, the United States Marshals Task Force, assisting with the capture of dangerous fugitives and the Illinois Attorney General's Crimes Against Children Task Force.
Crouch's contributions to law enforcement have been recognized with numerous awards, including the William Herndon Award for plain clothes detective in 2005, the Sangamon County Advocate of the Year in 2012, and the American Red Cross Hero Award for Public Service in 2013.
In 2017, Crouch received the Abraham Lincoln Award for community service.
Since her retirement, Crouch has served as the Chief Deputy of Administration for the Sangamon County Circuit Clerk's Office.
The open seat of Sherriff
Campbell retired on Aug. 31 in the wake of the fatal shooting of Sonya Massey, a 36-year-old Black woman and mother of two children, who had called 911 about a possible prowler. Massey was shot in her own home.
Campbell had been sheriff since 2018.
Sean P. Grayson, a former Sangamon County Sheriff's deputy, faces murder charges and is in custody.
Since Aug. 31, Sangamon County Coroner Jim Allmon has been serving as sheriff in a temporary capacity.

title: T for turnaround: How the North Mac football team flipped the script from 1-8 to 3-0
author: Bill Welt
description: Roark Lewis missed out last year due to injury but now leads the North Mac football team in 3-0 turnaround
content:
VIRDEN — Roark Lewis quickly turned the page.
The senior running back reeled off a 40-yard touchdown run on his first carry in a Week 0 scrimmage against New Berlin and in one fell swoop disposed last season's woes.
2024 football coverage: High school football in the Springfield area: Complete coverage from the 2024 season
It was a visceral moment for Lewis on a personal level after missing most of last season due to a hip injury and all the while signaled a new era of North Mac football after the Panthers went 1-8 last season.
'I've been waiting for this all off-season,' Lewis said. 'I've been working hard, getting my mind and body right.
'I was very excited.'
Best fit for North Mac
It was precursor of things to come for the Panthers, now 3-0 following a 26-14 win over Litchfield.
They are now among three of the last remaining undefeated teams in the South Central Conference ahead of their Week 4 visit to 3-0 Pana on Friday.
They are anything but satisfied, said senior quarterback Payne McLean.
'(We went) 1-8 last year, so that just lights a fire under us,' McLean said. 'We're here to set the tone.'
Lewis only suited up for Week 1 against Hillsboro before sitting out the rest of 2023. He now leads the team with 475 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 45 carries. Against Litchfield, he amassed 191 rushing yards and a TD on 24 attempts.
Junior fullback James Graves has supplied 278 rushing yards and four scores, too, supported by an experienced offensive line that includes juniors David Enrietta and James Nolting and seniors Trent Hundtermark and Andrew Scroggins to name a few.
'It feels good running the ball a lot,' Lewis said. 'I think coach (Robbi Howard) has a great scheme for me, he gives me the ball a lot and gets all our guys equal amounts of touches. It's a pretty good offense.'
North Mac now champions the Wing-T — which is more in line with Howard's previous teams at Beardstown. It's hard to argue with the results.
Beardstown qualified for the playoffs in each of Howard's four seasons — including 10-1 in 2019 — after enduring two seasons without a win before his arrival.
'I think it's a perfect fit for our team,' Lewis said.
Top athletes
North Mac only graduated one senior from last season: quarterback Dane Vance.
McLean has assumed the mantle, completing 18 of 29 passing attempts for 330 yards and five TDs to go along with 114 rushing yards and three scores on 19 carries.
'I feel like it's a pretty big change going from the offenses that we had in past years,' McLean said. 'But I think it's a lot of fun because I just kind of get to watch my guys go make plays and I'll make plays myself, too, because even though we're Wing-T we still throw the ball quite a bit.'
Lewis and McLean each harbor hopes to play football at the next level. They additionally participate in other sports such as basketball, baseball and track. Lewis, in particular, will attempt to reach the boys track and field state finals in the long jump this spring.
Both their dads also hail from the Girard side and played football there before the co-op with Virden. Lewis' dad, Raymond, and brother, Reed, were each running backs in high school.
'He always wanted me to be a running back, of course,' Lewis said of his dad. 'He was also my JFL coach, so he taught me quite a bit. He says I run a lot like him when he was my age.'
McLean also plays safety, not unlike his dad, Pat.
'We're defending the pass a lot better this year,' McLean said of the defensive improvements. 'We've matured and we've kind of figured it out this year with the pass game. The pass defense is probably the biggest change. We've always been able to stop the run pretty well.'
Howard said they may be 3-0, but they want to keep getting better. Lewis doesn't have a shortage of fuel.
'Whenever I need encouragement, I think about that record and about my injury last year,' Lewis said.

title: Southeast side grocery store closing in November
author: Claire Grant
description: A southeast side grocery store is shutting down. Here's what's going on at Kent Plaza.
content:
(This story has been updated to because an earlier version included an inaccuracy.)
A grocery store the serves neighborhoods on the city's southeast side is shutting its doors in early November.
According to Niemann Foods director of consumer affairs Gerry Kettler, the County Market store at 2777 S. Sixth St. has not been able to renew its lease.
Staff was given notice of the closing on Sep. 12. Employees were then contacted by Niemann Foods that when the store closes, employees will be transferred to other County Markets in the area.
'The good news will be that all of our associates will be employed at our stores,' Kettler said. 'We're not necessarily closing it. We are, but we don't have a lease. We can't operate.'
The store plans to close Nov. 2, 2024, according to employees. If stock runs out, they may close earlier, they said.
The store is located in Kent Plaza.
Cleeman Realty Group arranged the $6,300,000 sale of Kent Plaza in July of 2020 in an off-market transaction to a private investment firm based out of Maryland.
Cleeman Realty's Michael Cleeman and Sam Seelenfreund represented both the buyer and the seller of the 94,260 square-foot center during the sale.
Kettler said the owners of Kent Plaza want to perform upgrades, including improvements in the space occupied by County Market.
'I don't know what they were going to be fixing but I know there are a lot of problems with the electronic things and the doors,' said County Market associate Meg Alexander. 'It's just an old store. This happens. Things get worn out. … I think Neimanns is trying to take care of their valued employees because they have a record of doing that.'

title: FBI responds to Springfield Board of Elections building for suspicious mail
author: Tom Ackerman
description: The Board of Elections building in Springfield received a suspicious parcel Friday, prompting presence from the FBI and a hazmat team.
content:
The FBI responded to the Illinois State Board of Elections building in Springfield after a suspicious package was found.
Election offices across the U.S. have been receiving suspicious mail, in upwards of 15 states, according to a report Tuesday from Associated Press.
Matthew Dietrich, a spokesperson for the Board of Elections, said the Springfield Police and Fire Departments responded to the building at 2329 S. MacArthur Blvd. until FBI arrived.
Employees became suspicious when they read an odd-looking return address on the parcel.
"We were expecting to get something like this, based on the fact that so many other state election offices around the country had already received them this week, so we were on the lookout for it,' Dietrich said. 'We knew if anything halfway suspicious came in, we knew not to open it, so when it arrived, we did not open it.'
About 20 people were inside the building when the package arrived and everyone evacuated.
Nationally, the FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service on Tuesday were investigating the origin of suspicious packages were sent to or received by elections officials, according to the AP report, but there have been no reports of injuries or hazardous materials found within the parcels.
Public Affairs Officer for FBI Springfield, Becky Cramblit, provided the following statement:
'The FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating a series of suspicious mailings sent to election officials in several states. Some of the letters contained an unknown substance and we are working closely with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident and safely collect the letters. We are also working with our partners to determine how many letters were sent, the individual or individuals responsible for the letters, and the motive behind the letters. As this is an ongoing matter we will not be commenting further on the investigation, but the public can be assured safety is our top priority. We would also like to remind everyone to exercise care in handling mail, especially from unrecognized senders. If you see something suspicious, please contact law enforcement immediately.'

title: Winning $1M scratch-off ticket sold in Springfield
author: Tom Ackerman
description: A winning $1 million scratch-off lottery ticket was sold at a Springfield gas station.
content:
A winning $1 million scratch-off lottery ticket was sold at a Springfield gas station.
The Illinois Lottery said the ticket was sold at the Marathon at 3801 S. Sixth St.
The lottery player won the top prize on a $10 Gold Multiplier Instant Ticket, which launched earlier this month, according to the Illinois Lottery.
The store will additionally receive a bonus of $10,000, which is one percent of the prize amount, for selling the winning ticket.
So far this year, more than 45.8 million winning Illinois Lottery Instant Tickets have been sold, netting players over $1.1 billion in prizes, according to a news release.
The winning ticket was sold days after the Illinois Department of the Lottery named its Springfield building the E.J. "Zeke" Giorgi Lottery Building. The grandson of Giorgi, State Rep. Dave Vella, D-Loves Park, was present at a ceremony on Sept. 18.
The Illinois Lottery began selling tickets in 1974 as a result of legislation sponsored by the State Representative Edolo J. "Zeke" Giorgi – earning him the title of "Father of the Lottery."

title: Free COVID tests are coming soon: How and when to order them
author: Eric Lagatta
description: The program, offered through the U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) agency, will offer up to four nasal swab tests per U.S. household when it opens.
content:
Americans will soon be able to order free COVID-19 test kits from the federal government to be delivered to their homes.
The program, offered through the U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) agency, will offer up to four nasal swab tests per U.S. household when it opens at COVIDTests.gov.
HHS is reopening the program at a time of year when COVID-19 cases and other respiratory illnesses are expected to make their yearly surges. The tests will detect current virus strains and will be available through the end of the year.
As of Monday, the agency did not have an exact date for when the program would start. The website says the tests will be available for order at the end of September.
Here's what to know about the free COVID-19 tests.
How to order free COVID-19 tests
To order the tests, visit COVIDtest.gov. Once ordered, the at-home tests will be shipped to homes for free.
Each household can receive up to four free tests.
When will free COVID tests be available to order?
An agency spokesman did not provide a program start date when reached Monday by USA TODAY. The website says tests will be available for order by the end of September.
What do the tests detect?
The tests will be able to detect the dominant variants that are circulating, according to the CDC.
The at-home tests typically provide results within 30 minutes or less and can be administered to both vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals. Many COVID-19 tests now have extended expiration dates.
While positive results are accurate, the HHS warns that negative results don't necessarily rule out a COVID-19 infection. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration recommends two negative antigen tests for people with symptoms or three antigen tests for people without symptoms, each performed 48 hours apart.
CDC recommends updated COVID-19 vaccine
The program will begin at a time as COVID-19 is expected to hit its winter peak along with the flu and respiratory virus (RSV.)
As of this month, the COVID-19 variant KP.3.1.1 now accounts for more than half of positive infections in the United States, according to the latest projections from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
Prior infections or vaccines may grant individuals with some degree of immunity or protection, but it doesn't last forever. The CDC recommends that everyone ages 6 months and older receive an updated COVID-19 vaccine regardless of whether they have ever previously been vaccinated.

title: Iowa-based grocery store with Springfield location is voted best grocery store
author: Claire Grant
description: USA TODAY readers have made their voice heard and declared the best grocery store across all 50 states—which has a Springfield location.
content:
Show Caption
USA TODAY readers have made their voice heard and declared the best grocery store across all 50 states—which has a Springfield location.
It's the first time this store has won Best Grocery Store in America in USA TODAY's 10Best Readers' Choice Awards.
America's most loved grocery store
Hy-Vee has been voted the Best Grocery Store in America, taking the top spot among the most-loved grocery stores in the country. Previously the company ranked within the top three spots, but this is the first time on the golden podium for the Iowa-based company.
The second place on the list was Fresh Market which uses a warehouse style supermarket and operates in 22 states, while third place was taken by Heinen's Grocery for their rewards and family-owned chain style.
Did Hy-Vee win any other awards?
Hy-Vee was also voted America's Best Grocery Store for Produce and ranked the No. 2 Best Grocery Store for Prepared Food in the nation.
About the Reader's Choice Awards
The State Journal-Register is part of USA Today. The USA TODAY's 10Best Readers' Choice Awards is conducted annually. A panel of experts nominates 20 grocery stores as the best in the U.S. for their offerings, selection and great service.
USA TODAY readers, like you, are then encouraged to cast their votes during a 28-day voting period. The nominated stores who received the most votes are designated as the Readers' Choice for their category.
About Hy-Vee
Founded nearly 95 years ago, Hy-Vee has become known for its quality, variety and Chinese takeout section. The retail giant operates more than 570 business units across the U.S. and is one of the largest employee-owned companies in the nation.
The business operates across nine Midwest states with sales of more than $13 billion annually.
The Hy-Vee in Springfield is located at 2115 S. MacArthur Blvd. and offers a pharmacy, gas station and a Wahlberg's burger bar conjoined to the main store.

title: National Coffee Day 2024: Free coffee at Dunkin', Krispy Kreme plus more deals, specials
author: Mike Snider
description: National Coffee Day is Sunday, Sept. 29, and that means freebies, deals and specials at spots including Dunkin', Krispy Kreme and Peet's Coffee.
content:
Coffee is a go-to drink for most Americans, with more than six out of 10 downing a cup daily. Folks can celebrate the beverage on National Coffee Day, which is Sunday, Sept. 29, with many coffee spots having specials and freebies.
Coffee consumption hit a two-decade high earlier this year, with about 67% of U.S. adults having at least one cup daily, according to a January survey from the National Coffee Association. That dipped slightly to 63% in a subsequent July 2024 NCA survey, also conducted for the trade association by Dig Insights.
Coffee lovers are increasingly getting their java jolt away from home, too. More than one-third of the respondents who said they had coffee in the past day (36%) got their caffeine fix away from home, the highest level since the COVID-19 pandemic.
National Coffee Day facts
How much coffee do we drink? About 2½ cups per person each day, the NCA survey found.
Favorite brands: Starbucks edges out Dunkin' as the favorite coffee brand, with 48% of those in the Drive Research survey preferring that brand, compared to 45% for Dunkin'. Other favorites? Folgers (29%), McDonald's McCafé (18%), and Green Mountain (18%).
How we drink our coffee: With milk or creamer (39%); with sweetener and milk or cream (38%), black (18%); with sweetener (5%).
Coffee and health: Coffee drinking has some health benefits with research suggesting two to three cups daily might help you live longer and reduce risk of heart disease and stroke. But you may want to make sure you don't drink too much coffee, as many experts suggest no more than four cups daily.
Coffee is "a touchstone in Americans' everyday lives," said National Coffee Association president and CEO William 'Bill' Murray in a statement. "It embodies comforting traditions, provides fun opportunities to try new trends, and people are increasingly aware of significant scientific evidence that drinking coffee is associated with positive health outcomes."

title: Quincy Notre Dame football scores a rollicking CS8 win over Springfield High
author: Bill Welt
description: Quincy Notre Dame stands atop the CS8 West standings following Wyatt Mueller's late touchdown run against Springfield High
content:
(This story was updated to add new information.)
Wyatt Mueller can get the job done through different means.
The Quincy Notre Dame senior completed a key fourth-down pass before plunging over the goal line for the go-ahead touchdown late in the fourth quarter en route to a 14-9 Central State Eight Conference win over Springfield High at Memorial Stadium on Friday.
Mueller tossed a nine-yard pass to Jack Brenner to keep the game-winning drive alive on fourth-and-4 with under three minutes remaining.
"We repped that play all of the time, just a little play-action," Mueller said. "I'm guessing they were keying on me running the ball because we were doing that an awful lot. But Jack (Brenner) was right there.I just pitched it down andluckily he was able to get downreally quick (to catch the pass) and we just kept the ball moving."
Mueller scored two plays later on a 3-yard run with 1 minute, 41 seconds left.
"The O-line gave me a great push to get in there and coach Jack (Cornell) drew up a great play," Mueller said. "The counter was working really well with our left side and (offensive lineman) Ryan Darnell really just got that linebacker and had a great push, so I'm super proud of our O-line and how our team played overall."
Mueller totaled five touchdowns in a 37-7 win over Sacred Heart-Griffin in Week 4, and the Class 2A No. 3 Raiders (4-1, 3-0) now hold the sole lead in the CS8 West.
Mueller had 11 carries for 68 yards while junior running back Oliver Triplett had 47 rushing yards on 19 attempts.
QND junior QB Hunter Shuckman completed 13 of 16 passing attempts for 82 yards and a score. That included 5-yard TD pass to senior Taylin Scott for a 9-8 deficit late in the third quarter.
The Senators (4-1, 2-1) reached as far as the QND 21-yard line but stalled on their final possession after an untimely pre-snap penalty.
SHS senior running back Armanze Lewis jumpstarted the team's opening drive with a couple of big gains before scoring on a 1-yard TD run. He totaled 21 carries for 129 yards.
Kia Rinaberger supplied the 29-yard field goal to extend the lead 9-0 to start the third quarter.
"It was nice jumping to a 9-0 lead," SHS coach Jon Hebb said, "unfortunately we couldn't sustain it. We just had too many mistakes down the stretch and hats off to QND because they put together two drives in the secondhalf and they were able to punch it in both times and come out with the win.

title: What makes you the best grocery store in town? Hy-Vee raises the stakes
author: Claire Grant
description: What goes into becoming the most loved grocery store in the country? The Springfield store director weighs in.
content:
What goes into becoming the most loved grocery store in the country? Is it low prices to beat the rest, an assortment of food and home goods one notch above the next or even the charities the store donates to?
Maybe it's steak dinners with a side of potatoes and green beans and burgers with celebs?
According to Hy-Vee Springfield store director, it takes all that and a little bit more to win best grocer.
'We're trying to provide 100 million meals in the nine states that we help support and that we serve,' District Store Director Jim Blizzard said. 'We're up to 800 or 83,000,000 meals so far that we've raised in just a short little time… So we expect to hit that goal of 100 meals here in the next just a little while. Locally, we were able to provide $90,000 to the Central Illinois Food Bank as part of this program.'
For the first time ever, Hy-Vee, an Iowa-based grocery store chain, was voted Best Grocery Store in America in USA TODAY's 10 Best Readers' Choice Awards by readers of Gannett papers, like The State Journal-Register.
In previous years, the company has ranked within the top three spots, but according to Blizzard some changes in the past year have helped Hy-Vee come out on top, at least in Springfield.
Paul Wahlberg, brother to actors Donnie and Mark Walhberg, visited his Wahlburgers store on April 11 of this year. The Springfield store joins three other central Illinois locations participating in the 100 million meals challenge, with two in Quincy and one in Jacksonville.
What was once the former Kmart building, an abandoned bowling alley and payday loan store, in 2012 Hy-Vee Corp. purchased the store at 2114 S. MacArthur Blvd. transforming the section of MacArthur into a busy strip. The store offers savings by gas saving deals of 20 cents a gallon, a plethora of grocery and ready-to-eat food options and a drive through pharmacy, continuing to sustain the now bustling corner of the boulevard.
While headquarters are in Iowa, the Springfield location has worked on supporting their city through partnerships with organizations like the Red Cross.
'I think last year when we had the derechos and the storms that came through, we were the folks that were providing Red Cross with the meals down at Bank of Springfield,' Blizzard said. 'We were the ones that were providing meals to all of the CWLP line workers that were out day night trying to fix all the power and get all the power back up.'
Interested in their hot food? You aren't the only one – it's one of the store's main attractions. The infamous Hy-Vee steak night on Thursdays from 4 to 7 p.m. Guests can get a choice cut steak with mashed potatoes and green beans for $10, with add-ons like shrimp and onions for just a buck or two more. The night has been extremely popular Blizzard says and that every Thursday, the line will be wrapped nearly around the store with repeat customers.
'We have a wide variety of promotions that we're able to help folks save even more money with our weekly ad, where there'll be thousands of items in the ad that are well below the market price,' Blizzard said. 'We do this by having great partnerships with our vendor community where we're able to get those prices down and be competitive across the area.'
To celebrate, the store is giving customers what they want on Oct. 5, in a customer appreciation day according to Blizzard.

title: Springfield man sentenced for trying to kill his ex-girlfriend
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Authorities said the suspect cut his ex-girlfriend's throat with a boxcutter before running off and later being arrested in Colorado.
content:
A Springfield man has been sentenced to 40 years in prison for trying to kill his ex-girlfriend.
Clarence Hopson was sentenced on Oct. 3 after being found guilty of attempted first-degree murder, home invasion, aggravated battery and aggravated stalking in July.
Prosecutors argued that Hopson had stalked his ex-girlfriend and ultimately tried to kill her two years ago.
The woman testified that Hopson broke into her Springfield home around 5:30 a.m. on Nov. 12, 2022, when he and cut her throat and chin with a boxcutter, in addition to slashing her wrist.
After cutting her, Hopson ran out of the house, and the woman called 911.
Authorities said Hopson then went to Chicago and Las Vegas before being arrested in Colorado.
But Hopson left his box cutter at the crime scene, and lab results showed his DNA on the handle, according to a news release from the Sangamon County State's Attorney's office.
Phone records and social media data showed Hopson was at the woman's home around 1 a.m., several hours before the attack. Authorities also said Hopson called the woman 39 times and sent several text and Facebook messages between 1 a.m. and the time of the attack.
'You broke into that house with the intent to murder her; I have no doubt in my mind about that,' said Judge Adam Giganti, according to the press release.
Giganti said there were numerous opportunities to stop what he was doing, and he articulated that Hopson had stalked and harassed the victim for weeks prior to the attack.
Hopson represented himself at the trial and the sentencing hearing. The case was prosecuted by Special Assistant State's Attorney Derek Dion and Assistant State's Attorney Meghan McCarthy.

title: Springfield's West African restaurant is closing its doors—but not for good
author: Claire Grant
description: Springfield's destination for West African cuisine is closing up shop on South MacArthur Boulevard but won't be leaving the foodies scene for long.
content:
Show Caption
Springfield's destination for West African cuisine is closing up shop on South MacArthur Boulevard but won't be leaving the foodies scene for long.
Travelers Kitchen at 1731 S. MacArthur Blvd. is shutting its doors on Oct. 15, according to owner Ansumana Darboe. The restaurant has been a part of Springfield's lively restaurant scene since April of 2023 and is one of the sole providers of traditional West African food.
While the location is right on a busy street, due to the cost of rent and operation costs, the kitchen isn't making enough margin of profit to stay open in its current form, according to Darboe.
The solution for Darboe is shifting the business model on wheels – in the form of a food truck. The food truck is already bought and set to be ready by February of next year.
'We want a food truck because you can do more publicity around the food,' Darboe said. 'Then once we have a new location in the summer, we can park the food truck there.'
Darboe says in the near future he plans on reopening at a new location, and plans on finding a permanent place to either own or rent for a more feasible price by May, or June of next year.
Until the food truck is up and running, catering will continue with the West African restaurant with orders still available on their Facebook page.
The taste of Gambia, chicken Yassa, a flavorful tomato and lemon dish that pairs with fufu, a starchy dough used for scooping hot spicy stews are just a few of the dishes to try.
Darboe said thank you to all of his customers, and that while the location may be gone for a short period, the food will return.

title: Braddock Cates, Williamsville football hum in Sangamo win over Athens
author: Bill Welt
description: Williamsville football nearly reached 400 rushing yards in a win over Athens on Friday
content:
(This story was updated to add new information.)
ATHENS — Braddock Cates bolted out of the gates with a touchdown run in the opening two minutes and the Williamsville football team coasted to a 52-6 Sangamo Conference win over Athens on Friday.
Cates supplied the first two touchdowns in the first quarter and racked up 177 total yards of offense. He finished with 14 carries for 127 yards and three scores. He also had three catches for 50 yards.
"I think we're moving in a really good direction and a really good pace," Cates said. "The first few weeks, it wasn't bad. It's never been bad. I think we're really starting to pick it up. I think we're on a really good track right now."
The Bullets (5-1, 5-0 Sangamo) amassed 385 rushing yards as a team. Senior tailback Gage Paul's 91-yard TD burst and Will Zinn's 27-yard field goal created a 24-6 halftime lead. Paul ended with 113 rushing yards on just two carries.
Junior quarterback Jackson Sanders also kept the offense humming. He went 9-for-11 for 117 yards and one TD in addition to 22 rushing yards. Senior tight end Carson Beattie had the TD catch to go along with a sack defensively.
Athens (2-4, 2-4) pared the early deficit to one possession on Talon DiGiovanna's 9-yard scoring run. Athens also recovered a fumbled snap to begin the third quarter but couldn't capitalize. Williamsville subsequently scored on its next four possessions.
"I think kind of a big turning point for us was after we fumbled to start the second half and we got them to go four-and-out," Williamsville coach Aaron Kunz said. "I thought that was huge and we rolled from there. I felt all season we have a lot of playmakers and tonight we really did a good job of distributing the ball to them."
Junior running back Gage Honn led Athens with 59 rushing yards but left the field at the start of the second half due to injury. Brodee Rector had 50 rushing yards.

title: Remaining Neuhoff owned radio stations officially sold in Springfield area
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Woodward Communication, Inc. officially acquired the final 7 Neuhoff family-owned radio stations in Springfield and Bloomington. Here's what to know.
content:
The acquisition is complete and the Neuhoff family is officially out of local radio after nearly 70 years.
Woodward Communication, Inc. officially acquired seven radio station brands from Neuhoff Media in Springfield and Bloomington on Sept. 30, according to a press release from WCI.
'We are pleased to announce that today we successfully consummated the acquisition of Neuhoff Media's radio stations and brands based in Springfield and Bloomington, IL,' stated WCI President/CEO Tom Woodward in the news release. 'Over the past couple of months, we have gotten to know each other better, shared ideas, aspirations, etc. which in turn has created positive momentum and energy on which we can enhance our capabilities to serve our customers and communities."
The stations sold in Springfield include country music station 104.5 WFMB, Sports Radio 92.3FM and 1450AM, adult contemporary station 99-7 The Mix, adult hits station 96.7 BOB FM, and Channel 1450, a digital platform covering high school sports.
The Springfield channels are broadcasted from the radio station on South Fourth Street.
In Bloomington, WCI adds Rock 96.7, adult contemporary NOW 100.7, and BOB FM 97.9.
No layoffs are expected, and programming as of now will remain the same, said Kevin O'Dea, General Manager of Woodward Community Media in Springfield.
'All employees of Neuhoff Media Springfield and Bloomington are all remaining on board and we're moving forward with business as usual," he told The State Journal-Register.
Neuhoff Family Limited Partnership announced in July an agreement between Neuhoff Media LLC in Springfield and Bloomington to sell the seven different channels to WCI.
WCI is an employee-owned company which operates several radio stations in Wisconsin among other properties owned in Wisconsin, Illinois, and Rhode Island.
In February of this year, Neuhoff sold nine radio and website channels in Decatur and Danville to Champaign Media group, marking the company's first leap to exit the broadcast industry.

title: New Berlin, Springfield High come up clutch, and other Week 6 football takeaways
author: Bill Welt
description: Springfield High's Brody Scheffler and Kale Thurman didn't have the only clutch plays in the area in this week's top takeaways in football
content:
Show Caption
(This story was updated to add new information.)
Here are the top takeaways from Week 6 of high school football around Springfield:
Big play, dominant second half keeps Pretzels unbeaten
Trailing 14-0 at halftime in its Sangamo Conference road game at Stanford Olympia, New Berlin needed a momentum shift, and the Pretzels got it one the second half kickoff.
A line-drive kick from Olympia was picked up by Drew Johnson, and the sophomore raced 80 yards for a touchdown, and New Berlin started to reverse its fortune to get within 14-7 in the third quarter.
It was a new game as the Pretzels went on to hold the Spartans scoreless in the second half while scoring 21 unanswered points for a 21-14 victory.
The Pretzels got their ground game going in the fourth period, leaning on Clark Nelson, who scored two second-half touchdowns and finished with 132 yards on 23 carries. Nelson tied the game in the fourth with a 5-yard TD run, and after pinning Olympia deep in its own territory, New Berlin received the ball after a punt at the Spartans' 43-yard line with 5:53 remaining.
Nelson rumbled for 15 yards on the first play of the possession, and a personal foul on Olympia put New Berlin at the 13-yard line. An 11-yard run by Charlie Newman put the Pretzels in deep, and Nelson scored the go-ahead TD from 2 yards out. Nelson had a sack on the defensive side of the ball as Olympia attempted to even the score with 2:01 left. The Spartans, facing a fouth-and-5 was stopped short, and New Berlin took possession at their 34-yard line with 1:54 to go.
From there, Nelson pounded out 12 more yards on the ground as the Pretzels ran out the clock and improved to 6-0.
Lincoln offense paves way for CS8 win
Not only did Tate Johnston run for 111 yards on 20 attempts, but the senior quarterback also completed 10 of 13 passes for 121 yards and two touchdowns in Lincoln's 43-33 victory over Decatur MacArthur in a Central State Eight Conference game.
The Railers (4-2 overall, 2-2 in the CS8) had three players rack up over 100 rushing yards to finish with 395 total. Gabe Smith rushed 14 times and led Lincoln with 141 yards, while teammate Paytan Bunner had 21 carries for 107.
Bunner ended with four touchdowns, catching two TDs in the first half from 13 and 5 yards. His two rushing scores were from 14 and 8 yards. Kyle Koehler's 9-yard TD run in the third quarter gave Lincoln the lead for good, 28-21, after MacArthur led 21-14 at intermission. Johnston iced the win with a 5-yard score in the fourth after the Generals got within 36-33.
Lincoln outgained MacArthur 516-364 and nearly doubled the Generals in total plays 80-41. The Railers were efficient on third down, converting 10 of 15 tries and went 2-for-2 on fourth down.
Stout, Rockets shake off early miscue
On the first play from scrimmage, Rochester's Kaiden Stout turned the ball over on a fumble.
It was the last mistake the junior running back would make as he churned out 134 yards on just seven carries and scored two touchdowns in the Rockets' 55-0 running-clock victory over Decatur Eisenhower in a Central State Eight Conference game at Rocket Booster Stadium.
Stout scored the first touchdown, a 6-yard run in the first quarter. He added a 55-yard TD in the third quarter to put Rochester (4-2 overall, 3-1 in the CS8) ahead 27-0.
The Rockets concluded with five rushing TDs, and quarterback Tanner Beal completed 9 of 12 passes for 183 yards with a touchdown. Khorbin Gregory caught two passes for 70 yards and rushed seven times for 41 with a TD.
The Rochester defense stepped up in the shutout, coming away with four interceptions. Zane Zulauf returned an INT 36 yards for a touchdown off Eisenhower reserve quarterback Martavious Johnsons.
Johnsons was intercepted three times after coming in for starter Garryon Henderson, who was injured in the third quarter. Henderson was transported to the hospital by ambulance when he landed awkwardly on the sidelines. The status of his injury is not yet known.
Senators learn from the past
It was just a week ago Springfield High lamented its final possession against Quincy Notre Dame.
The Senators (5-1, 3-1 Central State Eight) reached as far as the QND 21-yard line with just over a minute remaining before stalling in a 14-9 loss to the Raiders in Week 5.
SHS found itself in the same position against Jacksonville but with even less time to spare. The Senators trailed 29-28 with 1 minute, 2 seconds left before junior QB Brody Scheffler dialed up four straight passes to Kale Thurman, including the go-ahead 40-yard TD pass with 35 seconds left for a 36-29 Week 6 victory.
Thurman, the team's leading receiver, was perhaps the missing piece of the puzzle. He had just two catches for 22 yards in the loss to QND.
This bounce-back win could certainly be taken as another sign of progress under coach Jon Hebb, and SHS is now playoff eligible for the first time in three seasons.
QND stands alone
Did anybody see this coming?
Quincy Notre Dame is the last remaining team unbeaten in conference play following Chatham Glenwood's 33-13 loss to Normal U-High.
QND, 5-1 overall with the only loss to 7A No. 5-ranked Quincy in Week 1, throttled Lanphier 77-6 after leading 56-6 at halftime to move to 4-0 in the Central State Eight conference. Senior running back Ivan Hun returned to action and found the end zone multiple times after missing last week's win over Springfield High due to an injury the previous week against Sacred Heart-Griffin.
The 2A No. 3 Raiders still face a couple of tough roadblocks from going 7-0 in their first year in the CS8. That includes two 4-2 teams fighting for a playoff berth — at Jacksonville, then back home against Lincoln in consecutive weeks before finishing the regular season at Decatur MacArthur.
New Berlin, Williamsville to clash in the trenches
New Berlin senior Clark Nelson leads the team with 687 yards and 12 touchdowns following the 21-14 comeback win over Stanford Olympia.
That prowess is also matched by his defense. He also led the Pretzels with 11 tackles, including the key sack on Olympia's final possession. That is hardly surprising considering Nelson was all-Sangamo first team defensively last season.
They next welcome Williamsville in a Week 7 showdown. Both are tied atop the Sangamo Conference standings alongside 2A No. 1 Maroa-Forsyth. Williamsville fell to 3A No. 1 Byron in a nonconference game.
It figures to be a battle of who has the strongest ground game. Williamsville nearly ran for 400 rushing yards in its 52-6 win over Athens, led by senior all-state running back Braddock Cates.
Pana, North Mac bounce back in SCC
Pana rebounded in a big way with a 48-21 win over Hillsboro after jumping to a 41-0 halftime lead.
It also finds itself tied atop the South Central Conference standings following Vandalia's stunning 35-34 overtime win over previously unbeaten Greenville. That prompts a three-way tie for first place between Pana, Vandalia and Greenville, the last of which seeking its second straight SCC title.
Pana (5-1) opened with a 21-14 win over Vandalia in Week 1 and next draws Gillespie, Litchfield and Staunton.
Also in the SCC, North Mac (4-2) toppled Carlinville 21-14 after a blistering start to move one game away from becoming playoff eligible after going 1-8 last year. Roark Lewis scored two touchdown runs against the Cavaliers, his second 30 yards out for a 21-7 lead with 10:38 left in the second quarter.
The defense preserved the win after consecutive losses to Pana (51-24) and Vandalia (42-12).

title: Official: Witnesses say boy, 10, wasn't intended target in fatal shooting
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Witnesses have told officials the boy who was fatally shot in Peoria who had ties to Springfield was not the intended target. Here's the latest.
content:
A botched drug deal may have led to the fatal shooting of Torres L. Johnson II, a 10-year-old boy who lived in Peoria but had ties to Springfield.
Witnesses said the shooting happened after a drug deal involving cannabis went wrong and led to an attempted armed robbery between the suspect Maurice Sargent, 33, and two juveniles, according to the Peoria County State's Attorney's Office.
The State's Attorney's Office said Johnson not involved in the drug deal and was simply walking by when the shooting occurred in the middle of an attempted robbery.
Sargent was charged with first-degree murder and armed habitual criminal in the shooting.
'My office will do everything we can to get justice for Torres and his family,' Jodi M. Hoos, Peoria County State's Attorney, said in a news release.
Peoria Police said that in addition to Sargent, a 14-year-old boy was identified as a suspect in the case. The teen was arrested for attempted armed robbery.
Johnson was shot at an apartment complex Sunday evening in Peoria. He was found, lying in the grass with a gunshot wound to the chest.
Police took Sargent into custody on Oct. 1.
