title: What is a bollard? Were they removed from Bourbon Street before attack? Here's what to know
author: Miguel Legoas
description: Were bollards up during the New Year terrorist attack on New Orleans? What even is a bollard? Could it have saved lives? Here's what we know.
content:
While some are talking about New Year's resolutions and college football, many others are talking about the attack in New Orleans.
A man identified as 42-year-old Shamsud-Din Jabbar, a U.S. citizen from Texas, drove a truck into a crowd early Wednesday while shooting at officers, leaving 10 dead and 35 injured. One question among those watching the news unfold is "Were bollards up?"
A bollard is a short, sturdy, vertical poll used to divert traffic and to keep vehicles out of particular areas. They are meant to prevent incidents like the ones in New Orleans from happening.
The bollards along Bourbon Street were being replaced as part of an ongoing project that began in November, said New Orleans mayor LaToya Cantrell. The project was planned to be complete before the Super Bowl in February.
City Council President Helena Moreno reportedly pushed back on the idea that the absence of bollards was to blame and said the suspect could have made it onto Bourbon Street another way.
There were barriers in place, such as police vehicles, to block off Bourbon Street, police officials said during a press conference, but Jabbar bypassed the blockade by driving onto the sidewalk.
"This person was determined to inflict pain and death and harm on Bourbon Street, and I think he would have done that any way he could," Moreno said.
The driver was killed by officers. The White House and the FBI have confirmed that this attack is being investigated by the Bureau as an act of terrorism.
"My heart goes out to the victims and their families who were simply trying to celebrate the holiday," President Joe Biden said on X (formerly known as Twitter). "There is no justification for violence of any kind, and we will not tolerate any attack on any of our nation's communities."

title: Student of the game: Glenwood's Knoedler locks up SJ-R's Large School Football POTY award
author: Adrian Dater
description: Colten Knoedler believes in being a student first, but the SJ-R's Large School Football POTY is also first in a number of Glenwood records.
content:
His father played baseball in the Detroit Tigers' minor-league system and his uncle played parts of three seasons for the San Francisco Giants. Colten Knoedler also plays baseball for Chatham Glenwood, but don't assume that's what he'll play beyond high school. In fact, football appears to be a more likely athletic pursuit.
'To be honest with you, it changes by the day,' said Knoedler, when asked whether he prefers one sport over the other.
But college football coaches already have their eyes on the 6-foot-1, 190-pound quarterback of the Titans, who is The State Journal-Register's Large School Football Player of the Year for 2024. Leading the Titans to the Class 6A state quarterfinals for the second straight year, Knoedler completed 177-of-284 passes for 2,643 yards, 29 touchdown passes, and just four interceptions.
The standout posted a number of individual game, season and career records at Glenwood: most completions in a single game (tied at 22); most passing yards in a game (475); most TDs thrown in a game (six, tied); most pass attempts in a season (284); most completions in a season (177); most passing yards in a season (2,643), and most career completions (329).
Knoedler is readying himself to be the starting catcher this spring for the Glenwood baseball team, but the junior admits he's already excited for his senior football season, for a team that will return several other outstanding players.
'I think we'll be bigger, stronger and faster. I think we know more what it takes to get ourselves to where we want to be, which is a state champion,' Knoedler said.
The Titans gave eventual state champion East St. Louis a tough game for more than 30 minutes in the quarterfinals before the Flyers pulled away. To that point, the Flyers had allowed zero points and only three first downs in two playoff games, but Knoedler led Glenwood to two touchdown drives and could have had more if not for some missed opportunities.
Knoedler is fast (he runs the 40 in 4.7 seconds) and has a strong right arm. Nearly as important, says his coach, David Hay, are his exceptional leadership qualities.
'We hit a little bit of a rough spot in the middle of the season. We lost to (Normal) University High. But you could see him really start becoming more of a leader at that point. He really gets his teammates to buy in, to want to work as hard as he does,' Hay said.
Of a future in football beyond high school, Hay said: 'I think he's a college quarterback. He's got the size and the arm strength. And, he's going to get even stronger.'
But what about baseball? After all, his father, Jason, and uncle, Justin, played professionally. His father was drafted in the sixth round of the 2001 MLB Draft by Detroit, and he had more than 1,100 at-bats in the minors. Uncle Justin, who along with his brother starred at Springfield High School, was drafted in the fifth round in 2001 by the Giants and played from 2004-06 with San Francisco.
That might well be the sport of his future. At this point, Knoedler is just seeing where the fates take him. If he doesn't pursue baseball, that will be OK with his father.
'You know what? Whatever he decides, that'll be his own decision. And we know that will be a well-considered decision. We've never pushed him into anything athletically,' said Jason Knoedler, an executive at Bank of Springfield. 'Colten is kind of an old soul. He takes life seriously, but he also knows how to have a lot of fun. He loves hanging out with his buddies. They're all over here a lot.'
Indeed, high-intensity games of College Football 25 are commonplace with his friends at the house, Colten said. Other than sports and some video-game leisure time, academics are paramount to Knoedler. His grades place him in the top 20 of his class.
'I'm definitely a student first,' Knoedler said. 'I believe that's what's most important. Sports usually aren't forever.'
When his athletic career is over, Knoedler said he'll likely consider going into banking, like his father, or he might pursue a career in medicine. Anatomy has always been one of his favorite subjects.
Bottom line, Knoedler has options. All of them, seemingly good ones.
Said Knoedler: 'I owe so much to my coaches, but most of all, my parents. My mom (Melissa) is really the reason I'm doing what I'm doing. She does all my meal prep and makes sure I do what I'm supposed to do. She's awesome.'

title: Illinois coach Bret Bielema appears to taunt South Carolina coach, who is held back at Citrus Bowl
author: Austin Curtright
description: South Carolina coach Shane Beamer erupted Tuesday after Illinois coach Bret Bielema appeared to taunt him during the Citrus Bowl.
content:
South Carolina football coach Shane Beamer got his team fired up on Tuesday in the Citrus Bowl against Illinois.
Beamer had to be held back as the Gamecocks approached Illinois' red zone late in the third quarter, as Fighting Illini coach Bret Bielema appeared to taunt Beamer after signaling to Beamer with a substitution gesture used by game officials.
Bielema was on the field tending to one of his injured players when the ESPN broadcast caught Bielema taunting Beamer.
That, of course, caused Beamer to snap.
Beamer had to be held back by numerous staff members as he appeared to yell and run toward Bielema, before the situation ultimately dissolved. Numerous players from both teams were on the field as everything blew over.
"Shane just turned to me and said, 'You saw what he did,' " ESPN sideline reporter Quint Kessenich said on the broadcast. "I did see it. He taunted the opposing coach."
The Gamecocks took a 17-14 lead on the same possession after quarterback LaNorris Sellers found Joshua Simon for a 6-yard touchdown. Beamer, unsurprisingly, erupted with emotion after taking the lead.
After the game, Beamer addressed Bielema's gesture.
"It's heated and competitive out there, but in all my years of being around football, I've never seen an opposing head coach come over to the opposing team's sideline and basically make a gesture towards the opposing head coach," Beamer said. "I think he was upset about something that we did on the kickoff return. ... I would say he needs to check the rule book, because that's something that we cleared with the officials before the game. Disappointing."
Beamer said the dispute stemmed from a gesture made by his player during a kickoff. Beamer said he cleared it with officials before the game.
"I think his issue was when we threw the throw-back kickoff return, our kickoff returner did this (arm out to side), which for most teams that's a signal that it's a touchback and you're not going to return the kick," Beamer said. "You're allowed to do that as long as you don't do a waving motion. ... There was no waving of the arms, and I cleared it with the Big 12 officials before the game. I told them we were going to do it, making sure they were good with it, and they said, yeah, just as long as he doesn't wave the arms.
"I think he had an issue with that. You have to ask him why he didn't take it up with the officials and why he felt the need to come over here, while his player was on the ground and look at me and say something to me and do that motion at me like I was full of you know-what.
"That's what I have an issue with. I'm a competitive guy. When somebody says that to me, I'm going to respond, because I thought that was bush league, just to be completely honest."

title: Chatham Glenwood grad wins best DIII football player award for second straight season
author: Bill Welt
description: The former Chatham Glenwood star won the most prestigious award in NCAA Division III football for a second straight season
content:
North Central College quarterback Luke Lehnen won the 2024 John Gagliardi Trophy for a second straight season on Friday.
The 2020 Chatham Glenwood graduate seized the highest honor in NCAA Division III football after leading the Cardinals to a fifth straight national championship berth. They will meet Mount Union in the Stagg Bowl in Houston, Texas on Sunday, 7 p.m. Both teams are 14-0.
This will be Lehnen's fourth straight Stagg Bowl appearance. He won the national title against Mount Union in the 2022 season before bowing to Cortland the ensuing year for the team's only loss.
He is coming off a blistering 66-0 semifinal victory over Susquehanna University after the Cardinals reached the end zone on their first nine possessions. The win tied the DIII semifinal record for largest margin of victory.
Lehnen finished 16-of-17 for 275 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions, while also scoring a rushing TD.
Last season, Lehnen set multiple DIII records. They included passing efficiency (263.2), yards per pass (14.7), yards per completion (20) and percentage of passes completed for touchdowns (20.7%). He also broke school records for career rushing yards (2,348) and rushing TDs (36).
The four-year starter and graduate student is on pace to set the career NCAA passing efficiency record (211.8) across all divisions, while shattering all-division records for consecutive games with a touchdown pass (58) and touchdowns responsible for (208).
His 15,632 career total offensive yardage has also far exceeded the previous record of 14,568. He currently remains tied for career touchdown passes (158) in DIII history and third overall in college football history behind only John Matocha of the Colorado School of Mines (162) and Tyson Bagent of Shepherd College (159).
Illinois College quarterback Destin Chance was also among the five finalists for the Gagliardi Trophy.
The 2019 Auburn grad finished 234 of 381 (61.4 %) for 3,593 yards and 50 touchdowns. He also rushed for 586 yards on 89 carries with eight scores. He led DIII in total offense with 417.9 yards per game and is the school's all-time leader with 116 career TD passes.
He recently announced on social media that he will be entering the transfer portal with one year of eligibility remaining for Division I.
His older brother, Drew, was named the DIII Coordinator of the Year on Thursday, while fifth-year senior receiver Collin Brunstein, a Jacksonville graduate, earned first-team All-American laurels from The Associated Press with 73 receptions for 1,540 yards and 27 touchdowns in his final season at IC.
Brunstein set an NCAA record with 77 career touchdown receptions. He exits as the school's all-time leader in receiving yards (5,047) and touchdown receptions (77).

title: Authorities identify Springfield woman shot and killed on New Year's Day
author: Tom Ackerman
description: A Springfield woman who was shot and killed on New Year's Day has been identified. Here's what we know.
content:
A Springfield woman who was shot and killed on New Year's Day has been identified.
Kilanna Gladney, 31, died from a single gunshot wound, preliminary findings from an autopsy show.
Gladney was wounded with a gunshot on the 1600 block of South 17 th Street on Wednesday around noon. She was taken to HSHS St. John's Hospital's emergency room where she died shortly after noon.
Officers arrived to the scene around 11:40 a.m. and found Gladney.
No arrests have been made as of Friday morning.
The shooting is still under investigation.

title: Top performers: Mia Clark, Lincoln girls hoops upset Morton, plus other basketball results
author: Trevor Lawrence
description: Lincoln's Mia Clark made the go-ahead free throws against ranked Morton, plus other week's top performers
content:
This is a daily list of top performers from Springfield-area high school sports teams for Jan. 2-4, compiled from information provided to The State Journal-Register by coaches, athletic directors, and team statisticians.
Results can be emailed to sports@sj-r.com.
Saturday, Jan. 4
Girls Basketball
Game of the Night
LINCOLN — Lincoln jumped out to a 14-0 lead at the end of the first quarter but battled down the stretch to pull out a 52-50 win over state-ranked Morton at Roy S. Anderson Gymnasium.
Mia Clark made two free throws with 7.5 seconds left to give Lincoln the go-ahead score. Morton tied the game 50-50 when Ellie VanMeenen hit a layup with 19.5 on the clock.
Abby VanMeenen put up a contested shot at the buzzer, but Lincoln survived when the shot missed.
Paige Selke got Morton on the board with a putback basket on the Potters' first possession of the second quarter. By halftime, the Potters had trimmed the Railsplitters' lead to 22-14.
Makinley Knapp and Clark both scored 18 points apiece to lead Lincoln (8-6). Meanwhile, Lily Holmes scored 10 for the Railers.
Ellie VanMeenen led Morton (12-4) with 17 points, Abby VanMeenen had 12 and Salke finished with seven.
Morton was tied at No. 8 in the most recent Associated Press Class 3A high school girls basketball poll. Lincoln, the 2024 undefeated state champion in 3A, is unranked.
Morton defeated Chatham Glenwood 43-30 on Friday.
Izzy Hassebrock/Reese Watson, Sacred Heart-Griffin: Hassebrock and Watson buried three 3-pointers each and combined for 29 of SHG's points in a 41-34 defeat to Bloomington. Hassebrock led with 17 points and Watson scored 12.
Boys Basketball
Game of the Night
Lanphier rallied back from a 15-point deficit to beat Collinsville 67-59 in a nonconference boys basketball game at Lober-Nika Gymnasium.
Shaunassey Hatchett Jr., scored 16 of his game-high 26 points in the third quarter to spark the Lions' run. Collinsville (7-8) led 35-25 at halftime.
Lanphier forced Collinsville into 18 turnovers and outscored the Kahoks 23-6 off giveaways. Hatchett also led Lanphier with six rebounds and was 9-for-12 at the free-throw line.
JaiQuan Holman scored 13 points for the Lions (10-6) while Soriano Hayes contributed 12 points.
Lanphier outshot Collinsville 52.5% (21 of 40) to 44.0% (22-for-50), despite going 2-for-12 from behind the 3-point line. But the Lions scored 23 of their points at the free-throw line.
Donovan Coates led Collinsville with 23 points and had 11 rebounds. Collinsville outrebounded Lanphier 38-18, including 14 offensive boards. Evan Wilkinson added 10 points for the Kahoks.
Lanphier has alternated wins and losses over its last seven games. The Lions started the season 5-0 before suffering a three-game losing streak.
Blake Horn, Lincoln: He led Lincoln with 14 points in a 43-42 nonconference win over Rockford East at Roy S. Anderson Gymnasium. Brody Tungate was fouled by Rockford East with 1.6 seconds left, missed his first free throw before intentionally missing the second. Rockford East's Brian Harper attempted a full-court shot to win the game, but the heave fell harmlessly short of the basket. Karson Komnick scored 12 points off the bench for Lincoln and Gabe Smith added 10 points. The Railers nearly shot 50% and finished 17 of 35 (48.6%).
Cooper Schallenberg, Pleasant Plains: The Plains' senior scored 15 of his 17 points on five 3-pointers to lead the Cardinals past Warrensburg-Latham 50-41 in a nonconference game on Saturday. Grady Grisham poured in 10 in the win.
It is Warrensburg-Latham's third straight loss after a 14-0 start to the season. Two of the losses have come against Sangamo Conference teams: Pleasant Plains and Williamsville in the Williamsville Holiday Tournament championship game on Monday. Plains improved to 6-7.
Nathan Southern led Warrensburg with 12 points.
Owen Paluska, South County: The Vipers' junior led the team with 15 points in a 48-36 MSM Conference win over Nokomis. Paluska went scoreless in the first quarter but had five in the second and scored eight in the fourth, including going 6-for-8 at the free-throw line. Leo Bergschneider added 10 for the Vipers.
Ian Keller, Nokomis: The Nokomis senior scored 11 points before fouling out in the team's 48-36 loss to South County in an MSM Conference game.
Julian Rice, Riverton: The sophomore guard ushered a game-high 20 points in a 64-50 win over Pana.
Madyx Angel, Pana: The junior hit two 3s in the first quarter and finished with 19 points in the loss to Riverton.
Friday, Jan. 3
GIRLS BASKETBALL
Senior guard Kyleigh Heimsness hit a couple key 3s and Taylorville's 1-2-2 zone defense clamped down to withstand Springfield High's gritty comeback in a 63-56 win at Dolph Stanley Court.
The Senators (6-9) trailed 36-17 at halftime before clawing back within one possession, 48-45, on an Aniyah Rhinehouse layup with six minutes left in regulation.
A Grace Rogers steal and subsequent Heimsness 3 helped the Tornadoes (9-6) regain control in the final four minutes.
Taylorville senior guard Addison Tarr knocked down three 3s in the first half for a team-high 19 points. Heimsness and Rogers each had 15 points. Senior forward Mazie Fleming had nine points and eight rebounds.
'We started off strong and then Springfield finally found their rhythm and they were making a lot of shots,' Tarr said. 'We just had to come back together and play hard. It comes first on the defensive end. We rebounded well pretty well, I thought. We didn't give them a lot of second chances, so I think that helped a lot for sure.'
Freshman guard Abigail Malit sparked the Senators off the bench and scored 17 of her game-high 21 points in the second half. Senior forward Ariana Williams also carried the banner and shot 7 of 9 from the field for 17 points before fouling out in the fourth period.
SHS coach Brad Scheffler hopes that second-half effort can be a springboard for next week.
'The No. 1 team in the state is Washington (in Class 3A) and over Thanksgiving we were ahead of them the whole second half and they hit a 3 at the buzzer to beat us (52-50),' Scheffler said. 'I know if we can play with them, we can play with anybody. It's just being consistent and playing 32 minutes of good basketball. Right now with this group, we're mixing different lineups and trying different things to see what has success.
'Tonight we had success in the second half, so hopefully we'll continue that on to next week.'
— Bill Welt
Taylor Keirs/Fynlee Hart, North Mac: Keirs dropped a game-high 21 points and Hart followed with 16 in North Mac's 62-27 home victory over Bunker Hill.
BOYS BASKETBALL
Game of the Night
Sacred Heart-Griffin sophomore Tereik Hurd spurred a comeback with 12 points in the fourth period and the Cyclones rallied to beat Quincy Notre Dame 58-55 in a nonconference game at Jim Belz Gymnasium.
QND had its biggest lead of the game at 51-44 with 4 minutes, 21 seconds remaining in the fourth. Hurd then went on an 8-0 run by himself, scoring eight straight points that included a pair of 3-point plays to give the Cyclones a 52-51 advantage with 2:49 to go.
Surrounded by two free throws from Hurd, QND's Jace Allensworth scored a pair of baskets as the Raiders went ahead 55-54 with 43.7 left. SHG's Zion Lee then stuck a jumper and the Cyclones went back in front 56-55.
After a QND miss on its next possession, Myles Montgomery snared a rebound and was fouled and the sophomore drained two free throws with 9.8 remaining for a 58-55 SHG lead. The Raiders attempted a game-tying 3-pointer, but the shot was short as time expired.
Hurd finished with a team-high 18 points and he scored the first 12 points of the fourth quarter for the Cyclones. Lee scored 13 points, Cam Brinkman added 10 and Montgomery ended with six.
QND led 17-16 after one quarter before SHG went into halftime with a 34-31 lead. The Raiders went on a 9-0 run during the third period and led 45-42 heading into the fourth.
Allensworth netted a game-best 21 points for the Raiders (8-5).
Griffin McClure, Petersburg PORTA/A-C Central: The senior guard delivered a team-high 16 points in a 57-44 win over Rushville-Industry. Jett Kerrick (12), Gavin Gronewald (11) and Drew Marr (10) also reached double figures.
Bennett Fretueg, Rushville-Industry: The senior drained two 3s and finished with a game-high 17 points in the loss to PORTA.
Eli Cox, Rochester: The sophomore scored 16 points to lead the Rockets to their seventh win in a row with a 63-45 nonconference decision over Lexington. Rochester (10-3) has also won nine of their last 10 games. Nate Swaney, Khorbin Gregory and Kai Bruce all had eight apiece for the Rockets.
Ethan Saathoff, Litchfield: The Purple Panthers ' junior scored a team-high 13 points in a 57-34 nonconference loss to Troy Triad.
Caden Colwell, South County: In Bluffs, Colwell scored a team-high 12 points for the Vipers, but Winchester West Central avenged a 22-point loss to South County on Monday by beating the Vipers 44-33 on Friday. West Central (12-4) trailed 19-14 at halftime but outscored the Vipers (7-8) 22-4 in the third quarter to take a 13-point lead into the fourth.
Sawyer Hill/Carson Moscardelli, Athens: The duo combined for 12 of the team's 14 points in the first quarter and each finished with a game-high 14 points in a 67-23 win over Havana. Trevor Schilling supplied 12 points.
Brock Brown, Taylorville: The freshman drained four 3s to lead the Tornadoes with 17 points in a 60-36 win over Charleston. Drake Howard had 16 points.
Thursday, Jan. 2
GIRLS BASKETBALL
Game of the Night
Gillespie outscored Nokomis 13-3 in overtime and pulled out a 60-50 win in a nonconference home game.
Senior Mia Brawner, who finished with a game-best 21 points, scored four in OT to pace Gillespie (12-5). Sophomore Amari Vickery made a 3-pointer and scored four in overtime to finish with 13. Teammate Delaney Taylor hit one of her two 3s in the extra period and ended with 11.
After trailing 26-19 at halftime, Nokomis got within 36-33 after three quarters. NHS forced overtime by outscoring the Miners 11-8 in the fourth period, and the game was tied at 47 apiece at the end of regulation.
Junior Kinley Stolte and senior Natalie Brownback led NHS with 11 points each. Senior Grace DeWerff scored the only points for Nokomis in OT with a 3-pointer, finishing with two 3s in the game and 10 points. Sophomore Alivia Sabol added 10 points in the loss.
Aubrey Vogel, Carson Arthalony, Petersburg PORTA/A-C Central: Vogel nailed two 3-pointers and finished with a game-high 22 points, and Arthalony made five field goals with a trey while hitting 8 of 10 free throws for 19 points in PORTA's 51-39 home win over Hardin Calhoun.
Addison Wheatley, Auburn: The senior netted 12 of her team-high 14 points after halftime, and the visiting Trojans defeated Kincaid South Fork 45-36. Graysen Allen scored 12 points for Auburn.
Angelina Ippolito, Kincaid South Fork: She scored 16 second-half points and finished with a game-high 20 in Kincaid's home loss to Auburn.

title: Springfield hospitals limit visitors due to respiratory illness uptick
author: Tom Ackerman
description: If you have a loved one in the hospital in Springfield, you may want to coordinate when you're going to see them with other family members.
content:
Springfield hospitals are limiting visitors of patients in response to an uptick in certain respiratory illnesses.
Both Memorial Health and Hospital Sisters Health Systems announced restrictions that temporarily limit visitors to two per patient at any one time. All visitors must also be 18 years of age or older and show no signs of illness.
The Illinois Department of Public Health recommended temporary visitor restrictions because of a statewide increase in respiratory illness, a press release from Memorial health reads.
The IDPH said that hospital admissions ticked up for COVID-19, flu and RSV in the week ending Dec. 14. The percentage of emergency department visits due to respiratory illness also increased 13.8% in the previous week to 14.7%, the agency said in a news release on Dec. 23. Illinois is also continuing to see a rise in Intensive Care Unit admissions due to Respiratory Syncytial Virus, driven by children up to four years old.
Memorial Health applied the rules to the inpatient units at their five hospitals in Illinois, including Decatur, Jacksonville, Lincoln, Springfield, and Taylorville. The restrictions do not apply to outpatient Memorial Care locations, including urgent or primary care and laboratory or imaging appointments.
HSHS applied the rules at their Illinois and Wisconsin hospitals.
Memorial Health encourages the use of masks, but they are not required. They will provide disposable masks for interested visitors.
The hospitals also advise that soap and water or hand sanitizers are the some of the most effective ways to prevent respiratory illness transmission and should be used when entering and exiting patient rooms.
The Food and Drug Administration and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have approved new vaccines for COVID-19 and flu as well as updated who can receive the RSV vaccines.

title: Top performers: Auburn's Cooper Carter, Clayton Kessler combine for 45 points vs. Calvary
author: Trevor Lawrence
description: Auburn boys basketball had four players in double figures in dogfight win over Calvary on Tuesday, plus other top performances around Springfield
content:
This is a daily list of top performers from Springfield-area high school sports teams for Jan. 6-11, compiled from information provided to The State Journal-Register by coaches, athletic directors, and team statisticians.
Results can be emailed to sports@sj-r.com.
Tuesday, Jan. 7
Boys Basketball
Auburn coach Seth McCoy knows Calvary's Luke Blackford is a ton and a matchup with the Saints is always going to be a dogfight.
Blackford indeed scored a game-high 31 points, but Auburn prevailed 84-66 with four different players in double figures.
Auburn senior guard Cooper Carter scored 14 of his team-high 23 points in the third frame to withstand a late comeback, while senior forward Clayton Kessler had 22 points. Senior forward Ryan Lash and senior guard Carter Hunley totaled 14 and 10 points, respectively.
'Teams that want to single guys out are going to find that you're going to have to change your game plan on that because we have so many guys that can hurt you,' McCoy said. 'When you're playing with a good pace offensively, good things happen.'

title: 'Embarrassing for our city': Questions raised about process of naming new city clerk
author: Steven Spearie
description: Springfield has a new city clerk, but concerns were raised about how it happened. "I don't believe the process we used was fair to the voters."
content:
After four votes on various amendments and motions, and with some heightened emotion about the process, Ward 1 Ald. Chuck Redpath Sr. became Springfield's City Clerk, ending a nearly three-decade tenure on the city council.
Redpath, in his final term as Ward 1 alderman because of term limits, garnered five "yes" votes, including his own, at Tuesday's special city council meeting.
He replaces Frank Lesko, who held on to the clerk's seat until Dec. 31.
Lesko squeezed out a razor-thin victory over Josh Langfelder for the Sangamon County Recorder's seat and was sworn into the office on Dec. 2. Langfelder pursued a discovery recount, but a daunting court schedule and potential prohibitive costs made Langfelder decide not to pursue a petition the court for a full recount.
Redpath received other "yes" votes from Ward 7 Ald. Brad Carlson, Ward 8 Ald. Erin Conley, Ward 9 Ald. Jim Donelan and Ward 10 Ald. Ralph Hanauer, who nominated Redpath.
Ward 2 Ald. Shawn Gregory, Ward 3 Ald. Roy Williams Jr. and Ward 4 Ald. Larry Rockford voted against the amendment with Ward 5 Ald. Lakeisha Purchase and Ward 6 Ald. Jennifer Notariano voting "present."
Redpath, who was in law enforcement for more than three decades, was first elected to the city council in 1987, the year the form of government changed to an aldermanic form from a mayor-commissioner form, and has served since, except for an absence from 2007 to 2015.
"I approach this with a deep sense of responsibility, knowing how important this office is to our city," Redpath told the city council at the outset.
Redpath said he wanted to modernize the office as well as bring back stability. He planned to name a deputy clerk, possibly by this week, and a hire a full-time person dedicated to handling Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests.
Just two staff persons have been running the office, he said.
Redpath, 68, said he would not stand for election for clerk in April 2027.
Redpath's name was put forward as an amendment to an ordinance declaring the office vacant.
Only one other name was voted on, ironically, Langfelder's, but he didn't have enough votes to bump Redpath.
Gregory, Williams, Rockford and Notariano all questioned the process of gathering candidates' names and having a more robust vetting system.
City council members, not the mayor, nominate candidates for clerk.
Williams made a motion to send the ordinance back to the committee of the whole, in essence to delay the vote for Redpath, but it ended up in a 5-5 tie with Mayor Misty Buscher casting a "no" vote to break the tie.
"I don't believe the process we used was fair to the voters," Notariano said. "We came to them with a name (Redpath) and decided we would vote amongst ourselves. We didn't really allow the public to put forth names or put forth themselves.
"The people deserved to have a say."
That process also didn't sit well with some public commenters.
"My job at a retail clerk store puts more work in in finding (employees)," Ken Pacha said. "This is an elected position. Quite frankly, why does (Redpath) get to waltz into a city clerk position without an honest job search?
"This is embarrassing to the city."
Redpath maintained he played by the rules. When the position came open, he said he was asked by some people if he would consider taking the spot.
"I told the mayor I was interested in it," Redpath said. "I talked to every (alderperson). Once that ordinance was put up to the city council, everybody knew what was going on. It had to be a nomination from an (alderperson). People can't come up and just apply for it.
"I followed every rule. I was pushing to try to get if I could get the interest and I got the interest."
Redpath's daughter, Colleen Redpath Feger, holds the treasurer's job.
"This is my last shot," Redpath admitted. "She's just starting her career. She's a good treasurer. She's going to be fine."

title: Illinois residents may soon be able to own digital driver's licenses and state IDs
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Illinois residents may soon be able to present state identification by opening an app on their smartphone or smartwatch. Here's what you need to know.
content:
Illinois residents may soon be able to present state identification by opening an app on their smartphone or smartwatch.
The Illinois Secretary of State office has announced a goal of launching their initiative for residents to be able carry digital driver's licenses and state ID by the end of this year.
Here's what you need to know.
How will the IDs work?
The digital IDs will not be mandatory and will serve as a companion to the physical card, rather than a replacement.
Residents will be able to present their driver's license and State ID using their iPhone or Apple Watch by opening the " Apple Wallet" application on their device.
Users will be able to do this without taking out their physical card or handing over their device.
What if I don't have an iPhone or Apple Watch?
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias' office said they plan to offer the digital IDs to other digital wallets such as Google Wallet for Android users but did not provide a date.
What the advantage of a digital ID?
The office says the advantage of digital IDs are convenience and privacy, going so far as to say that presenting an ID in Apple Wallet will allow for more security and privacy than presenting a physical card in some cases.
Can I present the digital ID to rent a car or purchase alcohol?
Yes, users who purchase alcohol or rent a car will be able to present their ID without sharing more personal information than is needed, like their address. Residents will also be able to review and authorize the information being requested by scanning their face or finger before it is released to the merchant, according to a news release.
Still, upon request by law enforcement, a credential holder must provide their 'physical credential', according to a report from Capitol News Illinois. The law allows agencies and private entities to choose if they want to accept electronic IDs in place of physical ones.
Why is the state pursuing this?
The bill's sponsor, Rep. Kam Buckner D-Chicago, said previously in a news release that offering the digital ID would bring Illinoisians up to speed with other states.
'Other states already have mobile driver's licenses and ID cards, and this bill gives our residents the same ability to have a mobile card if they want one, while still providing them with the option of a traditional physical card,' the representative told Capitol News Illinois this past summer.
How can I get the digital ID?
Interested residents can sign up to receive updates about the program and when it will be available. Visit ilsos.gov/mDL to sign up.

title: New Springfield restaurant offering authentic middle eastern food
author: Claire Grant
description: If you're in the mood for a shawarma wrap, you may want to check out one of the newest Springfield restaurants.
content:
If you're in the mood for a shawarma wrap, you may want to check out one of the newest Springfield restaurants.
Almadina Halal restaurant opened on Dec. 23 last year at 3109 Chatham Road, just across from the Chatham Square shopping center. The restaurant serves authentic middle eastern and southeast Asian meals, making it a rare find in Springfield.
Whether you're a fan of deep-fried and spiced chickpea falafel, lamb gyros or chicken biryani, a highly seasoned rice dish with bits of chicken from southeast Asia, the food is halal.
Halal is an Arabic word meaning 'permitted' in Islamic teachings toward food and drink Muslim people are allowed to have. Halal meats are the only type of meat observant Muslim people can eat. The meat is slaughtered before being bled dry and has lived on a natural diet through a healthy life to meet religious standards.
Hamood Hizam co-owns the business with Abdulrahman Alyafi and Hani Almnamer. Hizam spends his time in the back kitchen roasting chicken on skewers with Alyafi.
This isn't the only establishment run by the team as Alyafi co-owns Almadina International Foods mart at 2700 W. Lawrence Ave., one of the few places in the capital city to find middle eastern ingredients.
The co-owners said the idea to open a restaurant was initiated from customers saying they wanted more to-go options. Originally planning on a food truck, Alyfi pivoted at the opportunity when Amer Snober, owner of Fresh Hut, was leaving his location. When Fresh Hut closed leaving the kitchen equipment behind, the co-owners leapt at the opportunity.
'We took over from Amer and basically just before we opened then officially after that,' Almnamer said. 'We were thinking a year and a half ago or so opening a place just for middle eastern food. … when (Snober) was closing Fresh Hut one day before closing he called me and told me to come and buy that (location) so we did.'
Snober recently re-opened his restaurant California Kitchen in the old Kentucky Fried Chicken building at 1111 N. Ninth St. on Dec. 26, following a fire in the late summer of last year which shuttered his location at 1132 N. Ninth St.
The co-owners said they still intend to launch a food truck in the future after settling into their establishment and growing a customer base. Finding a distributor for halal ingredients is hard in central Illinois, so long drives and importing are typical. Almadina Foods imports produce from Chicago and Detroit, while meat comes from St. Louis.
Almnamer wants more people to experience middle eastern cuisine if they've never tried before, as most dishes are marinated and savory with familiar pairings like rice or french fries. If lamb or falafel isn't up your alley, the business also sells fried chicken and sandwiches.
Shawarma is meat marinated usually with lemon, spices and olive oil slow roasted to be tender and juicy. Chicken Mandi is a Yemeni smokey chicken and rice dish prepared with a lime and melted butter marinade.
The restaurant is open from 10 a.m. to midnight seven days a week.

title: Sangamon County home listings asked for less money in December - see the current median price here
author: The State Journal-Register
description: Here's a look at how monthly real estate listings changed in Sangamon County last month.
content:
The median home in Sangamon County listed for $172,500 in December, down 13.7% from the previous month's $199,900, an analysis of data from Realtor.com shows.
Compared to December 2023, the median home list price increased 4.6% from $165,000.
The statistics in this article only pertain to houses listed for sale in Sangamon County, not houses that were sold. Information on your local housing market, along with other useful community data, is available at data.sj-r.com.
Sangamon County's median home was 1,633 square feet, listed at $108 per square foot. The price per square foot of homes for sale is up 2.5% from December 2023.
Listings in Sangamon County moved briskly, at a median 46 days listed compared to the December national median of 70 days on the market. In the previous month, homes had a median of 40 days on the market. Around 114 homes were newly listed on the market in December, a 9.6% increase from 104 new listings in December 2023.
The median home prices issued by Realtor.com may exclude many, or even most, of a market's homes. The price and volume represent only single-family homes, condominiums or townhomes. They include existing homes, but exclude most new construction as well as pending and contingent sales.
Across the Springfield metro area, median home prices fell to $164,950, down 0.1% from a month earlier. The median home had 1,649 square feet, at a list price of $107 per square foot.
In Illinois, median home prices were $292,450, a slight decrease from November. The median Illinois home listed for sale had 1,671 square feet, with a price of $175 per square foot.
Throughout the United States, the median home price was $402,502, a slight decrease from the month prior. The median American home for sale was listed at 1,800 square feet, with a price of $222 per square foot.
The median home list price used in this report represents the midway point of all the houses or units listed over the given period of time. Experts say the median offers a more accurate view of what's happening in a market than the average list price, which would mean taking the sum of all listing prices then dividing by the number of homes sold. The average can be skewed by one particularly low or high price.

title: How long before you get frostbite in extreme cold weather? This chart will show you
author: Tom Ackerman
description: How long can you be outside in extreme cold weather? This chart will show you how quickly it can happen.
content:
When a severe cold comes along, we are safest when we know the most up to date information about hypothermia and frostbite.
Frostbite is an injury caused by freezing, according to the U.S. Center for Disease Control and Prevention. You might have frostbite if you lose feeling and color in an affected area, which is usually in our extremities like the nose, ears, cheeks, chin, fingers, and toes.
The cold-induced injury can permanently damage the body and possibly lead to amputation.
In sub-zero degree temperatures, a person can get frostbite in less than 30 minutes, according to the National Weather Service.
Do I have frostbite?
Early signs of frostbite may look like redness or pain in any skin area.
Other signs are when an area of skin is colored white or grayish-yellow, when the skin that feels unusually firm or waxy, or numbness.
What is hypothermia?
Hypothermia is a possibly dangerous drop in body temperature that usually happens in very cold temperatures. However, the condition can also take hold when the temperature is above 40 degrees, according to the CDC.
In adults, symptoms can be:
Shivering
Exhaustion
Confusion
Fumbling hands
Memory loss
Slurred speech
Drowsiness
In infants, hypothermia can look like:
Bright red or colored skin
Very low energy
What to do if you think you have frostbite or hypothermia
If you think you are experiencing hypothermia or frostbite, you should get medical help as soon as possible. Hypothermia is a more serious condition and requires emergency medical care.
People with a temperature below 95 degrees should immediately find medical help.
For someone experiencing frostbite but not hypothermia, a second-best option to medical care is to get to a warm room or shelter.
Then, remove any wet clothing and warm yourself under dry layers of blankets and clothing.
People should also place their frostbite-affected areas in warm-to-touch water.
What NOT to do if you think you have frostbite
Do not walk on your feet or toes if you think those areas are affected.
Do not use a fireplace, heat lamp, radiator, or stove for warming.
Do not use a heating pad or electric blanket for warming.
Do not rub or massage affected areas.
Who is most at risk?
People most at risk for these conditions are older adults, particularly if they do not have access to proper food, clothing or heating.
Additionally, people who stay outdoors for long periods of time should be wary.
People who drink alcohol excessively or use certain drugs should also be wary.
Lastly, people should look out for babies sleeping in cold rooms.

title: How this freshman guard lifted Springfield High girls to repeat City title
author: Bill Welt
description: This freshman said she was nervous but provided the spark and carried Springfield High to at least a share of repeat City girls basketball title
content:
Abigail Malit stepped up like a veteran.
The Springfield High freshman guard scored eight of the team's first nine points and finished with a game-high 19 points to clinch at least a share of the program's second straight City girls basketball title at the Bank of Springfield Center on Friday.
The Senators (13-9 overall) can secure the crown outright with a win over Sacred Heart-Griffin on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. It is their first repeat title since 2014-19, when they won six straight.
'It's fun to see the growth of these guys,' said SHS coach Brad Scheffler, who has won 15 City titles over 22 seasons at SHS. 'These guys were 6-9 at the start of January and we've won seven in a row, hopefully we can keep it going tomorrow night.'
Get to know Malit
Southeast (13-9) jumped ahead 8-0 early until Malit snuffed out the ball on the defensive end for a couple layups. Malit had 12 points in the first half for a 21-13 halftime lead.
'I feel like us pressuring really allowed me to get the steals and I feel like overall the defense really played a part,' Malit said.
This wasn't her first game as a starter, but she is still learning the nuances of the offense. That development is being assisted by other experienced starters such as seniors Keziah Toran and Ariana Williams as well as junior Aniyah Rhinehouse.
Toran supplied 16 points.
'I feel like Keziah and all the rest of the team played a big part in that as well because me being a freshman, I was really nervous out there on the court — my first City tournament,' Malit said. 'They really helped guide me and honestly I wouldn't have been able to do it without them.'
Springfield area top performers: Anna Weber, Plains capture Sangamon County girls title
'Fun to see'
Malit wasn't the only freshman on the floor. Guard Morgan Leininger had a key assist on an inbounds pass to senior forward Jameara Townsend in the fourth quarter — not to mention a dagger 3 with under three minutes left. Scheffler's daughter, Chloe, also pitched in with six rebounds.
'It's fun to see not only for this year but for the future years, too,' Scheffler said of the team's growth.
Townsend delivered nine points and eight rebounds off the bench. She dislocated her shoulder against Normal U-High on Jan. 11 before returning to practice this week.
'For her to play this weekend shows her toughness,' Scheffler said.
Sophomore guard Navehua Collier led Southeast with 13 of her 15 points in the second half. Juniors Corrine Pickett and Zaria Weston had nine apiece.
Sacred Heart-Griffin 65, Lanphier 25: Izzy Hassebrock shot 3 of 6 from 3-point range and led the Cyclones with 19 points. Norah Long and Gigi Gray had 11 points apiece. Reese Watson spurred a hot start with back-to-back 3s in the first quarter for all her points.
Amiyah Jarrett led Lanphier with eight points and eight rebounds.

title: Here are some places around the world that are warmer than Springfield today
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Even for tried-and-true Midwesterners, the weather admittedly feels cold. This "brr" got us wondering – where is it warmer today in the world?
content:
Even for tried-and-true Midwesterners, the weather admittedly feels cold.
Monday brought wind chill values of -7 and 3 in Springfield, with gusts as high as 21 mph, according to the National Weather Service.
That cold likely won't let up until around Wednesday.
The "brr" got us wondering: where is it warmer today in the world?
Here are four such places.
Longyearbyen, Norway
Weather in this Norwegian archipelago in the Arctic Ocean is predicted to be warmer than Springfield on Tuesday.
Longyearbyen is expected to see a high of 14 tomorrow, while Springfield is predicted to see a high near 7 and gusts as high as 17 mph.
The town with 2,400 residents from over 50 counties is 'inhabited by nature enthusiasts who live in close unity under tough climatic conditions with the High Arctic wilderness right on their doorstep,' according to a tourist site for the archipelago, also called Svalbard.
The area sees 24-hour darkness in the winter and is known to be an ideal place to see the northern lights.
Barrow, Alaska
Barrow (also known as Utqiagvik) is the northernmost city in the United States. The town is surrounded on three sides by the Arctic Ocean. From October through May, the temperature rarely gets above freezing.
At 9 a.m. Monday, it was 26 degrees in Barrow.
Pituffik Space Base, Greenland
Formerly known as Thule Air Base, Pituffik is on the northwest coast of Greenland -- about 750 miles north of the Arctic Circle.
The place gets so cold that they have to use tugboats to move icebergs around to get ships in with supplies, according to a USA Today report. That's in the summer, when they can actually get ships into the port.
Pituffik saw a high of 6 on Monday.
Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
Springfield is predicted to be colder than the Mongolian capital tomorrow, which is expected to see a high of 18.
This place is known to be the coldest national capital in the world, due to its location deep in the interior of Asia and its high elevation.

title: Casino night fundraiser, historic Valentine's Day celebration happening in Springfield
author: Claire Grant
description: This weekend, roll the dice and play your hand with a Casino night to benefit a local school district or have an historic Valentine's Day celebration.
content:
This weekend, roll the dice and play your hand with a casino night to benefit a local school district, or step back centuries to celebrate Valentine's Day how the Victorians did.
Here are five things to do this weekend in Springfield.
Casino Night at the Firefighters Lake Club
What: Hosted by the Rochester Education Foundation and held at the Firefighters Lake Club, one ticket will buy you a night of appetizers, draft beer and gambling. In addition, a silent auction with prizes and cocktail hour will run alongside the boards. All funds raised this year will go directly to funding grants for innovative projects and programs that encourage student achievement, enhance educational opportunities, and support academic excellence throughout Rochester CUSD 3A.
More: Tickets are $60 per person on the Rochester Education Foundation Eventbrite and includes up to $1,000 in chips. Tickets at the door will be raised to $75.
Puzzle Day at the Kidzeum
What: From jigsaw puzzles and Rubix's cubes to riddles and brain teasers, we're here to celebrate the most befuddling thought experiments ever made. All puzzle-related programming will be free with general admission tickets with the exception of our escape room, which will require an additional fee.
When: 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sunday
Where: 412 E. Adams St., Springfield
More: Prizes will be awarded to the little scientists for completing puzzles.
The Ragin' Cajun at Donnie B's
What: Presenting as a showstopper for Donnie B's Comedy Show 26th Season, John Morgan is helping Springfield to a heaping helping of The Ragin' Cajun' Southern charm at your local club this Friday and Saturday. Morgan has worked steadily at comedy clubs, corporate events, and musical arenas. He has made national television appearances on MTV, Showtime, and Night Watch with Charlie Rose. He has been the opening act for Kathleen Madigan, Michael Bolton, The Monkeys, Ronnie Cole, Jerry Seinfeld and Helen Reddy.
When: 8 p.m. Friday, 7:30 p.m. Saturday
Where: 2200 Meadowbrook Road, Springfield
Winter Fungi Workshop
What: Kathy and Michael Egan return to Lincoln Memorial Garden to share additional mushroom knowledge this weekend. This is a follow-up workshop to the first which took place in 2024. Topics of the second workshop will include log-grown mushrooms versus compost-grown mushrooms, ways to incorporate mushrooms into a diet to capture their vitamin D health benefits as well as tea and how to brew these fun guys.
When: 1 p.m. Saturday
Historic Valentines
What: Ever wanted to make Victorian Era Valentines or want to know more about how the holiday was celebrated a century ago? The Historic Edwards Place is offering a workshop combining the two into one fun day. The workshop offers information about the general history of valentines and illustrations of original Victorian, Civil War era cards and envelopes. Participants will have the opportunity to construct their own Victorian valentines in much the same way as in the 1800s.
When: 9 a.m. to noon Saturday
Where: 700 N. Fourth St., Springfield
More: This workshop will take place on the 1st floor of Historic Edwards Place, which has an accessible entrance through the SAA office.
Can't make the workshop or want something cute and custom to hang up for Valentine's Day? Friday and Saturday the women at Wooden It Be Lovely will host a pop-up sale for the hearty holiday.

title: All of Springfield's McDonald's soon to be owned by same person
author: Natalie Morris
description: Come Saturday, all 11 Golden Arches in the Capital City will be owned by the same franchise operator.
content:
AI-assisted summary
This marks the first time since 1999 that a single franchisee owns all of the McDonald's restaurants in Springfield.
Springfield's lone Quiznos is under new ownership.
Greenie's Grill Food Truck opens brick-and-mortar location in Rochester.
All of the McDonald's restaurants in Springfield are soon to be owned by the same man.
As of Feb. 1, Mike Kasprzyk will own all 11 Golden Arches in the Capital City after purchasing two stores from to other franchise operators, Dr. Paul and Mary Breznay and Kim Derringer, in December.
The back-to-back acquisitions doubled Kasprzyk's Springfield footprint after only entering the market last year.
'I stand on the shoulders of giants. A lot of great families before us,' said Kasprzyk, sole owner of the newly christened Capital City McDonalds franchise. He is only the third to capture the entire market since the first McDonald's opened in Springfield in 1957.
'It all happened rather quick, organically. The other owners were looking to retire or relocate.'
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
The Springfield resident said the size and scale possible with a single franchise operator will translate to more consistent customer service and more opportunities for staff.
Kasprzyk bought his first McDonald's franchise in 2015, but didn't dip his toes into the local market until January 2024 when Brad Davis retired, selling his six Springfield locations.
The Springfield market has been carved up among several, frequently rotating franchisees for the past 26 years. But that doesn't reflect the chain's longer history in the Capital City.
John Mack introduced Springfield diners to the brand in 1957—a decade before the chain's signature sandwich, the Big Mac, debuted. Mack and his children had sole franchise rights for the market until selling to the McGraw family in 1989.
McGraw Enterprises held Springfield's McDonald monopoly for a decade before selling two locations to former employees in 1999. A year later they sold four west side holdings, including the Chatham location, to Kasprzyk's parents, Joe and Revella, who already had been running the McDonald's in Jacksonville for a decade.
The senior Kasprzyk's have since retired. Their son Mike now owns the Jacksonville store, as well as locations in Chatham, Beardstown, Havana and Mt. Sterling.
The headquarters for Capital City McDonalds will be in Jacksonville.
New cafe opens
Java Junction opened Tuesday in White Oaks Mall's center court.
The new cafe, located in the footprint of the former Gloria Jean's Coffee, features grilled wraps, sandwiches and soups, as well as a breakfast menu. The beverage selection includes a full line of espressos and other hot and cold caffeinated drinks.
Table and counter seating available. Operating hours are 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Thursday, 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday and noon to 6 p.m. Sunday. However, orders can be filled as early at 7:30 a.m. on weekdays via online or phone orders and delivered curbside outside the mall entrance just west of Dick's Sporting Goods
Phone: 217-572-1237.
Dalton Ingram is the sole owner of Java Junction.
Permanent lunch menu
Wednesday lunch hours are now a permanent offering at Bloom Wine Bar & Floral after a successful test run for the downtown establishment in December.
'We've had a lot of repeat customers, a lot of positive reviews, surrounding chatter for us to decide it was worth our time,' said Brittney Robinson, who co-owns the business at 2 S. Old State Capitol Plaza with partners Caitlin Becker and Hannah Goss.
The lunch menu includes soups, sandwiches and salads, as well as Bloom's standing nibbles of flatbreads, dips and charcuterie spreads. The lunch menu is available Wednesdays and Saturdays from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. Dine in, take out available. Reservations recommended via Bloom's website at www.bloomspringfield.com. Phone: 217/679-1830.
New ownership
New ownership at Springfield's sole standalone Quiznos is taking the sandwich shop in a different direction. Literally.
Samantha Clardy has purchased the toasted sandwich shop at 2701 W. Lawrence Ave. from her former bosses, Matt and Toni Hurt. The Hurts continue to operate the Denver-based chain on the Lincoln Land Community College campus.
Clardy said the only change customers will notice at the Lawrence Avenue locale is a new traffic flow. Patrons will begin placing orders at the cash register and then proceed to have their custom orders made.
The Hurts opened the Lawrence Avenue sandwich chain location in 2004 before opening a satellite site on LLCC's main campus in 2018.
New brick-and-mortar location
Fans of Greenie's Grill Food Truck no longer have to wait for better weather to enjoy their favorite smashburgers.
Operators Adam Greenfield and Kayla Webster opened a brick-and-mortar location, Greenie's Grill Rochester, Jan. 25 in a footprint carved out of the former Rochester IGA building.
'(The food truck) was going well. As it took off, we realized a store front would be crucial for this business model to be sustained year round,' Greenfield said.
Greenie's Grill Rochester has an open kitchen format with food cooked to order while customers watch.
The menu highlights a variety of smashburgers made with fresh ground beef from Humphrey's Market. Other selections include cheese steaks, sandwiches, wraps, horseshoes and appetizers.
Hours are 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday. The quick service, carry out establishment has limited seating but is located next to The Back 9 bar and golf course simulator. Phone: 217-498-1038.
Greenie's Grill Food Truck will continue to accept bookings for events only.
The A La Carte column highlights restaurant openings, closings, renovations and relocations, as well as personnel changes and business news. Natalie Morris can be reached at 217/737-7254 or by email at natalie.sjr@gmail.com.

title: Illinois lawmakers file bill to repeal 'Trust Act,' require police to work with ICE
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Illinois Republicans announced they would again try to repeal a law that limits law enforcement's participation in federal immigration enforcement.
content:
Show Caption
Illinois Senate Republicans Tuesday announced they would again try to repeal a law that limits state and local law enforcement's participation in federal immigration enforcement.
Sponsors seek to reverse aspects of the 2017 law that prohibits law enforcement from participating, supporting or assisting the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Illinois law enforcement can currently only work with ICE if presented with a federal criminal warrant or otherwise required by federal law.
Senate Bill 1313 would rather require state law enforcement agencies to cooperate with ICE, 'ensuring undocumented immigrants charged with or convicted of a felony are identified, reported, and deported,' according to a news release.
The bill is sponsored by State Sen. Neil Anderson (R-Andalusia) and was filed Tuesday morning. Additional legislation, sponsored by State Senators Terri Bryant (R-Murphysboro) and Andrew Chesney (R-Freeport), seeks to repeal the Illinois TRUST Act in its entirety.
Multiple bills aiming to repeal the Act were filed in the last two-year General Assembly session that ended earlier this month.
HB4187 was filed in October of 2023 with around 35 sponsors and was referred to the Rules Committee. It would need to be reintroduced in the current session for it to still be considered.
Already in this session, multiple repeal bills for the Act have been filed that have been referred to the Rules Committee.

title: Creating a Fury: Springfield native part of Grammy-nominated blues album
author: Steven Spearie
description: Springfield has a rooting interest in the 67th Grammy Awards this weekend.
content:
Springfield has a rooting interest in the 67th Grammy Awards on Feb. 2.
Sacred Heart-Griffin High School and Millikin University graduate Mary Lemanski was a guest artist on Antonio Vergara's album "The Fury," which earned a nomination in the Best Contemporary Blues Album category.
Chappell Roan, Teddy Swims, Sabrina Carpenter and Billie Eilish are among the Grammys' scheduled performers.
Who is Mary Lemanski?
A Springfield native now living in Downers Grove, Lemanski is a singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist who has been putting out her own music since 1999.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
Lemanski plays and writes music in a number of different genres, including pop-rock, hip-hop, country, jazz and classical.
In addition to being an artist, Lemanski has taught music business, piano, voice, songwriting and composing and has worked extensively in the music industry, including stints at Epitaph Records, BMG Entertainment and Clear Channel Radio/iHeart Radio. She has a certification in audio engineering from the Conservatory of Recording Arts & Sciences, and an MBA in e-business from the University of Phoenix.
The mother of two children, Lemanski has a large extended family and is a cousin of former Springfield Mayor Jim Langfelder.
Lemanski created a national stir--and found herself out a job with the DuPage County Democrats--in 2021 over social media posts linking the Kyle Rittenhouse verdict to the killings in a Waukesha, Wisconsin, parade.
Antonio Vergara's career
A native of Ecuador, Vergara is a heralded blues guitarist, vocalist and lap steel player who has appeared on over 90 albums as a sideman. He previously was nominated for a Latin Grammy.
Also an attorney and educator, "The Fury" is Vergara's 12th solo project.
Vergara is up against Joe Bonamassa and Shemekia Copeland, among others, for the Best Contemporary Blues Album.
Collaboration on 'The Fury'
Lemanski said she has been friends with Vergara for over a decade through online networking.
"He's liked some of my past work, so he invited me to contribute to ('The Fury')," Lemanski said.
That turned out to be a spoken word piece on "Outro," a 14-minute musical mosaic that is the last track on the album.
In 2017, Lemanski collaborated with Indian composer Rupam Sarmah, whose album "Together in Peace" went to No. 1 on Billboard World Music chart.
How to listen to 'The Fury'
Listen to "The Fury" here: https://antoniovergara.ffm.to/thefury
How to watch 2025 Grammy Awards
The awards show airs live on CBS at 7 p.m. (Springfield time).
Paramount+ subscribers with the Showtime add-on can stream the Grammys live. Paramount+ subscribers with any plan can stream it the day after it airs. Live streaming services that include CBS in their lineup, include Hulu + Live TV, YouTube TV and FuboTV.
Various news outlets will offer red carpet coverage on Feb. 2.
Presentation of Best Contemporary Blues Album comes during a separate Grammy ceremony.

title: New community center for children opening on Springfield's east side this spring
author: Claire Grant
description: Better Life Better Living For Kidz is ready to open a community center focused on building the groundwork to success for children on the east side.
content:
After almost a decade of planning, Better Life Better Living for Kidz is ready to open a community center on the east side.
The nonprofit started Sunday Funday at Comer Cox Park in 2015.
Now, the nonprofit is seeking additional funding to keep their programs running for children.
After almost a decade of planning and four years of placing the building blocks, Better Life Better Living for Kidz is ready to open a community center focused on building the groundwork to success for children on the east side.
The Better Life Better Living For Kidz Community Center is set to open at 1507 E. Cook St. on March 1 taking the location used previously by the New Hope Missionary Baptist Church.
The after-school program will provide a computer lab, audio and video studio and coding classes. The center will also offer financial literary classes and a chess team.
President of the organization Better Life Better Living For Kidz, M'Banna Kantako II, said children will be required to wear membership badges for identification, and each badge will cost $5 per month.
'It's just a membership fee, that's why we made it so cheap,' Kantako said. 'We want the parents to be invested into the program as well.'
Kantako's dream for children in Springfield having a better life stem back to 2015, through the start of Sunday Fundays in Comer Cox Park. The idea was to create a local space for kids to engage with each other in a safe environment.
Kantako's non-profit started working toward making that dream space a reality.
However, funding has been a recurring barrier to the program, through both the city and state. Originally applying for funding under the "The Teen Empowerment Zone" project, the organization's board of directors felt a hard stop after the previous mayor, Jim Langfelder left office.
Kantako said the organization pushed to begin work on the project out of pocket.
'All we do is hear complaints about the children of the east side,' Kantako said. 'Our position is that we cannot continue to do the same thing over and over expecting different results.'
After four years, the group was approved for the statewide Community Connections Grant for up to $215,000. The grant was issued to decrease violence on the eastside from August to this July through a reimbursement model.
The reimbursement model was its own barrier, according to the grassroots organization. A reimbursement grant has nonprofits spend up to the funding cap with their own finances and then present the receipts to be reimbursed.
Originally asking for the capital upfront because the nonprofit lacked the funding, Kantako said the organization was denied. Turning to the city, Antwaun Readus Sr, who runs First Class Barbershop on Welsey Street and is vice president of BLBL4K, shared his and the organizations struggles at an Oct. 29 city council meeting about the violence in the city, and how the nonprofit could keep kids away from it.
In November, with the help of Ward 2 Ald. Shawn Gregory, whose ward the center falls in, the city approved a recurring loan of $30,000 up to $215,000 for the organization, starting in January of this year, five months through the funding timeline.
'With our organization being completely grassroots, that stipulation sets us up for failure,' Kantako said. 'Not to mention the looming deadline of when the funds have to be exhausted.'
The remaining funds the nonprofit plans to use before time runs out will be spent entirely on programs for the children, including Sunday Funday at Cox Park.
The location will be open until 9 p.m. and will be operating a summer program with classwork and field trips. Parents can apply at betterlifebetterlivingforkidz@gmail.com or at the front desk, once the center opens.
Kantako says the nonprofit is still searching for additional funding, as the loans from the city are limited to $30,000 a month, in a seven-month span. That puts a cap on the center, Kantako hopes to raise in time through supplicant grants.
'Of course sustainability is the goal, but we just couldn't wait any longer,' Kantako said.

title: Trump to talk tariffs with leaders of Canada and Mexico: 'They owe us a lot of money'
author: Swapna Venugopal Ramaswamy
description: Trump has said tariffs are a way to force the countries to stop the flow of migrants and fentanyl across the borders and into the U.S.
content:
Show Caption
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump said he will talk to leaders from Canada and Mexico on Monday, a day before the 25% tariffs he imposed on the country's top two trading partners go into effect.
Within hours of Trump's Saturday order, Canada's Prime Minister Justin Trudeau hit back with tit-for-tat retaliatory 25% tariffs on American goods. Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum said she was considering "tariff and non-tariff measures in defense of Mexico's interests."
"I'm speaking with Prime Minister Trudeau tomorrow morning and I'm also speaking with Mexico tomorrow morning," Trump said Sunday, as he landed at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland, after flying back from his Florida home. "They owe us a lot of money, and I'm sure they're going to pay."
Trump has said tariffs are a way to force the countries to stop the flow of migrants and fentanyl across the borders and into the U.S. Tariffs have been central to Trump's economic strategy, leaning on them to increase tax revenue and protect jobs. He also views them as tools to aid negotiations with various countries.
On Sunday, Trump also said he wanted the countries to "balance out their trade, number one."
According to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, the U.S. goods trade deficit with Canada was $80.1 billion in 2022, a 68% increase over 2021. Meanwhile, the trade deficit with Mexico stood at $131.1 billion in 2022, a 24% increase over 2021.
A lower tariff of 10% was set for Canadian energy, including natural gas and oil. Trump also has imposed 10% tariffs on goods from China, starting on Tuesday.
During a news briefing with reporters on Saturday, Trudeau said he had not spoken to Trump since his inauguration. Trump said Americans could feel some "short-term pain" from the emerging trade war.
"But long term, the United States has been ripped off by virtually every country in the world," he said, adding that the U.S. had trade deficits with "almost" every country.
"We're going to change it," Trump affirmed. "It's been unfair."
