title: Lawmakers weighing use of solitary confinement in Illinois prison. Here's what to know.
author: Patrick M. Keck
description: Supporters say the use of solitary confinement has drastic negative impact on inmates' mental health, often lasting beyond their prison sentence.
content:
Last year, Gov. J.B. Pritzker signed legislation making it illegal to confine incarcerated youth in solitary confinement for any purpose other than preventing immediate physical harm. Now advocates and lawmakers are calling for limits of the practice for incarcerated adults.
There appeared to be momentum brewing during the spring session for such legislation — dubbed the Nelson Mandela Act — passing out of committee and wracking up dozens of Democratic co-sponsors. If passed, it would have limited solitary confinement to no more than 10 consecutive days or 10 days within a 180-day period.
Supporters say the use of solitary confinement has drastic negative impact on inmates' mental health, often lasting beyond their prison sentence. The limits would have at least lessened the psychological toll, they said.
But then the legislation was amended.
Now referred to as the Restrictive Housing Data Publication and Verification Act, the pending legislation would require the Illinois Department of Corrections to post quarterly updates on how it uses restrictive housing on its website.
Starting Jan. 1, 2025, the department would also submit an annual report to the governor and the General Assembly accessible to the general public.
House Bill 4828 passed in the House 73-40 in the closing days of the spring session and now awaits a vote in the Senate. Lawmakers return to Springfield after the election for a six-day veto session in November, where the measure could be passed then or during the January lame duck.
Rep. Kevin Olickal, D-Skokie, led the bill in the House. His hope is the upper chamber takes it up in veto session, saying a "sense of urgency" exists in bringing the legislation to the governor's desk.
The corrections department, he told The State Journal-Register, understood the intent of his legislation but felt that more research was necessary before a law could be crafted. The amended version also saw the Illinois Sheriffs Association, who opposed HB 4828 in its original form since it applied to county jails, remove its position.
"There's a huge difference between a prison and a jail," ISA executive director Jim Kaitschuk said during a phone interview earlier this week, describing the association's position. "The nature of jail is much more transient population. So what if I only had one inmate? I'd be in violation of this act."
Olickal and Restore Justice policy director Lindsey Hammond believe that the data would provide more insight on the harms of unrestricted solitary confinement. However, based on what is known already, they want these limitations in statute soon.
"We obviously still want to restrict or even abolish solitary confinement in the state," said Hammond during a Sept. 11 interview. "It's a form of torture...we have a human rights crisis in our prisons."

title: Springfield-area woman turning 112 years old is likely state's oldest resident
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Wenonah Bish turns 112 years next week. Bish is likely the oldest person in the state and one of the oldest people in the country.
content:
A Springfield-area woman is likely the be oldest living resident in Illinois.
Wenonah Bish, who currently lives in Sherman, will be turning 112 on Oct. 2.
The State Journal-Register got the chance to celebrate with Bish last year when she blew out the candles as the likely second oldest person in the state at the time. The former eldest person lived in Maywood.
Bish's family describes her as someone who prefers to look at what's coming rather than what's behind her. She loves calling and talking to her daughter Delores throughout the day, in addition to speaking with her grandson Dirk, who lives in Miami, and her grandson Don who lives in the Dominican Republic.
Last year, Sangamon County Clerk Don Gray confirmed that Bish was the oldest living voter in the county. Further, the family provided a copy of the birth certificate (For history buffs, Dwight H. Green was the governor at the time, who is listed at the top of the document).
It is possible that others in the state may be older, but they may not have made contact with the organizations that keep track of the data.
Bish is believed to be the 12th oldest person in the U.S. and the 55th oldest person in the world, according to the Gerontology Research Group, which tracks the ages of supercentenarians, or people who have lived to be 110 and older.

title: Investigator: 'Inconsistencies' in statements given by murder defendant who pleaded guilty
author: Steven Spearie
description: Neither defendant in the triple murder case took the stand Tuesday.
content:
Attorneys for two defendants on trial for a triple murder in the Harvard Park neighborhood in 2021 again on Tuesday pressed that stories from a third defendant who pleaded guilty two weeks ago changed as the lead investigator in the case took the stand for a second day.
Attorneys for Kelton Galmore of Jacksonville and Larry McClain Jr. of Springfield did not put on any witnesses after the prosecution rested its case. Both declined to take the stand when asked by Presiding Circuit Judge Ryan Cadagin.
Galmore and McClain could face 45 years to natural life behind bars on each count and mandatory life if convicted on two or more first-degree murder counts. Any sentence would have to be served at 100%.
Closing arguments are scheduled for 9 a.m. Wednesday before the case goes to the seven-man, five-woman jury.
Savante English, 27, and Keyera Gant, 25, of Springfield, and Bryant K. Williams, 27, of Houston, Texas, were all fatally shot in a house in the 2500 block of South 10th Street on Aug. 9, 2021.
English and Williams, a budding rapper in the Houston area who went by the name BK Yola, were childhood friends in Springfield. Williams was scheduled to return to Texas the day of the murder.
English and Gant were cousins.
Attorneys Monroe McWard and Mark Wykoff again tried to bring into question the believability of Joseph Hembrough's testimony.
Hembrough, who like Galmore and McClain was charged with three counts of first-degree murder, pleaded guilty on the eve of the trial and was sentenced to 20 years in the Department of Corrections.
Hembrough testified against Galmore and McClain on Friday, but had been cautioned that the plea could be revoked if he wasn't being truthful.
Springfield Police Det. Ryan Maddox, the case agent, testified that he interviewed Hembrough three times and confirmed that Hembrough initially told him that he wasn't present for the shooting and robbery, though he provided Maddox a blow-by-blow detail.
During a Feb. 22, 2022, interview, Maddox said Hembrough's story changed "somewhat," though he admitted to being present at the scene.
Asked by McWard, Galmore's attorney, if it was fair to say that Hembrough "lied," Maddox said he was "forthcoming but minimized his involvement."
"There were some inconsistencies?" McWard asked.
"Yes," Maddox responded.
Some of those inconsistencies, McWard and Wykoff said, centered around the amount of drugs taken in the robbery at the 10th Street house the night of the murders, who the Mercury Milan used by Hembrough belonged to, the identity of a gray satchel at the crime scene and about Hembrough seeing Gant that night.
Pressed by McWard, Maddox said he couldn't recall if Hembrough said "something to the effect that he wasn't going to spend the rest of his life in jail."
Maddox testified to obtaining digitial images from Hembrough's garage after he was evicted from his home in January 2022. Timestamps showed that the Mercury Milan Hembrough used was not in the garage at the time of the crime.
On cross, McWard continued to insist that the crime scene was "compromised or disturbed" for a full 12 hours before police arrived and that witness Letravian Medley of Springfield was in the house twice and "might have" touched two of the victims.
Another Springfield Police Det. Jason Sloman testified earlier that Medley was in the house earlier.
Maddox admitted the scene was "open."
McClain was identified as being at a one-year Celebration of Life for De'Arius Equan Jones and at an after-party at the 10th Street home, both on Aug. 8, 2021. Maddox confirmed that a print from McClain was lifted from a glass jar that contained cannabis used at the party.

What goes into becoming the most loved grocery store in the country? Is it low prices to beat the rest, an assortment of food and home goods one notch above the next or even the charities the store donates to?
Maybe it's steak dinners with a side of potatoes and green beans and burgers with celebs?
According to Hy-Vee Springfield store director, it takes all that and a little bit more to win best grocer.
'We're trying to provide 100 million meals in the nine states that we help support and that we serve,' District Store Director Jim Blizzard said. 'We're up to 800 or 83,000,000 meals so far that we've raised in just a short little time… So we expect to hit that goal of 100 meals here in the next just a little while. Locally, we were able to provide $90,000 to the Central Illinois Food Bank as part of this program.'
For the first time ever, Hy-Vee, an Iowa-based grocery store chain, was voted Best Grocery Store in America in USA TODAY's 10 Best Readers' Choice Awards by readers of Gannett papers, like The State Journal-Register.
In previous years, the company has ranked within the top three spots, but according to Blizzard some changes in the past year have helped Hy-Vee come out on top, at least in Springfield.
Paul Wahlberg, brother to actors Donnie and Mark Walhberg, visited his Wahlburgers store on April 11 of this year. The Springfield store joins three other central Illinois locations participating in the 100 million meals challenge, with two in Quincy and one in Jacksonville.
What was once the former Kmart building, an abandoned bowling alley and payday loan store, in 2012 Hy-Vee Corp. purchased the store at 2114 S. MacArthur Blvd. transforming the section of MacArthur into a busy strip. The store offers savings by gas saving deals of 20 cents a gallon, a plethora of grocery and ready-to-eat food options and a drive through pharmacy, continuing to sustain the now bustling corner of the boulevard.
While headquarters are in Iowa, the Springfield location has worked on supporting their city through partnerships with organizations like the Red Cross.
'I think last year when we had the derechos and the storms that came through, we were the folks that were providing Red Cross with the meals down at Bank of Springfield,' Blizzard said. 'We were the ones that were providing meals to all of the CWLP line workers that were out day night trying to fix all the power and get all the power back up.'
Interested in their hot food? You aren't the only one – it's one of the store's main attractions. The infamous Hy-Vee steak night on Thursdays from 4 to 7 p.m. Guests can get a choice cut steak with mashed potatoes and green beans for $10, with add-ons like shrimp and onions for just a buck or two more. The night has been extremely popular Blizzard says and that every Thursday, the line will be wrapped nearly around the store with repeat customers.
'We have a wide variety of promotions that we're able to help folks save even more money with our weekly ad, where there'll be thousands of items in the ad that are well below the market price,' Blizzard said. 'We do this by having great partnerships with our vendor community where we're able to get those prices down and be competitive across the area.'
To celebrate, the store is giving customers what they want on Oct. 5, in a customer appreciation day according to Blizzard.

title: Trump tours Hurricane Helene damage in Georgia, falsely says Biden and Kemp haven't spoken
author: David Jackson
description: Trump held off on direct criticism of President Joe Biden and Vice President Kamala Harris while speaking with reporters in Valdosta, Ga.
content:
Show Caption
WASHINGTON - Former President Donald Trump pursued the politics of disaster on Monday as he traveled to the storm-hit battleground state of Georgia to survey damage from Hurricane Helene.
Trump held off on direct criticism of President Joe Biden and his 2024 White House rival, Vice President Kamala Harris, as he visited a devastated area of Valdosta, Georgia. Trump told reporters "we're not talking about politics now," but he did attack Biden and Harris' hurricane response in the hours leading up to the trip.
Trump on Monday in a post on his Truth Social platform mocked a Harris statement and photo about a hurricane briefing she received. In another post about his trip to Valdosta, Trump said "I'll be there shortly, but don't like the reports that I'm getting about the Federal Government."
Administration officials said it is not advisable for Harris or Biden to travel now because local leaders are still assessing the extent of the damage and trying to save lives.
In his public remarks in Valdosta, Trump said "we do need some help from the federal government." He also said, falsely, that Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp – a Republican who did not appear at the event – was trying to reach Biden about relief, but had not been able to get him.
The White House quickly pointed out that Biden and Kemp had indeed spoken. Biden on Monday criticized Trump's comments, saying "I don't know why he does this, and the reason I get so angry about it, I don't care about what he says about me, but I care what he communicates to the people that are in need. He implies that we're not doing everything possible.
Trump said he brought truckloads full of relief with him to Georgia, including fuel, water and equipment. The former president tried to encourage residents as they recover from the remnant of a Category 4 storm that led to at least 100 deaths and more than 2 million homes and businesses across the region still without power.
"I would have bought some furniture, if you had some in there," Trump said he told the owners of a local store that fell to the hurricane.
"It's called an hour of need," the Republican presidential nominee also told supporters in Georgia. "You're in our prayers." In brief remarks, he vowed "We have to all get together and get this solved."
Still, during a speech Sunday in Erie, Pennsylvania, Trump accused Biden of "sleeping" in Delaware while Helene tore through the South.
The Trump presidential campaign added Monday's trip to Valdosta to its schedule on Sunday. The campaign said in a statement Trump would "receive a briefing on the devastation of Hurricane Helene, facilitate the distribution of relief supplies, and deliver remarks to the press."
Trump and his aides have already started to criticize the Biden administration's response, including the lack of a visit by either Biden and Harris, even as officials on the ground are just now assessing the extent of the damage. Administration officials have said Harris and Biden do not want to divert police and first responders for VIP security as they are just starting recovery and clean-up.
"The Vice President intends to visit impacted communities as soon as it is possible without disrupting emergency response operations," said an administration statement.
Some opponents criticized Trump and accused him of interfering with local responders.
In one of his critical Truth Social posts, Trump said he also wanted to visit ravaged North Carolina - another battleground state - but "access and communication is now restricted, and we want to make sure that Local Emergency Management is able to focus on helping the people most affected."

title: Full Massey Commission, working group members named
author: Steven Spearie
description: After replacing two-chairs on the Massey Commission last week, a full list of 14 commissioners have been made public.
content:
After replacing two-chairs on the Massey Commission last week, a full list of 14 commissioners was made public Tuesday.
The commission now includes two members Sonya Massey's family: Shadia Massey, who was named a co-chair last week, and Sontae Massey.
Sonya Massey, the namesake of the commission, was fatally shot by a now former Sangamon County Sheriff's deputy in her home in an unincorporated part of Woodside Township on July 6.
Former Sangamon County Sheriff's deputy Sean P. Grayson, 30, was charged with Massey's murder. He is next in court on Oct. 21.
Both Shadia and Sontae Massey are Sonya Massey's cousins.
In addition to the 14 commissioners, members were named to four working groups.
'More than 200 concerned citizens submitted their names and indicated their willingness to serve on the Massey Commission," Shadia Massey said in a press release Tuesday. "That gives me hope that this family tragedy may lead to real community solutions."
Two commission co-chairs, the Rev. T. Ray McJunkins and Nina Harris, were replaced last week.
JoAnn Johnson, the first Black woman to reach the rank of colonel with the Illinois State Police and a law enforcement trainer in police bias, was the other new co-chair named last week. Jerry Kruse, dean and provost of SIU School of Medicine and CEO of SIU Medicine, will continue to serve as the other co-chair.
Kruse, speaking to The State Journal-Register Tuesday, said he, McJunkins and Harris went through all 204 applications. Several commissioners had accepted before the Sept. 16 listening session, Kruse said, though they were not publicly named then.
After Johnson and Massey were named co-chairs, they also went through the applications, completed the commission and named members of the work groups, Kruse said.
The commission, he added, is talking about adding a listening session.
"Originally, we had planned to have the first commission meeting after the first listening session and I think we're sorting that one out in the next few days," Kruse said.
Sontae Massey, Kruse added, was in the original group of commissioners named. Shadia Massey was not an applicant before being added as a co-chair.
"The listening session informed us about that and led us to a good decision about bringing Shadia Massey on board and having good representation from the Massey family and others close to the issues were addressing," Kruse said.
The commission seeks to address systemic issues in law enforcement practices, mental health responses and community relations, with the goal of creating "tangible, practical and equitable solutions for the betterment of all who call Sangamon County home."
It will look to produce a comprehensive report outlining findings, recommendations and proposed actions within a year.

title: Braddock Cates, Williamsville football hum in Sangamo win over Athens
author: Bill Welt
description: Williamsville football nearly reached 400 rushing yards in a win over Athens on Friday
content:
(This story was updated to add new information.)
ATHENS — Braddock Cates bolted out of the gates with a touchdown run in the opening two minutes and the Williamsville football team coasted to a 52-6 Sangamo Conference win over Athens on Friday.
Cates supplied the first two touchdowns in the first quarter and racked up 177 total yards of offense. He finished with 14 carries for 127 yards and three scores. He also had three catches for 50 yards.
"I think we're moving in a really good direction and a really good pace," Cates said. "The first few weeks, it wasn't bad. It's never been bad. I think we're really starting to pick it up. I think we're on a really good track right now."
The Bullets (5-1, 5-0 Sangamo) amassed 385 rushing yards as a team. Senior tailback Gage Paul's 91-yard TD burst and Will Zinn's 27-yard field goal created a 24-6 halftime lead. Paul ended with 113 rushing yards on just two carries.
Junior quarterback Jackson Sanders also kept the offense humming. He went 9-for-11 for 117 yards and one TD in addition to 22 rushing yards. Senior tight end Carson Beattie had the TD catch to go along with a sack defensively.
Athens (2-4, 2-4) pared the early deficit to one possession on Talon DiGiovanna's 9-yard scoring run. Athens also recovered a fumbled snap to begin the third quarter but couldn't capitalize. Williamsville subsequently scored on its next four possessions.
"I think kind of a big turning point for us was after we fumbled to start the second half and we got them to go four-and-out," Williamsville coach Aaron Kunz said. "I thought that was huge and we rolled from there. I felt all season we have a lot of playmakers and tonight we really did a good job of distributing the ball to them."
Junior running back Gage Honn led Athens with 59 rushing yards but left the field at the start of the second half due to injury. Brodee Rector had 50 rushing yards.

title: CS8 stunner: U-High beats Glenwood for first time since joining league
author: Ryan Mahan
description: The Normal U-High offense jumped out to a big lead and stymied Glenwood almost the entire night to earn first CS8 win over Titans.
content:
NORMAL — If last year's win over Decatur MacArthur turned the page for the Normal U-High football team, then Friday's stunning victory over Chatham Glenwood started a new chapter.
"I think that's probably a fair statement," U-High coach Brody Walworth said. "Last year against MacArthur was pretty special, too. That was a corner-turning win last year and now we're in a situation where we think we're competitive with the best teams in the league. To finally get over the hump in (a big game) is awesome."
U-High quarterback Alek Weiland threw five touchdowns and finished with 318 yards passing as the Pioneers beat Glenwood 33-13 in a Central State Eight Conference east division game at Illinois State University's Hancock Stadium.
When Weiland found AJ Holden for a 1-yard touchdown with 1 minute, 44 seconds left in the first half, it gave U-High a 26-0 lead.
"I think we knew we had it in us and we knew we could play with these guys and I knew we could beat them," Weiland said. "A lot of people didn't think we could win this game, but coming in, I think we all thought we were just as good, if not better, than them."
The Titans (4-2 overall, 3-1 CS8 east) found their offensive groove long enough to cut the deficit in half, when Brady Dwyer scored a 1-yard touchdown run with 12 seconds left in the second quarter and junior quarterback Colten Knoedler found Jonathan Helm for a 21-yard score on the Titans' first possession of the second half.
Glenwood's defense held the Pioneers (4-2, 3-1 CS8 east) scoreless for almost the entirety of the second half but couldn't get any closer. U-High cemented the win when Weiland and Holden connected on an 18-yard strike with 2:47 to play.
But, Glenwood coach David Hay said, that defensive play in the second half wasn't good enough.
"They just beat us: flat-out beat us," Hay said. "We didn't show up to the game until maybe somewhere in the third quarter. We can't do that. If we think we're good enough to do that, I think we just found out that we're not.
"We had places where we played well, but this is a team sport, a team game and that's not good enough."
Heading into Friday's game, Glenwood was 7-0 against U-High since the Pioneers entered the CS8 in 2017. That first season, Glenwood pulled out a 37-36 overtime win, but since then, the Pioneers haven't been within a mile of the Titans with Glenwood holding a 326-106 scoring advantage in the series.
Glenwood fans were heard starting to get restless after the Pioneers went up 12-0 on Weiland's second TD throw to Cade Cunningham, this one a 19-yard pass after the two connected on a 34-yard score to start the game.
Twice in a row, Glenwood had to punt out of its own end zone in the second quarter. The first time, U-High couldn't convert a fourth down from the Glenwood 3. Four plays later, the Titans had a fourth and 11 from their own 2. After a 25-yard punt, Weiland found Carson Stevens for his third TD throw, and U-High found itself up 19-0.
"The biggest thing defensively is, we know we've got the right guys — we can play — but we've got caught in a trap of playing what I call, 'Hero ball,' where we try to do too much," Walworth said. "I think tonight was a great example of when you have 11 guys playing disciplined football, doing their jobs.
"We played really well (on the defensive) side. The pressure was great, but forcing them to be one-dimensional (was key). (Glenwood) wants to run the ball, they like running it and I think we did a great job up front controlling the line of scrimmage, as well."
Glenwood committed a holding penalty on first-and-10 from its own 9-yard line, then had to again punt from its own 3. The Titans' defense committed a pass interference on first and 10 from the Glenwood 20, and three plays later, Holden and Weiland put the Pioneers up 26-0.
Holden's second touchdown was the final touch.
"That last play, we knew what we had to do to drive that nail, so we just go out there and executed," Holden said. "Now, we know we can beat the best teams in the state and in the conference."
U-High managed to run for 129 yards to finish with 447 yards of offense. After the game, Hay was asked what his team did right. Hay had some thoughts.
"Maybe a couple of drives, we got a couple of stops on defense, but generally, we didn't cover, we missed tackles, we didn't block, at times we didn't catch and at times, we didn't throw," Hay said.
U-High made the playoffs five straight seasons from 2011-15, but didn't make it back to the postseason until last year. Now, a win away from playoff eligibility has the Pioneers excited, but not content.
"I think we can build a ton off this," Weiland said. "Even though we won, we still have things to improve on and we're going to go watch film (Saturday) and improve on those things in practice next week."
Knoedler finished 22-for-39 for 236 yards and two interceptions. He found six different receivers, including Gavin Simmons, who caught 11 passes for 131 yards.
U-High forced Glenwood into a one-dimensional team on Friday. The Titans rushed 16 times for just 42 yards and one touchdown. Glenwood also committed seven penalties for 57 yards, while U-High was whistled four times for 30 yards.
"That's a good football team," Hay said of U-High. "I don't want anyone to misunderstand. A good football team, they're playing great, Brody does a hell of a job, but we expect more of ourselves."

title: Chatham Glenwood boys golf to savor state berth, plus other golf state finalists in the area
author: Bill Welt
description: The Chatham Glenwood golf team missed a state berth by one stroke last season. They turned the corner on Monday, plus other state qualifiers
content:
FORSYTH — Here are the boys and girls golfers advancing to the IHSA state finals this Friday through Saturday.
Chatham Glenwood locked down a boys team appearance in Class 3A and will play at Fox Creek Golf Course in Bloomington. Ditto Jacksonville in Class 2A after taking second place in the Champaign Centennial Sectional.
Sacred Heart-Griffin, meanwhile, has the Class 1A girls team title in their crosshairs after coasting to first place in the Rochester Sectional at Lincoln Greens Golf Course.
🏌Boys state qualifiers
➤ Chatham Glenwood (team)
To experience this year's state finals with the rest of the team in tow means everything to Chatham Glenwood senior Drew Downen.
Last season, Downen individually advanced to the Class 3A finals but the Titans collectively missed a team state berth by just one stroke in Pekin.
Downen not only tied for third place at the Class 3A Decatur MacArthur Sectional on Monday, but the team also finished in the third and final qualifying spot.
Downen shot even-par 72 at Hickory Point Golf Course, while the Titans totaled 306 strokes just behind first-place Washington (304) and runner-up Minooka (305).
'I'm happy that everything started to click today,' Downen said. 'It's kind of been a struggle this year, there's always something going on. But it's finally working and I'm so happy that the team played well enough to get out of here because the difference between going by yourself and with the team, it's so much more fun with the team and that's what I'm excited for.'
Senior teammate Derek Dulceak carded 4-over for 14 th place, while fellow seniors Brayden Muller (78) and Cam Appenzeller (80) rounded out the team score. Fellow senior Jack Turnbull turned in an 85.
Downen won the individual Central State Eight Conference title even-par 71 at the Lincoln Elks Club earlier this season after Appenzeller, The State Journal-Register's reigning Male Athlete of the Year, won last year's CS8 title.
Mueller and Dulceak then led the Titans individually with third and fourth place, respectively, for the Collinsville Regional team title prior to descending on Forsyth.
'It is much harder in 3A,' Mueller said. 'It's really good competition. Mentally, just knowing that we're just as good as these other teams out here. We can compete and that's the goal.'
Downen, who also plays baseball with Appenzeller, said he especially gravitated toward golf while playing with Dulceak during the COVID-19 pandemic at Piper Glen Golf Club. Both Downen and Dulceak credited former LPGA player Audra Burks for enhancing their game.
'I've really dropped the amount of putts that I've had,' Dulceak said. 'I had a couple poor putts today, but that's all right because the greens were tough. Other than that, a 76 is solid.'
Downen, who ironed out his approach shots over the past week with Burks, converted four birdies at Hickory Point, including the par-5 No. 2.
'It kept that momentum going for the rest of the round — that's what I tried to do at least,' Downen said.
➤ Jacksonville (team)
Junior A.J. Charpentier tied for fifth place individually at the University of Illinois Golf Course and the Crimsons missed the team 2A sectional title by just one stroke behind Normal U-High with 301.
Charpentier managed three birdies and finished 1-over 73. Senior Colton Barr also made the top 10 at 2-over. Junior Elias Martin (76) and sophomore Maddux Moore (78) rounded out the team score.
Barr earlier won the individual Canton Regional title at Wee-Ma-Tuk Hills Country Club with a 2-under 70. The Crimsons will appear at Weibring Golf Club in Normal.
➤ Sam Schwab/Tucker Maguire, Litchfield
Schwab missed the individual Class 1A Zeigler-Royalton Sectional title by one stroke. The junior forged a round of even-par 71 behind Effingham St. Anthony junior Jack Swingler's 70. Schwab totaled 16 pars with a birdie on the par-5 No. 17 at Franklin Country Club.
Maguire tied for ninth place with a 75. They will visit Prairie Vista Golf Course in Bloomington.
➤ Bryce Cowdrey, Raymond Lincolnwood
The sophomore also tied for ninth place at the 1A Zeigler-Royalton Sectional with a 75. Cowdrey claimed the boys' 14-15 division title at the Drysdale Junior Golf Tournament at Bunn Golf Course this past summer.
➤ Anderson Thielen, Pleasant Plains
The senior posted an 80 for 14 th place at the 1A Quincy Notre Dame Sectional at Spring Lake Country Club.
➤ Cade Ross, Beardstown
The senior followed with an 81 for 16 th place at the 1A QND Sectional.
➤ Reed Fretueg, Rushville-Industry
The senior nabbed the final individual qualifying spot at the 1A QND Sectional after a round of 83.
🏌Girls state qualifiers
➤ Sacred Heart-Griffin (team)
Reigning Class 1A individual state champion Izzy Hassebrock and sophomore teammate Maddy Johnston just missed the individual Class 1A Rochester Sectional title in a playoff after ending with rounds of 2-over 74 in regulation. Carlyle's Sarah Hyten prevailed as the medalist.
But the Cyclones easily captured the team sectional title by 37 strokes. Junior Natalie Zak (76) and senior Macie Petropoulos (77) also finished in sixth and eighth place, respectively.
Hassebrock, the SJ-R's Large School Girls Golfer of the Year last season, not only captured the individual state title with a 3-over-par 147 total at Red Tail Run Golf Course, but the Cyclones also took second place as a team behind Mount Carmel.
➤ Alaina Ervin, Pleasant Plains
The four-time Sangamo Conference champion tied for ninth place at the 1A Rochester Sectional. She fired a 78. She returns to Red Tail Run after taking seventh place at last year's state finals.
➤ Jersey West, North Mac
The junior tied for 12 th place with a 79 at the 1A Rochester Sectional. She previously won the Drysdale Junior Golf Tournament with a match-play victory over Rochester graduate Kiley Torres in the girls' 16-18 age division.
➤ Lilly Bandy, Staunton
The senior shot an 80 to grab one of the last remaining qualifying spots at the 1A Rochester Sectional.

title: Job postings will look different in Illinois next year. Here's what you need to know
author: Patrick M. Keck
description: Looking for a new job in the new year? A new Illinois law will change what you see on job postings. Here's what you need to know.
content:
Looking for a new job in the new year? An Illinois state law going into effect on Jan. 1, 2025, will soon give those scouring job boards more information on employment opportunities.
Now, prospective candidates will be able to see a pay scale and benefit information in job postings. Here's what you need to know.
Does every employer have to post this information in job postings?
Employers with more than 15 employees are required to share pay scale and benefits in job postings. In the case that these postings show up on a third-party job site like LinkedIn or Indeed, they would be required to either to show on that site or have that information linked.
What happens if the pay scale and benefits are not posted?
The Illinois Department of Labor will be receiving complaints of job postings not including this now-required information. From there, the department will notify the employer and give a set date for when it must be remedied.
What's the penalties for businesses not showing this information?
Penalties range depending on whether the job posting is active. If it is active, a first-time offense could come with up-to a $500 fine or $250 if not active. A second-time offense carries a maximum of a $2,500 fine.
After the third offense, there could be a penalty not exceeding $10,000.
Are there other states that have pay transparency laws?
Yes, Illinois will join such states as California, Colorado, Hawaii, Minnesota, New York, New Jersey, Vermont and Washington that have pay transparency laws on the books.

title: Man dies after being found shot inside of a car in Springfield
author: Steven Spearie
description: The man was found in the front seat of the vehicle in the area of 17th and Cook streets early Sunday morning.
content:
A man found in a vehicle with a gunshot wound later died Sunday morning according to Springfield Police.
The man was found in the front seat of the vehicle in the area of 17th and Cook streets, according to a news release. A shots fired report came in shortly after 1 a.m.
The man was taken to a hospital where he was treated for his injuries but did not survive.
SPD detectives and crime scene services were processing the scene for evidence.
Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to call SPD at 217-788-8311 and/or Sangamon/Menard County Crime Stoppers at 217-788-8427.

title: High school boys soccer playoff schedule, results: How this Lutheran duo became a force
author: Bill Welt
description: Lutheran forwards learn to click in final season together, plus the complete high school boys soccer schedule with results for the Springfield area
content:
Lutheran forwards Noah Rodenburg and Carter Matteson are on the same wavelength.
'A lot of my goals are off his assists and a lot of his goals are off my assists,' Rodenburg said. 'It's been amazing.'
Rodenburg indeed scored all three goals on Matteson assists in a galvanizing 3-2 nonconference win over Pleasant Plains near the end of the regular season.
Top performers: Chatham Glenwood's Ellie Surges remains perfect in CS8 girls tennis
And following a 3-0 win over Southeast on Wednesday to improve to 18-4 overall, the duo has combined for 81 goals and 38 assists this season ahead of their Class 1A Riverton Regional semifinal against the No. 6 Hawks on Friday at 6 p.m.
'Honestly I think me and Carter have just been working better together,' Rodenburg said. 'In previous years, we've kind of been doing it on our own. This year, it's been a lot more together, working and playing off each other.'
They first paired up at Our Savior's Lutheran School before spending three years together at Lutheran. Rodenburg, a senior with 37 goals and 16 assists, initially started on the back line as a freshman before joining Matteson, a junior with 44 goals and 22 assists, at the top.
'It's been me and him up in that front for three years and every year it feels like we've clicked a little bit more and understand where the other is playing,' Matteson said. 'That just shows in the numbers. We give each other our own points and that's just how it goes.'
Lutheran coach David Isham described the tandem as one of the top combinations in the area.
'They just constantly want that ball,' Isham said. 'They know how to go to the goal, they're unselfish and they carry the offensive load for us.'
They also try to light a fire under their teammates, especially their young defensive back line that includes Rodenburg's younger brother, Evan. Both Rodenburg and Matteson said their counterparts have stepped up and responded.
'They've locked it down most of the year — a lot of shut outs, I'm really proud of them,' Rodenburg said.
Both also duly credited their coaches for their upward trajectory, and Rodenburg said there's nothing that the team can't do. Matteson agreed.
'Whatever comes next, we're ready,' Matteson said.

title: Storm tracker: All eyes on 2 systems in Atlantic; one could become a depression
author: Gabe Hauari
description: The National Hurricane Center is monitoring two systems. One, Invest 94L, could soon become a tropical depression or storm.
content:
The National Hurricane Center said Tuesday that it is tracking two systems in the Atlantic basin, including one that could strengthen into a tropical depression later this week.
The system, currently designated as Invest 94L, was described by the hurricane center as a "well-defined area of low pressure" located over the central tropical Atlantic that is currently producing occasional showers and thunderstorms.
Forecasters said the system remains "embedded in a dry air environment," and that development is unlikely over the next couple of days, but that the system is forecast to move generally westward and environmental conditions are expected to become more favorable for gradual development by the middle to latter part of this week.
Tropical depression or storm could form
"A tropical depression could form as the system begins moving west-northwestward and approaches or moves near the Leeward Islands late this week," the hurricane center said. The system has a 60% chance of formation through the next seven days.
"It looks like any development over the next couple of days will be slow," AccuWeather hurricane expert Alex DaSilva said. Late in the week, probably Thursday or Friday, that's when the window opens for it to develop into a tropical storm as wind shear relaxes. AccuWeather's forecast is for the system to become a tropical storm by Thursday night, early Friday, or, at the earliest, by Thursday afternoon.
The next storm that forms will get the name Nadine. It will be the 14th named storm of the 2024 Atlantic hurricane season, which is right about the average for number of named storms.
First frost of the fall?
Another system lingering in Caribbean Sea
The hurricane center also said Tuesday that it is keeping tabs on a "broad area of low pressure" that could develop over the southwestern Caribbean Sea by the middle to latter portions of this week.
Some gradual development of the system is possible if it stays over water while it moves slowly west-northwestward toward northern Central America, the hurricane center said. However, regardless of development, locally heavy rainfall is possible across portions of Central America later this week.
The system is not currently forecast to impact the U.S.
Florida hit by 3 hurricanes this year
Florida has been hit by three hurricanes so far this season: Hurricane Debby, Hurricane Helene and Hurricane Milton. That puts 2024 tied with five other years for the most hurricanes making landfall in Florida during a single season, according to Colorado State University meteorologist Phil Klotzbach, who specializes in Atlantic basin seasonal hurricane forecasts.

title: Mamma Mia! Glenwood kicker Gerger sends Titans past SHG for first time since 2019
author: Adrian Dater
description: The emotional rollercoaster rivaled anything Six Flags has and Chatham Glenwood pulled out just its sixth CS8 win over SHG with field goal in OT.
content:
As Chatham Glenwood fans stormed the field, several Titans football players swarmed placekicker Mia Gerger and hoisted her on their shoulders for a short, makeshift parade. What a final scene to a classic high school football game Friday night at Ken Leonard Field.
Gerger's 21-yard field goal in overtime gave Glenwood a 34-31 thriller over valiant Sacred Heart-Griffin in front of an overflow crowd that might have witnessed the best game ever played in the 32nd Central State Eight Conference meeting of the longtime rivals.
Gerger's winning kick came not long after Cyclones senior kicker Tom Davis tied the game at 31 as the regulation clock expired with a 50-yard field goal that hit the crossbar and bounced just inside the left goalpost. Those were just two of the many heroic plays made by players on both sides of a game that left everyone shaking their heads in astonishment when it was finally over.
'In a game like that, you've got to make the last play, and that's what we did,' said Titans coach David Hay, whose team clinched a playoff spot and upped their record to 6-2 (5-2 in CS8).
Gerger's field goal came on third down, on Glenwood's possession of OT after Titans senior linebacker Colten Haacke made a great play, stuffing SHG running back Mike Groesch in the backfield to stop the Cyclones on fourth down from the 1-yard line.
By holding SHG scoreless to start overtime, the Titans needed a score of any type to win.
Glenwood got the ball at the Cyclones' 10 as part of OT rules, and looked to have won the game when running back Grady Mueller was about to cross the goal line on the first play of the drive. But the football popped out of Mueller's grasp and was recovered by SHG. Referees, however, ruled Mueller's knee touched the ground first. After Mueller was tackled for a loss on second down by SHG's Chuck Lanier, Hay elected to send Gerger onto the field, and she ended the drama with a perfect kick through the middle of the uprights.
'This is why I got into the sport. I love the pressure,' Gerger said. 'That was from (21) yards. It's just another extra point. I have a cross on my tee, and I look straight at the cross. I keep my head down, and after that, I look at my holder and tell him 'Good job.''
Said Hay: 'It wasn't a difficult decision at all to put her on the field on third down. You don't want to take a chance on a fumble, and she's the all-time leading points kicker in the history of the program.'
Cyclones coach John Allison was upset that Mueller's fumble was nullified, saying 'I just talked to my video guy, and he confirmed it was a fumble.'
But, Allison said, 'We can't hang our hat just on that one play. Our guys showed heart, I'll give them that. But we feel like we kind of let one get away there.'
The Cyclones (5-3, 4-3 with a game at Rochester next week) were down 24-14 at the half but took a 28-24 lead with 3 minutes, 1 second left in regulation after Groesch's 1-yard plunge on first down. That left a lot of time on the clock in a game like this, however, and the Titans marched right down the field to take a 31-28 lead with 38 seconds left on a jump-ball pass from the 6 by quarterback Colten Knoedler to 6-foot-7 tight end Mason Neumann.
But back the Cyclones came, getting the second of two near-miraculous kickoff returns from senior Jamarion Bardwell that gave them possession near midfield. Cyclones QB Cam Brinkman, who was Houdini-esque in evading many near-sacks, ran the ball to the Glenwood 33 with 2.3 seconds left, setting up Davis' sensational kick that got a little help from the crossbar. But, as Hay noted, the Titans just had one more big play in them than did SHG.
Mueller was unquestionably the offensive star of the game for Glenwood. He scored three touchdowns, including a 98-yard kickoff return that tied it 7-7 in the first quarter. He also had a 45-yard kickoff return on the drive that put them up 31-28. Overall, he ran for 165 yards on 24 carries.
'We wanted this one. We just kept battling to the end,' Mueller said. 'It feels great to be in the playoffs. But we know there's a lot more left to get done.'
Glenwood improved to 6-26 against SHG in conference play since the CS8 was formed in 1993. It was the Titans' third league win over the Cyclones since 2018. Including playoffs, SHG is 33-6 in that span over Glenwood, including seven playoff wins over the Titans.

title: What we learned from Week 8 of Springfield high school football: Bring on Fair Grove, Strafford
author: Wyatt D. Wheeler
description: Several conference championship shares were claimed in Week 8 and there are two that need to be decided during the final week of the regular season.
content:
One week remains in the Missouri high school football regular-season and plenty needs to be settled across the Springfield area.
Several conference championship shares were claimed in Week 8 with victories from Nixa, Carthage, Branson, Marionville and Seneca. There is still much to be decided in the Mid-Lakes Conference and South Central Association come next week.
Here's what we learned from Week 8 of the high school football season:
Fair Grove, Strafford football set up Mid-Lakes championship
Early this season, it appeared the Fair Grove-Strafford rivalry game could see both teams start their years 8-0 before playing in the regular season's final week for the Mid-Lakes Conference championship. The prophecy came to be.
Fair Grove will host Strafford next week. One will end the season undefeated and the other will head into district play with their first loss.
Fair Grove was last year's undefeated champ before advancing to the Class 2 semifinals. The Eagles dominated Forsyth in a 48-13 rout, their fifth-straight game of scoring 43 or more. Kellen Lair finished the night with four touchdowns.
Strafford cruised to a 49-14 win over Clever. Strafford has scored 34 or more in every game this season and 49 or more in its last three.
The Eagles won both games these two played last season, including in a district championship. Friday night will be their only meeting this season after Strafford was bumped up to Class 3.
Dylan Rebura's big day gives Nixa a Central Ozark Conference East, Backyard Brawl title
Add another six touchdowns to Dylan Rebura's totals for the season after he went off in a 48-3 win over rival Ozark to claim the Backyard Brawl title and a share of the Central Ozark Conference East.
Nixa can win the title outright with a win at Glendale next week.
It would be difficult to find someone who had a better Friday than Rebura who picked up his first scholarship offer from Southwestern College (Kansas) and added six touchdowns the same day. According to available stats on MaxPreps, he entered Friday tied for the state lead in scores with 22.
Missed extra point helps give Carthage a COC West share
Webb City quarterback Jackson Lucas broke away for a 73-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter for what appeared to be a game-tying score. The Cardinals followed by missing the extra point which proved to be the difference in Carthage's 14-13 win over its Joplin-area rival.
The win gave Carthage a claim to the COC West championship and the Tigers can win it outright next week against Neosho. Brady Carlton threw two touchdowns to lift Carthage to the win.
Branson football claims Ozark Mountain Conference title share
Branson's best season in decades added a conference championship with a 56-14 win over Logan-Rogersville on Thursday night. The victory put the Pirates at 8-0 and the opportunity to win the league outright when they host Hillcrest next week.
Much attention will now go to Class 5, District 6 where the Pirates entered the week leading the group and will finish with the first or second seed with Republic taking the other. The two used to be Central Ozark Conference foes and the district will likely come down to a championship game between them.
Republic has won its last three against the Pirates, dating back to 2021. Each year, the Pirates have narrowed the gap in the scoring margin. The Tigers will likely be without star quarterback Preston McCracken (torn MCL) through that potential matchup.
Marionville escapes Ash Grove upset bid to win Southwest share
The Comets extended their regular-season winning streak to 44 but it might have been more difficult than the 43 wins that came before it.
Marionville escaped with a 22-20 win over Ash Grove to claim its fifth-straight Southwest Conference title. A win next week against Miller would give the Comets the championship outright.
Marionville quarterback Bryer Guerin scored a go-ahead touchdown with 3:41 left before scoring the 2-point conversion to go up by eight.
Ash Grove marched down the field and faced a 4th-and-10 from the Comets 15 with under a minute left. Pirates QB Kyler Reece broke a handful of tackles before powering in for a touchdown to bring his team within two. A failed two-point conversion and onside kick allowed the defending Class 1 champs to escape with a win.
Even with Ash Grove being a state-ranked opponent, Marionville, the No. 1 team in Class 1, looked beatable for the first time over the last two years. Scoring margins have decreased recently and Ash Grove outplayed the Comets most of the game.
We could see these two get matched up again in the postseason.
Where things stand in the South Central Association
There is a three-way tie atop the South Central Association standings heading into the final week.
Liberty, Mountain Grove and Thayer each have 5-1 records in league play.
At least one team will drop from the top next week after Thayer hosts Mountain Grove. The Bobcats won 47-0 against Willow Springs and the Panthers beat Houston 41-20.
Liberty can claim a share if it beats Houston. The Eagles lost to the Panthers 44-24 earlier this season but beat the Bobcats 42-16.
Seneca claims share of Big 8 Conference
Undefeated Seneca clinched at least a share of its third-straight Big 8 Conference title after beating East Newton 63-21. It will have a chance to win the league outright for the second year in a row if it tops Lamar next week.
Although no longer in contention, Lamar has played better over the last two weeks, including a 35-0 win over Aurora on Friday night. The Tigers' two-game winning streak is in response to a three-game losing streak when two losses were by one point.
Nevada won the Big 8's biggest game this week when it topped Mount Vernon 55-42. If Seneca were to lose next week, it would share its title with the Tigers who completed their league schedule.

title: Arrest made in Rockford arson fire at high rise that injured 5 residents, 1 firefighter
author: Jeff Kolkey
description: Authorities say they have arrested a man suspected in two Rockford arson fires set in recent days.
content:
Rockford Fire Department investigators have arrested a 46-year-old man in connection with two suspected arson fires.
David B. Marshall of Rockford was charged with setting Thursday's early morning fire at the Rockford Housing Authority's Park Terrace Apartments, 1000 Chamberlain St. Five residents and a firefighter suffered injuries that were not life threatening during the fire which broke out about 3:30 a.m. Thursday in a first-floor office area.
Marshall was also charged with setting a fire at about 6:50 a.m. Oct. 6 at the Wired Café, 414 E. State St. which caused significant damage but no reported injuries. Marshall is being held in the Winnebago County Jail.
Rockford fire officials worked with Rockford Police Department detectives to investigate the incidents, a news release said.
Electronic Winnebago County court records indicate Marshall has been arrested several times including charges of theft and burglary. He was convicted in 2016 in another arson case.
Rockford Housing Authority officials said they are working to renovate and repair the high-rise apartment complex and that resident could move back into the building Wednesday at the earliest.

title: Meat, poultry in BrucePac listeria recall were sent to these 200 schools, USDA reveals
author: Mary Walrath-Holdridge
description: The USDA said that roughly 1.7 million pounds of the 11.8-million-pound BrucePac meat recall went to schools across the U.S. See the list here.
content:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture released a preliminary list of schools that received products included in the 11.8 million-pound BrucePac listeria recall.
Initially reported without a product list on Oct. 9 as a recall for 9,986,245 pounds of meat and poultry due to possible listeria contamination, the number rose on Wednesday to include an additional 1,779,040 pounds, increasing the weight to a total of 11.8 million pounds. The additional 1.7 million pounds were reportedly sent to schools, though a list was not offered at the time of announcement.
On Thursday evening, the USDA's Food and Safety Inspection Service (FSIS) updated the notice with a preliminary list of roughly 200 schools to which recalled products were distributed. The products that went to these schools were not part of USDA's National School Lunch and Breakfast Programs, the notice said.
The agency is also consistently expanding a list of products and product labels affected by the recall, which is 348 pages long as of Friday.
Here is the most recent list of schools across the U.S. that received recalled food, according to FSIS data.

What kinds of products are recalled?
Sandwiches, wraps and salads are the primary prepared foods affected by the recall. Frozen meals containing chicken products ranging from pastas and burritos to bowls and family meals are also affected.
The ready-to-eat meat and poultry items were produced from May 31, 2024, to Oct. 8, 2024. The products were shipped to other establishments and distributors nationwide and then distributed to restaurants, schools and institutions.
The USDA is continuing to update the list of affected products and suggests checking back at fsis.usda.gov/recalls frequently.
What is listeriosis or listeria poisoning?
Listeriosis, or listeria poisoning, is a foodborne bacterial infection most commonly caused by the bacterium Listeria monocytogenes. It is considered a serious condition and can be dangerous or life-threatening, especially to older adults, people with weak immune systems and pregnant people.
Signs and sympoms of listeriosis can take weeks after consumption to appear. Persons in the higher-risk categories who experience flu-like symptoms within two months after eating contaminated food should seek medical care and tell the health care provider about eating the contaminated food, says the USDA.

title: Shooting in Mississippi after homecoming game at trail ride leaves 3 dead, 8 hurt
author: Pam Dankins
description: A mass shooting in Lexington, Mississippi after a homecoming football game has left three people dead and eight others injured, authorities say.
content:
Three people have died, and eight others are injured after a Mississippi homecoming football game turned deadly.
Holmes County Sheriff Willie March told the Clarion Ledger, a part of the USA TODAY Network, that deputies responded to a 12:30 a.m. call stating multiple people were either shot or dead Saturday near North Highway 17.
Where did the shooting happen?
The shooting happened five minutes away from Lexington, Mississippi, about 62 miles north of Jackson, Mississippi.
How did the shooting happen?
According to March, people were on the trail ride when a shooter opened fire into the crowd following an altercation between young men.
March said the shooting occurred after the Holmes County Consolidated School's homecoming celebration.
'The football team had won the homecoming game, and people wanted to go out and celebrate the win, but others didn't have that same intention,' March said.
March told the Clarion Ledger that some of the injured victims were airlifted to a hospital in Jackson. The additional victims were transported by ambulances.
In addition, the sheriff told WJTV that the deputies are searching for the suspects in connection to the shooting. Agents with the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation are assisting with the case, he told the local outlet.
Who was killed in the mass shooting?
March revealed the identities of those who were killed in the shooting:
Martel Gibson, 25, of Durant
Shundra Chestnut, 19, of Kosciusko
John Jenkins, 19, of Durant
Third mass shooting in the South within a month
A mass shooting took place in Birmingham, Alabama last month on Sept. 21. The shooting killed four people and injured 17 others in the city's entertainment district. A suspect, Damien McDaniel, was arrested this week in connection to the deadly shooting.
And also last month, a mass school shooting at Apalachee High School in Winder, Georgia on Sept. 4 claimed the lives of four people and injured nine others. Accused school shooter 14-year-old Colt Gray and his father, Colin Gray, were indicted on numerous charges this week.

title: 'Every single inch matters': North Mac prevails in OT against Staunton
author: Ryan Mahan
description: North Mac gave up a 13-0 lead to Staunton, then bounced back after the Bulldogs took a 28-21 lead in overtime to win.
content:
STAUNTON — With fans in the bleachers huddling under blankets, hooded sweatshirts, drinking coffee and eating the concession-stand chili, Friday's South Central Conference matchup had all the hints of a playoff football game.
And players from both teams treated it as such.
North Mac gave up a two-score second quarter lead to trail Staunton before the Panthers bounced back to score last in overtime for a 29-28 win.
North Mac senior running back Roark Lewis ran the ball 25 times for 122 yards, but the only time he reached the end zone was on a two-point conversion on the final play of the game.
Moments after James Graves scored from the 2-yard line to get the Panthers (6-2) within a point of Staunton, North Mac lined up for the two-point try, quarterback Payne McLean got the ball to Lewis and the running back angled out to the edge before he was able to get in the end zone and dash the hopes of the Bulldogs in their homecoming game.
'Kids are finding ways to win,' North Mac second-year coach Robbi Howard said. 'Staunton played one heck of a game today. We knew they were playing for their (playoff) life. They're looking for five wins, and we knew we'd get their best effort and we made one just enough plays and we won by one point.'
Lewis also caught three passes for 52 yards and finished with 174 yards of offense.
'North Mac is a very good football team and they're going to be a tough out in the playoffs,' Staunton coach Austin Sherfy said. 'I'll tell you what: Roark Lewis is the best football player we've played all year and it's a tough ask to stop him four times in 10 yards.'
Where the game changed
North Mac got up 13-0 in the second quarter after McLean threw a 19-yard pass to Cade McCready in the first quarter then McLean ran in a 1-yard TD with 8:04 left in the second.
McLean was 13-for-19 with two touchdowns and 220 yards in the win. After the game, a very young Staunton fan asked McLean for his helmet after the two shared a high-five.
'I got to keep this one, buddy,' McLean told the traitorous Bulldogs' fan. 'I've got to play more football."
By this point, Staunton didn't even have a first down on its first three possessions.
The game flipped after Jesse Baker had runs of 24, 21 and seven yards to get the Bulldogs (4-4) to the 6-yard line. Tyler Diamond helped the home fans erupt when he scored on the next play to put Staunton on the board.
Staunton's next possession began with prime field position and the Bulldogs tied the game one play when Baker scored from the 17-yard line. Carter Legendre's extra-point kick gave Staunton a 14-13 lead with 3:51 to go in the first half.
'It's been a struggle all year,' Howard said. 'Several games, we've gone up two or three scores and they kind of took the gas off, stopped blocking, stopped tackling well and before you know it, it's a ballgame again. The halftime speech was, 'Get your butts back in gear.''
Baker, who didn't have a carry in the first quarter, had 69 yards and one TD on four carries in the second. He finished with a team-best 89 yards rushing on 13 carries.
A nail-biting second half
North Mac regained the lead after the Panthers' defense reestablished its dominance on the Bulldogs' first two possessions of the third quarter. North Mac, on its second possession, put together a seven-play, 72-yard drive that ended with McLean hitting Jacob Bickel for a 29-yard touchdown pass.
Then, Bickel hauled in McLean's two-point conversion pass for a 21-14 lead with 2:07 left in the third.
The Bulldogs once again battled back.
Staunton recovered its own fumble on first-and-10 from the North Mac 45 for what turned into a five-yard gain. Then, Staunton quarterback Elliot Frank completed his second pass, this time a 40-yard hookup with Hunter Wallace for a touchdown before Legendre tied the game with his PAT.
Staunton's red zone defense came up large to force overtime. North Mac had a first-and-goal from the 4-yard line, but after a false start penalty, Staunton stopped Lewis for no gain from the 9 before McLean found Khiry Taylor for a 7-yard pass to get to the 2. McLean got half the necessary yards on third-and-goal from the 2 before another false start flag. North Mac had a turnover on downs at the 6-yard line.
Staunton went for it on its own fourth down, but this one at the Bulldogs' 15-yard line. When North Mac got the ball with 3:03 left int he game, the Panthers started that drive at the 10, but North Mac had an illegal substitution penalty, followed by an intentional grounding flag on McLean. North Mac couldn't complete a third-and-33 from the 33 and McLean was sacked for a five-yard loss on fourth down.
Sherfy said despite the loss, there was a lot to like from his Bulldogs.
'We were down 13-0, we came right back, (North Mac) got up (again), we came right back, we stopped them twice in the fourth quarter down in the red zone,' said Sherfy, who is still hopeful for his first playoff berth in his fourth season. 'A lot to like. It stings, but we've got to move on.'
The final fireworks
In overtime, Staunton got the first try at the 10 and took all four plays before Taylor scored on a fourth-and-goal from the 1. Legendre booted a 26-yard extra-point after Staunton was whistled for the false start.
With North Mac trailing 28-21 in overtime, the Panthers got to work. Lewis took the first handoff eight yards to set up Graves' 2-yard touchdown. North Mac didn't play for a second overtime and instead opted to win or lose on a two-point conversion.
'In overtime, you've just got to (go all-out),' McLean said. "You've got to put your head down and go to work. You've go to get every single push. Every single inch matters."
The ball went to North Mac's leading rusher, Lewis. Already with more than 1,000 yards on the ground through seven games, Lewis ran to the left corner of the end zone and beat the Staunton defenders for the win.
'It was a great feeling,' Lewis said. 'I haven't been that excited all year. I just asked for my boys to block for me, I knew they'd get the job done and if my boys work for me, I work for them; I reward them.'
Lewis has 1,173 yards and nine touchdowns through eight games. Graves, a bruising back without whose touchdown run Lewis' two-point conversion wouldn't have been possible, has 586 yards and eight TDs on 99 carries.

title: Illinois State Police trooper killed in crash with truck driver. Here's what we know
author: Steven Spearie
description: An Illinois State Police trooper who was part of a motorcycle patrol was struck and killed by a truck driver in Champaign County Friday afternoon.
content:
An Illinois State Police trooper who was part of a motorcycle patrol was struck and killed by a truck driver in Champaign County Friday afternoon.
Corey S. Thompsen, 28, was part of a Special Operations Group and had been with the state police for nearly five years, said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly at a news conference in Pesotum Saturday.
Thompsen was on-duty finishing a traffic enforcement detail and traveling east on East Leverett Road Friday afternoon.
A truck, driven by Helen Torres, 32, of Thomasboro, was traveling south on County Road 1300 East and stopped at the intersection at Leverett Road when she pulled into the roadway, striking Thompsen's motorcycle.
A witness provided aid until first responders arrived and took Thompsen to an area hospital where he died of injuries around 4:30 p.m.
It is the first fatal crash involving a state police trooper this year.
The intersection is just east of Interstate 57 and northeast of Champaign.
Torres was cited for failure to yield right of way at a stop intersection and not having a valid driver's license (expired less than a year). Torres was treated at a local hospital for injuries.
'When we lose a public servant, a trooper like this, when we lose a noble knight like Corey Thompsen, I really have to ask you all for more than just your prayers and your thoughts," Kelly said Saturday. "Corey was a great trooper."
Gov. JB Pritzker tweeted that Thompsen "should have had a long life of service ahead of him. His family and loved ones will be in the thoughts of Illinoisans across our state."
Pritzker ordered all flags statewide to be lowered to half-staff in Thompsen's honor.
Thompsen, who attended St. Joseph-Ogden High School, is survived by his wife and parents.
